en.name: Qur’an.
description:
Written in *naskhi* script in black ink on delicate finished (*aharlı)* paper, the pages have thick gilded marginal lines and 13 lines of text per page. There are 346 pages in all. The first *sura* (*al-Fatiha*) and the first four verses of the second (*al-Baqara*) are illuminated with gilding between the lines of text. The chapter headings on the two facing pages on which these verses are written, as well as the areas outside the marginal lines, are covered with leaves of gilding and very colourful illumination in the Turkish Baroque-Rococo style. All the chapter headings are written in white *tawqi'* script on top of gilded illumination. Individual verses are separated by individuated gold rosettes, and rose motifs of various forms in the page margins mark the end of every five and 10 verses. The leather binding is brown on the outside and green on the inside. The exterior of the binding has floral designs rendered freely and naturalistically in green and yellow gilding.  
  
The calligrapher of this Qur'an, Mustafa Izzet Efendi (AH 1215–92 / AD 1801–76), was born in Tosya and came to Istanbul for his education. He learned calligraphy from Mustafa Vasıf and Yesarizade Mustafa Izzet Efendi. His most famous works are *hilya*s (prose descriptions of the Prophet Muhammad) and sheets with calligraphic exercises called *istif.* The inscriptions on the drum of the dome of Ayasofya, among the Islamic world's most famous, are by him.  
  
Two different artists worked on this Qur'an's decoration. They are Mehmet Salih, who was chief bookbinder at the Ottoman court in the time of Sultan Abdülmecid \['Abd al-Majid\], and his apprentice Rashid Effendi.  
  
Beginning in the 12th / 18th century, Turkish art experienced change under the influence of European art. This style, known as Turkish Baroque-Rococo, is reflected in the arts of the book. This Qur'an is the most beautiful example of its application to book decoration.

Illumination is a natural part of Qur'ans. Illuminators used naturalistic floral motifs influenced by Europe alongside classical elements to illuminate the Qur'ans during the AH 12th–13th / AD 18th–19th centuries.
holder: Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts.
artist: Calligrapher: Kazasker Mustafa Izzet Efendi; illuminators: Mehmet Salih Efendi, Mustafa Rashid Efendi.
keywords: Floral decoration; religious objects; waqf; Qur’an; Ottoman Baroque; religious manuscript
materials: Finished (*aharlı*) paper, written using black ink and illuminated with gilding and various colours; leather (binding).
tags: Finished (aharlı) paper, written using black ink and illuminated with gilding and various colours
partner: Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts

es.name: Corán.
description:
Las páginas de este Corán tienen cada una 13 renglones de letra *nasji* escrita en tinta negra sobre un delicado papel trabajado *(aharlı)*, con líneas marginales gruesas y doradas. En total hay 346 páginas. La primera sura *(Al-fatiha)* y las primeros cuatro aleyas de la segunda *(Al-baqara)* tienen los espacios entre líneas iluminados con oro. Los encabezamientos de los capítulos de las páginas contrapuestas en las que aparecen estos versículos, así como las partes externas a las líneas marginales, están cubiertos con panes de oro e iluminaciones muy coloridas en estilo barroco-rococó turco. Todos los encabezamientos de capítulo están escritos en letras *tawqi* blancas sobre ilustraciones doradas. Las aleyas aparecen separadas por rosetas de oro y el final de cada cinco y diez versos viene marcado por rosas de formas variadas situadas en los márgenes de la página. La encuadernación en cuero es marrón por fuera y verde por dentro. La parte exterior presenta diseños florales colocados de forma libre y naturalista en dorado, verde y amarillo.  
El calígrafo, Mustafa Izzet Efendi (1215-1292 / 1801-1876), nació en Tosya y se formó en Estambul. Aprendió la caligrafía con Mustafa Vasıf y Yesarizade Mustafa Izzet Efendi. Sus obras más famosas son las *hilya* (descripciones en prosa del profeta Muhammad) y las hojas con ejercicios caligráficos denominadas *istif*. También fue el autor de las inscripciones del tambor de la cúpula de Ayasofya, que están entre las más famosas del mundo islámico.  
En la decoración de este Corán trabajaron dos artistas: Mehmet Salih, encuadernador jefe de la corte otomana en tiempos del sultán Abdülmecid, y Rashid Efendi, su aprendiz.  
En el siglo XII / XVII, el arte turco empezó a experimentar cambios por la influencia del arte europeo. Este estilo, conocido como barroco-rococó turco, se encuentra especialmente reflejado en las artes del libro. Este Corán es el ejemplo más bello de su aplicación en la decoración de libros.

Las iluminaciones son una parte esencial de los coranes. Durante los siglos XII-XIII / XVIII-XIX, los artistas los decoraron con motivos florales naturalistas y elementos clásicos de influencia europea.

fr.name: Coran.
description:
Coran de 346 pages copié en écriture *naskhi* à l'encre noire sur un délicat papier préparé. Les pages à épaisses lignes de marge dorées comptent chacune 13 lignes de texte. La première sourate (*al-Fatiha*) et les quatre premiers versets de la deuxième (*al-Baqara*) sont enluminés de dorures en interlignage. Les titres de chapitre des deux pages face-à-face sur lesquelles ces versets sont écrits ainsi que les zones extérieures aux lignes de marge sont décorées d'un fond à la feuille d'or et d'enluminures très colorées en style baroque-rococo turc. Tous les titres de chapitres sont copiés en écriture *tawqi*' au-dessus d'une enluminure à l'or. Chaque verset est séparé de ses voisins par des rosettes dorées toutes différentes tandis que, en marge, des motifs de rose de formes variées signalent la fin d'une suite de cinq ou de dix versets. La reliure en cuir est brune à l'extérieur et verte à l'intérieur. L'extérieur présente des motifs floraux de style naturaliste libre à dorures vertes et jaunes.  
La calligraphe de ce coran, Mustafa Izzet Efendi (1215-1292 / 1801-1876 J.-C.), né à Tosya, fut formé à Istanbul. Il apprit la calligraphie auprès de Mustafa Vasif et de Yesarizade Mustafa Izzet Efendi. Ses œuvres les plus célèbres sont des *hilya* (Nobles Descriptions, en prose, du prophète Mahomet) et des feuilles d'exercices de calligraphie appelés *istif*. Les inscriptions accrochées sous la coupole de Sainte-Sophie, parmi les plus célèbres du monde islamique, sont de sa main.  
Deux artistes ont travaillé à la reliure de cet ouvrage. Mehmet Salih, maître relieur à la cour ottomane au temps du sultan Abdulmejid Ier (Abd al-Majid), et son apprenti Rashid Efendi.  
Au début du VIIIe siècle H (XIIe siècle J.-C.), l'art turc commença à changer sous l'influence européenne. Ce style, appelé baroque-rococo, a été appliqué aux arts du livre, et ce coran en est la plus belle illustration.

L’enluminure est un élément naturel du Coran. Les enlumineurs utilisaient des motifs floraux naturalistes influencés par l’Europe conjointement à des éléments classiques pour enluminer le Coran durant les XIIe-XIIIe siècles H (XVIIIe-XIXe siècles J.-C.).

tr.name: Kur’an-ı Kerim.
description:
İnce, aharlı kağıt üzerine siyah mürekkep ve nesih hat ile yazılmıştır. Sayfalar kalın altın yaldız cetvelli ve 13 satırdır. 346 sayfadır. Kur'an'ın I. Fatiha ve II. Bakara suresi, 1-4. ayetleri altın yaldız ile yapılmış *beyne's südûr* tezhip üzerine yazılmıştır. Bu ayetlerin yazılı olduğu karşılıklı iki sayfadaki sure başları ve cetvel dışında kalan bölümler altın yaldız varak kaplanmış ve üzerine çok renkli olarak Türk Barok-Rokoko üslubunda tezhip yapılmıştır. Tüm sure başları altın yaldız üzerine beyaz ve *tevki'i* hatla yazılmış ve tezhiplenmiştir. Ayetler hepsi birbirinden farklı altın rozetlerle ayrılmış, beş ve on ayet sonu sayfa kenarına yapılan farklı formdaki gül motifleri ile belirtilmiştir. Deri olan cildin, dış yüzü kahverengi, iç yüzü ise yeşil renklidir. Cildin dış yüzü, yeşil ve sarı altın yaldız kullanılarak yapılmış serbest natüralist bitkisel desenlidir.  
  
Kur'an'ın hattatı Kazasker Mustafa İzzet Efendi (1801-1876), Tosya'da doğmuş, daha sonra İstanbul'a gelerek eğitim görmüştür. Hattı, Mustafa Vasıf ve Yesarizade Mustafa İzzet Efendi'den öğrenmiştir. Ona en büyük şöhreti sağlayan eserleri hilye ve istifli yazı levhalarıdır. Ayasofya'nın kubbe kasnağında sergilenen İslam dünyasının en büyük levhaları ona aittir.  
  
Kur'an'ın tezhipleri üzerinde iki ayrı müzehhip çalışmıştır. Bunlar, Sultan Abdülmecid döneminde Sarayda Başmücellid olan Mehmet Salih ve onun çırağı olan Raşit Efendi'dir.  
  
H. 12. / M. 18. yüzyıldan itibaren Türk sanatında Avrupa etkisi ile bir değişim yaşanmıştır. Türk Barok- Rokoko üslubu olarak adlandırılan bu üslup, kitap sanatlarına da yansımıştır. Kur'an, bu üslubun kitap süslemelerinde uygulanmış en güzel örneğidir.

Tezhip sanatı, Kur'an'ların ayrılmaz bir parçasıdır. Müzehhipler, 12.-13. / 18.-19. yüzyıllarda Kur'an süslemelerinde, klasik bezeme öğelerinin yanında, Avrupa sanatı etkili natüralist çiçeklerden oluşan desenleri de severek kullanmışlardır.
artist: Hattatı: Kazasker Mustafa İzzet Efendi; Müzehhipleri: Mehmet Salih Efendi, Mustafa Raşid Efendi.

en.name: Qal‘at Misyaf
description:
The city and Citadel of Misyaf is located on the eastern slopes of the coastal mountains of Syria some 45 km west of Hama, on top of a rocky cliff surface. For military movement especially, the citadel (approx 70 m x 170 m) is very well positioned strategically on the fork of the communications routes between coastal Syria and the interior, and along the north–south route. The location had been a coveted for its strategic position since Roman times, and Septum Severum who was Roman Emperor from AD 191 until AD 217 used it as the military headquarters.  
During the medieval period in 389/999, Misyath Fortress, as it was known then, was destroyed by the Byzantine Emperor Basil II. Two subsequent Muslim Dynasties, the Hamdanid and Mirdasid then repossessed it. With the arrival of the Seljuqs, who bestowed the castle on the Banu Munqidh of Shayzar, it was used as a seigneurial residence and summertime location. In 535/1141 the Isma’iliyya al-Nizariyya, a clandestine missionary group who called themselves *Ashab al-Da’wa al-Hadiya* or, “Fellowship of the Guided Calling” took over the citadel. Under the leadership of Sinan Rashid al-Din (r.558–88/1163–93; known as the greatest Isma’iliyya leader of Syria more famously known as “The Third Sheikh of the Mountain”), Misyaf became the official capital of the Isma’iliyya al-Nizariyya Emirate of Mount Bahra. Well defended, the citadel even succeeded in defying a siege by Salah al-Din in 572/1176. Cordial relations between the Isma’iliyya leadership and the Ayyubid rulers, particularly al-Zahir Ghazi of Aleppo, followed.  
The castle continued to be governed by several Isma’ili leaders sent from Almut in Iran during the first half of the 7th/13th century. In 655/1258, the Mongols captured the castle, but the Mamluks freed it subsequently in 658/1260.  
The citadel’s nucleus is the interior fortress, or *qilla*, standing on the southern section of the cliff top. It is square with four towers, one on each corner, and a central ground-level courtyard or *castrum*. The *qilla*, enclosed by a wall with five square towers, once surrounded the entire surface of the cliff. A second, lower, wall surrounds the exterior and is similarly fortified by a number of square-based towers provided with arrow loops. Added during the 6th/12th century, the new exterior entrance-block was of huge dimensions and had formidable defences. A non-direct or elbow- shaped passageway that turns at a right angle northward for about 65 m and which is carved into the rock-face, connects the two great gates. More towers were added, made of larger stones and taller arrow loops, some 170 cm long.  
At the end of the 6th/12th century, when Sinan Rashid al-Din took over, the citadel witnessed a comprehensive renovation programme that included the construction of pentagonal-based towers on all sides. Each tower had five large arrow loops, thus highlighting the important military role played by the citadel during this period. The spaces between the interior and exterior walls were reworked to include reception halls and multipurpose buildings. A palace, built on the upper level of the citadel’s interior and distinguished by an ornamented gateway whose inscriptions attribute it to Hasan bin Mas’ud in 622/1226, is now more or less in ruins.  
The main gate of the citadel was also rebuilt, with the addition of a postrum and the construction of a barbacane, which included a hammam. During the Mamluk period, the castle witnessed major renovation works, such as the merlons along the southern and eastern rooftops, new halls on the second level of the exterior and redecoration of the palace.

en.name: Qur'an stand (*kursi*)
short_description: This tall, hexagonal brass side table has a flat top, six-sided body, and six baluster-shaped feet. The table is inlaid with inscriptional panels offset by engraved or pierced vegetal patterns. The sides are composed of several panels inset within a frame. This stand may originally have been used to support the Qur’an as it was read. For protection, the Qur’an could be stored inside the stand by opening the small doors and placing the text within.

en.name: Hooded cloak (*burnus*)
description: Cloak in green velvet with stencilled decoration of pomegranates and leaves in brown. This velvet is based on the Venetian ones of the 15th and 16th centuries. The cloak has a wide fullness at the bottom and a big hood, formed by four points. The cloak is lined in a green silk, printed in silver vegetal motifs.

en.name: Celebrations outside the station.
description: The German field-postcard part of the German series Die Türkei im Weltkriege (Turkey in the World War) records the procession organised outside Damascus’s Hijaz Railway Station following the arrival of Jamal Pasha during the First World War. According to the printed caption, a military band leads cadets, military school pupils and members of the Jugendwehr, or youth corps, around the station. Their participation reflects the wartime mobilisation of education and youth to physical training and elementary military preparation. The station functions here as a ceremonial entrance to Damascus, where military authority and public spectacle took place. Beside the station stands the Izzat al Malla Building, one of the prominent structures in the developing Halbouni district adjacent to the station.
keywords: Militay; Propaganda; World War; Photography; Conflict

en.name: Mabrak Al-Naqa Mosque and Madrasat Gumushtagin
description:
Situated on the north-east corner of the fortification wall, the complex covers a plot of 29 m x 15 m. The main, northern faade shows clearly the division in three parts, each provided by a proper entrance and distinguished by clear joins in the stonework. The oldest part is the so-called Mabrak al-Naqa on the western side, built of small stones of irregular size. The middle part  
is a prayer-hall, whilst the largest part is the *madrasa* on the eastern side.  
The Mabrak al-Naqa, “the place where the she-camel kneeled” is, according to the local tradition, the place where the Prophet Muhammad let his she-camel kneel down during his visit to the city on trade. The date of the shrine itself remains unclear but it continues to be a place of prayer. Certainly, the *qibla* wall forms the oldest part of the building, whereas the square forecourt was probably added during the medieval period. The *mihrab* is decorated with a *spolia*; a semicircular carved shell and two undecorated antique pillars. Below the shell there is an inscription in *kufic* script, which describes the place as “the Mosque of the Prophet”. The “kneeling spot” is an antique stone slab in front of the prayer-niche with several depressions, interpreted as the imprints of the camel.  
The middle part of the Mabrak  
complex, a small, square oratory of around 6.5 m x 6.5 m with a prayer- niche was added at a later stage, as the Mabrak itself was originally preceded by a square forecourt. The prayer-room  
is divided by a single transverse arch, which supports the roof-slabs in traditional local style. Here also, the prayer-niche is decorated with two antique spiral-fluted columns and tapped with a  
carved shell. A *madrasa* occupies the eastern half of the complex, commissioned by Gumushtagin in 530/1136, as mentioned in the incription above the entrance. It follows the four-  
*iwans*\-in-axial-symmetry layout whereby the four *iwans* are placed around a central courtyard. The west and east *iwans* are separated from the courtyard by a  
huge arch supported by antique abutments. The north *iwan* and the south *qibla iwan* have three doorways surmounted by windows with pointed arches. The *qibla iwan* is  
emphasised by its double depth of 8 m, requiring an extra transverse arch to support the roof. Originally, the inner walls were covered with red plaster; the yellowish plaster is a later addition.  
  
This *madrasa* is the earliest surviving example of a religious college in Syria. Both the institution of *madrasa* and the four-*iwans*\-in axial-symmetry layout are of  
Iranian origin, first introduced to Syria in the mid 5th/11th century and which subsequently spread all over the Muslim territories. Here, instead of barrel-vaults that were the usual covering for  
*iwans* in Iran, the roof is made of flat basalt slabs in the local Hauran style. Also exceptional for Iranian *madrasas*, the courtyard was covered by a dome, probably for climatic  
reasons but also because similar central domes have long been known in the local tradition, as can be seen in the impressive churches in Ezra en route between Damascus and  
Bosra.  
The minaret is only accessible via the roof of the complex and was probably a later addition from the first half of the 6th/13th century.

en.name: *Saka Postu* (small alcove where a new apprentice observed elders)
description: Upon entering the printing house through the large wooden door, one passes through the vaulted corridor and reaches the barrel-vaulted chamber. In the left-hand corner there is a raised platform covered by a hide over a carpet. Here *Nevniyaz* (a newly accepted apprentice) would sit and observe for a period of three days, at the conclusion of which he would decide whether to stay or leave.

en.name: Chapel of Nossa Senhora da Rocha
description: Perched on the edge of a sheer cliff overlooking the sea is the small white Chapel of Nossa Senhora da Rocha. It remains as a place of worship today, having been an important centre of Mozarab pilgrimage during the Islamic period. The main body of the church is quadrangular in shape and is crowned by an eight-sided dome dating from no earlier than the 17th century. The most remarkable feature is the porch or narthex where two columns and two ancient capitals support three semicircular arches. This natural platform seems to have been the site of other earlier constructions and was encircled along the whole length of the cliff by a masonry wall that has since disappeared; gradually swallowed up when the cliff face has fallen into the sea on successive occasions.

es.name: Capilla de Nossa Senhora da Rocha
description: En el extremo de un promontorio cortado a pico sobre el mar, blanquea la pequeña capilla de Nossa Senhora da Rocha (Nuestra Señora de la Roca), todavía hoy lugar de culto y que ya era centro de peregrinación *mozárabe* en época musulmana. El cuerpo del templo es cuadrangular y está coronado por una cúpula octogonal, que no será anterior al siglo XVII. Lo más notable es el alpende o pórtico, en el que dos fustes y dos capiteles tardoantiguos sostienen tres pequeños arcos centrales. En esta plataforma natural parece haber habido otras construcciones, y está rodeada, en todo el borde del acantilado, por un muro de albañilería que ha ido desapareciendo, engullido por sucesivos derrumbamientos sobre el mar.

cs.name: Mikulov
description: Části středověkého hradu byly začleněny do přestavby v manýristický zámek. Gotický palác byl přeměněn na Sál předků, vyzdoben nástěnnými malbami s portréty významných členů rodu, bylo postaveno divadlo a zřízen reprezentativní vstup do zámku. Kardinál Dietrichstein zde shromáždil jednu z největších evropských knihoven své doby. Soubor obohacený konfiskacemi knihoven protestantů byl odvezen r. 1645 Švédy. Dnešní knižní fond z 18. století obsahuje rodové knihovny získané koupí nebo dědictvím. Dominantu proti zámku ve spodní části náměstí proti Sv. Kopečku tvoří pohřební kostel Dietrichsteinů, původně Loreta. R. 1700 vypracoval J. B. Fischer z Erlachu projekt na její přestavbu, autorství současné architektury však není zcela jasné. Původní jednověžové renesanční průčelí bylo nahrazeno monumentální fasádou (1704–1708). Plastiky jsou od brněnského A. Rigy, reliéfy od M. Rotha.

Kardinál a pobělohorský vládce Moravy F. Dietrichštejn, ústřední představitel protireformace, zde budoval své sídlo jako zemské hlavní město. Části středověkého hradu byly začleněny do přestavby v manýristický zámek. Kardinál zde shromáždil jednu z největších evropských knihoven své doby. Soubor obohacený konfiskacemi knihoven protestantů byl odvezen r. 1645 Švédy. Při klášteře kapucínů nechal kardinál vystavět  r. 1622 poutní kapli – Svatou chýši, věrnou koupi italského Loreta, jednu z prvních v českých zemích. Symbolizovala přenesení části “svaté země” na rekatolizovanou Moravu.
artist: Knížecí rod Dietrichsteinů: Adam z Dietrichštejna (1575–1590), kardinál a kníže František z Dietrichštejna (1570–1636), Ferdinand z Dietrichštejna (1655–1698), Leopold z Dietrichštejna, Walter Xaver z Dietrichštejna (1664–1738)

Giovanni Giacomo Tencalla (c. 1600–c. 1650), Giovanni Tencalla, Johann Bernhard Fischer von Erlach (1656 Graz – 1723 Vídeň), Anton Riga (kolem 1660 Královec – 1728 Brno), Christian Alexander Oedtl (1654 Paznaun – 1731 Vídeň), Ignác Lengelacher (1698 Unter Paissenberg – 1780 Baden), Heinrich Gottfried Forster, Franz Anton Maulbertsch (1724 Langenargen am Bodensee – 1796 Vídeň)
history: Dietrichštejnové získali panství r. 1575. Kardinál a pobělohorský vládce Moravy F. Dietrichštejn, ústřední představitel protireformace zde budoval své sídlo jako zemské hlavní město. Povolal řády kapucínů (1611) a piaristů (1636) a církevními i světskými stavbami zde vytvořil centrum katolické reprezentace. Mikulov postihlo několik požárů (1663, 1719, 1784, 1945), takže původní stav rezidence je překryt řadou přestaveb, zachovávajících však většinou funkční i prostorové dispozice.

tags: Protireformace, konfiskace, pohanství, alegorie, Loreta, synagoga, Židé

en.name: Mikulov Town
description: The dominant landmarks of the town are Sv. Kopeček (Holy Hill), the Loreto) Chapel, the Holy Trinity Column, the Upper Synagogue, the monasteries, the Jewish quarter and a mannerist chateau, originally part of a medieval castle. An extravagant entrance to the chateau was constructed together with a theatre and a “Hall of Ancestors”, decorated with murals featuring portraits of significant family members. Cardinal Dietrichstein also created one of the largest libraries in Europe with a collection of books that was further expanded by items confiscated from Protestant libraries and which was looted in turn by the Swedish army in 1645. Today’s collection, dating from the 18th century, consists of the Dietrichstein family’s libraries acquired through purchase or inheritance. Situated opposite the chateau, in the lower section of the square facing Svatý Kopeček, is a chapel, originally modelled on an Italian Loreto to symbolise the birthplace of Christ, in which the family’s dead are interred. J. B. Fischer von Erlach designed its reconstruction in 1700 but who was responsible for its current form is not clear. The original Renaissance frontage with a tower was replaced by a monumental facade between 1704 and 1708. The sculptures are by the Brno artist, A. Riga, and the reliefs by M. Roth.

Inhabited since pre-history, Mikulov is a small town in south Moravia. Cardinal Dietrichstein, ruler of Moravia after the Battle of White Mountain in 1620 and a leading figure in the Czech Counter-Reformation, made his seat the hub of Moravia. Parts of a medieval castle were incorporated into a mannerist chateau where the cardinal created one of the largest libraries in Europe. He had a pilgrimage chapel built, modelled on an Italian Loreto and one of the first of its kind in Czech lands. Part of the town was an important cultural centre for the Jewish community.
artist: Counts Dietrichstein: Adam of Dietrichstein (1575–1590), Cardinal and Count Franz of Dietrichstein (1570–1636), Ferdinand of Dietrichstein (1655–1698), Leopold of Dietrichstein (1748–1784), Walter Xaver of Dietrichstein (1664–1738)

Giovanni Giacomo Tencalla (c. 1600–c. 1650), Giovanni Tencalla, Johann Bernhard Fischer von Erlach (1656 Graz – 1723 Vienna), Anton Riga, Christian Alexander Oedtl (1654 Paznaun – 1731 Vienna), Ignaz Lengelacher (1698 Unter Peissenberg – 1780 Baden), Heinrich Gottfried Forster, Franz Anton Maulbertsch (1724, Langenargen am Bodensee – 1796 Vienna)
history: The Dietrichsteins acquired the demesne in 1575 when Cardinal Dietrichstein became ruler of Moravia after the Battle of White Mountain in 1620. He was a leading figure in the Czech Counter-Reformation and made Mikulov his seat and the hub of Moravia. Summoning the Capuchin and Piarist orders (1611; 1636), he created a centre for the Catholic Church with both sacred and secular buildings. Mikulov was damaged by fire in 1663, 1719, 1784 and 1945 and the Cardinal’s residence has consequently undergone several reconstructions which have, however, held true to the original functional and spatial intentions.
keywords: Counter-Reformation, confiscation, paganism, allegory, Loreto, synagogue, Jewish community
tags: Counter-Reformation, confiscation, paganism, allegory, Loreto, synagogue, Jewish community

ar.name: مصابيح مسجد
description: من عام 1356 إلى عام 1363 أمر السلطان ناصر الحسن ببناء مسجد في القاهرة. وقد زينه بأفخر المصابيح المصنوعة من الزجاج المطلي بالميناء. وأكثر هذه المصابيح روعة كانت مصنوعة في ورشات حلب ودمشق. وفي المسجد فقد كانت المصابيح تعلق بسلاسل برونزية رفيعة من السقف وكانت تزين المكان أكثر مما تضيئه. ووفقا للمحيط الديني فإن زخرفتها تكون  متواضعة : حيث يستخدم بعض الأرابيسك الأنيق وبعض فواتح السور الشهيرة المعبرة عن الضوء  من القرآن وإهداء للمتبرع المعروف. ومصابيح المساجد بأبهة المتبرع تعلن كرمه وثروته. وفي عام 1885 يعتقد أن اثنين من هذه المصابيح الثمينة أشتريت من مصر من قبل الأرشيدوق النمساوي فرديناند ماكس وهو الإمبراطور المستقبلي للمكسيك وقد زينت واحد من قاعات قصره الممتع قرب تريسته .

en.name: Mosque lamps
description: From 1356 to 1363, Sultan an-Nasir al-Hasan commissioned a mosque to be erected in Cairo. He decorated it most luxuriously with mosque lamps made of enamelled glass. The most magnificent of them were produced in the workshops of Aleppo and Damascus. In the mosque, they are suspended on fine bronze chains from the ceiling, reminiscent of the star-spangled heavens. They decorate the space more than they illuminate it. In accordance with the religious surroundings, their ornamentation is modest: some elegant arabesques, the initial lines of the famous verses of light from the Qur'an and a dedication to the renowned benefactor. Together with his crest, the mosque lamps announce his generosity and his wealth. In 1855, it is believed that two of these precious mosque lamps were brought out of Egypt by the Austrian archduke Ferdinand Max, the future Emperor of Mexico; he decorated one of the splendid halls of his pleasure palace near Trieste with them.

ar.name: أربع قطع قماش ذات صفوف من البجع والماشية
description: إن العلاقات المتبادلة بين الصين وأوربا قد انعكست في التفاصيل الفنية المتحركة في أواخر العصور الوسطى مثل الأقمشة. وخلال التوسع الأعظم فإن الإمبراطورية المغولية امتدت من القاهرة إلى بغداد وهذا يعني مزيجا من التقاليد المصورة الشرقية والغربية التي بقيت مسيطرة في ورشات القماش المنغولية والذي جعل تحديد أماكن القطع القماشية صعبا. وفي هذه القطع الزرقاء الداكنة نرى تأثيرات من الفن الصيني في الأزهار والحيوانات.
dates: أواخر القرن الثالث عشر  - بداية القرن الرابع عشر

de.name: Vier Gewebefragmente mit gereihten Pelikanen und Rindern
description: Die wechselseitigen Beziehungen zwischen China und Europa werden auf spätmittelalterlichen, mobilen Objekten, wie den Textilien erkennbar. Das mongolische Reich reichte während seiner größten Expansion von China bis nach Bagdad. So kam es in den mongolischen Textilwerkstätten zu einer Vermischung von östlichen und westlichen Darstellungstraditionen. Diese  erschwert die genaue Lokalisierung von textilen Objekten. Auf diesen dunkelblauen Fragmenten sieht man Einflüsse chinesischer Kunst in den Rankenmotiven und Tieren.
holder: MAK – Österreichisches Museum für angewandte Kunst / Gegenwartskunst
partner: MAK – Österreichisches Museum für angewandte Kunst

en.name: Four textile fragments with rows of pelicans and cattle
description: The reciprocal relations between China and Europe are reflected in mobile artefacts of the Late Middle Ages, such as textiles. During its greatest expansion, the Mongolian Empire stretched from China to Baghdad. This meant that a mixture of eastern and western pictorial traditions held sway in the Mongolian textile workshops, which makes localisation of textile artefacts difficult. On these dark-blue fragments we see influences from Chinese art in the flowers and animals.
keywords: Textile; dark-blue; Iran; China; silk; Chinese influence; floral decoration; animal decoration
partner: MAK – Austrian Museum of Applied Arts / Contemporary Art

en.name: *Maria Eleonora Regina Johanna Juliana Pejačević* born *Erdödy de Monyorokerek*
description:
Countess Eleonora, depicted in a garden offering incense into an urn that stands in front of a statue of Cupid, has just married Count Karlo III Pejačević who is 25 years her senior; she is his second wife. Her dress is of fine, expensive material decorated with pearls. Her grey, powdered hair is also dressed with pearls.  
Marija Eleonora was born into the Erdödy family, members of which played a very important role in the history of Croatia.  
The Pejačević family, originally from Bulgaria, was one of the aristocratic families to whom the Habsburg Crown granted land in Slavonia after its liberation from the Ottomans.  
The painter of this portrait, J. G. Weickert, belonged to the generation of Austrian Rococo painters, the work of which already demonstrated components of the Neo-Classical style, which is especially visible in this portrait. For example, the pastel colours and charming grace of the countess' slender and vivacious figure, still in the Rococo style, have been infiltrated by undefined changes of tone, a degree of measure and a breath of melancholy underlined by the ambient Neo-Classical architecture.  
This is more than the portrait of a person: the content of the painting shows the countess herself in a symbolic act of throwing incense into an urn in front of a statuette of Cupid, an act supplicating happiness in marriage. Considering that the countess was 19 years old and that she had just married a man 25 years her senior, there were definite reasons to eternalise this act.  
In style, the portrait heralds the new age of the Enlightenment.

A portrait of Countess Maria Eleonora Pejačević, who by birth and marriage, belonged to two important noble families in Croatia. The painting is by the Austrian painter, J. G. Weickert, who was working during the Rococo period but whose paintings already show influences of the Neo-classical style. In this painting, the Neo-classical style is especially apparent, while it also announces the new spirit of the Enlightenment.
keywords: Portrait, Pejačević family; fashion; jewellery; women; mythology; Enlightenment; Neo-Classicism

ar.name: زوج من الأساور ذات زخرفة مقببة
description: الحجول (أساور) مثل هذه المعروضة هنا هي من عصر سلالة البوسعيد وكانت في بعض الأحيان ترتدى في القدم (خلاخل) وقد كانت ترتدي بشكل أزواج من قبل النساء والأطفال في وسط وشمال عُمان. وتوجد أحجار الصغيرة داخل الخشخيشة التي تصدر صوتا مع حركة الشخص الذي يرتديها. وإن استخدام مجوهرات الصدف يعود للألف الرابع قبل الميلاد والنماذج ذات النقطة في الدائرة الأكثر تعقيدا وجدت في الألف الثالثة والثانية قبل الميلاد في أوعية مصنوعة من الحجر الطري حيث كانت ترتب عادة في صفوف وتجمع مع العناصر الخطية. واليوم يستمر استخدام نماذج النقطة في الدائرة (الدائرة المنقوطة) من قبل الفنانين العُمانيين حيث يمكن رؤيتها اليوم على الطبول الخشبية، ونصول الفؤوس، وأغمدة السكاكين في شبه جزيرة مسندم، وكذلك على الحلي الفضية في شمال عُمان، والصناعات الفخارية في محافظة ظفار.

en.name: Pair of Bracelets with Chased Decoration
description: *Hujuls* (Bracelets) such as these from the al-Busaid Dynasty, sometimes worn as anklets, were worn in paired sets by women and children in Central and Northern Oman. Small stones sealed inside rattle with the movement of wearer. These are fine examples of one of Oman's oldest design elements, circles with central dots. Its use on shell jewellery has been dated to the 4th millennium BC. More complex dot-in-circle patterns are found on 3rd and 2nd millennium BC soft-stone vessels where they are typically arranged in rows and combined with linear elements. Today dot-in-circle patterns continue to be used by Omani artisans working in clay, wood, copper, silver and many other materials. They are seen on wooden drums, axe blades and knife scabbards of the Musandam Peninsula, on the silver jewellery of northern Oman and on the pottery of Dhofar.
keywords: Hujul; Bracelet; Silver; Jewellery; Dot-in-Circle

en.name: *Illustrations of the One Thousand and One Nights, vol. 1*
short_description: The *One Thousand and One Nights* played an important role in bringing the East and the West closer together. Galland was its first French translator, translating with much liberty what he had been able to understand in the early 18th century. The translated *One Thousand and One Nights* were extremely successful, and became the subject of a variety of art forms, both allowing Europeans to become better acquainted with the Arab world, but also forming the basis for lasting stereotypes.
keywords: Orientalism

fr.name: *Illustrations de Les Mille et une nuits. Volume I*
short_description: Les *Mille et une Nuits* sont un lien exceptionnel entre Orient et Occident. Le premier traducteur en français de ces contes est Galland, au début du XVIIIe siècle, qui prend quelques libertés avec les textes qu'il a pu entendre. Les *Mille et une Nuits* connaissent un succès extraordinaire, sous des formes artistiques diverses, contribuant à la fois à une meilleure connaissance de l'Orient par les Occidentaux mais aussi à la constitution de stéréotypes durables.
keywords: Orientalisme

ar.name: بيجان وهو يأخذ عنان جواد غوشتاهام ، صفحة  من الشهنامة (كتاب الملوك) بقلم أبو القاسم الفردوسي (توفي عام 1010)
description: إن ملحمة الشهنامة الشعرية  للفردوسي التي اكتملت عام 1010 التي تقص التاريخ الأسطوري لشاهات إيران (الملوك) حتى الغزو العربي للبلاد عام 642 واعتناق البلاد دين الإسلام ، وهذه الملحمة كانت مصدر إلهام للعديد من النسخ المصورة والصفحة الحالية فصلت عن نسخة تعرف باسم ""الرأس الكبير Big Head"" للشهنامة وهذا الاسم يشير إلى الميزة الخاصة لأكثرية رسومها :الرؤوس الكبيرة للشخوص البشرية.

en.name:
Bijan takes the reins of Gushtaham’s horse  
Folio detached from a *Shahnameh* (Book of Kings) by Abu’l-Qasim Firdausi (d. 1010)
description: Recounting the legendary history of Iran’s shahs (kings) up to the Arab conquest in 642 AD and the country’s adoption of Islam, Firdausi’s epic poem the *Shahnameh* (Book of Kings), completed in 1010, inspired many illustrated copies. The present folio was detached from a copy that is known as the “Big Head” *Shahnameh*. This name refers to the characteristic feature of the majority of its paintings: the large heads of its human figures.
artist: Dated 1494, copied by Salik b. Sa‘id, and dedicated to Sultan 'Ali Mirza

en.name: Villa Ghisilieri
description: The villa was not only a place for leisure but also the administrative centre of many commercial and rural activities. The villa of the patron had its own courtyard, separated from the hamlet. This is where a weekly market took place.

it.name: Villa Ghisilieri
description: La villa del proprietario, con la sua corte separata dal villaggio, dove si teneva il mercato settimanale. La villa non era solo il luogo del riposo ma anche un centro amministrativo per molte attività commerciali e agricole.

ar.name: ثوب الجلاية
description:
ثوب الجلاية، لونه أسود عليه تطريز كثيف، القبة مطرز عليها شكل القوس وتسمى أيضا "قلايد" وعليه أيضا زخارف نباتية. ويوجد على الردهة، وهي الجزء الخلفي من الكتف، قطعة حرير مطرز عليها بقطبة اللف بأشكال نباتية. الأكمام مطرزة بكثافة بعرق الدوالي، والبنايق مطرزة بعروق نباتية وعرق الريش والمناجل. ترتدي النساء هذا الثوب بشكل أساسي بالاحتفالات، مثل حفلات الزفاف، وهو الثوب الخاص بنساء محافظة الخليل جنوب القدس. اشتهرت الخليل منذ العصور القديمة بالحرف اليدوية، بما في ذلك الخزف والفخار والزجاج والتطريز والجلود والنسيج. يصنع هذا الثوب يدويًا من الحرير والكشمير بغرزة أطلس. ترتدي هذا الثوب النساء المتزوجات فقط، ويتميز بألوانه والغرز وزخارف الأزهار وغرزة الدوالي التي يحملها الفستان. الردفة الأمامية عليها ترقيع من قطع من الحرير الأصفر والبرتقالي والأحمر على شكل مثلثات، وعلى جانبيه قطع من قماش الكشمير. أما الردفة الخلفية للثوب، فمطرزة على قطعة قماش مركبة على الثوب وبلون أزرق، عليها تطريز بأشكال الطيور والنباتات. فإن استخدام الطيور والزهور - ملحوظ بشكل كبير، لكنه لا يحمل أي رمزية خفية، وإن استخدامه بكثرة يرجع لعمل النساء المستمر في الأرض، بالتالي كانت الطبيعة مصدر الإلهام الرئيسي للنساء، ليس فقط في منطقة الخليل ولكن بشكل عام.  
تاريخ الحصول على القطعة: 1983 م.
dates: النصف الأول من القرن التاسع عشر
keywords: تقليدي، منسوجات فلسطينية، ثوب

en.name: Jillayeh Wedding Dress
description: Black dress with heavy embroidery. The chest panel shows chevron pattern embroidery, which is also known as *qalayed* (necklace), as well as many floral motifs, while the back panel shows floral motifs embroidered on silk fabric with special stitches. The sleeves are heavily embroidered with vine leaves, while the *banayeq* (side panels) show motifs of flowers, feathers and *manajel* (thick braid work connecting the dress parts). This dress is mainly worn by the married women of Hebron for ceremonial events like weddings. Located in the West Bank, south of Jerusalem, and founded by the Canaanites in the early Bronze Age, Hebron has been famous since ancient times for handicrafts, including ceramics, pottery, glass, embroidery and leather. This gown is handmade from silk and cashmere using atlas stitch. The dress is worn only by married women of Hebron, and it is unique to them in respect of all the colours, stitches, floral motifs and vine leaf motifs that the dress exhibits. The bottom front panel has yellow, orange and red silk triangles with Kashmir cloth on the sides. The bottom of the back panel has a stitched-in piece of cloth with blue embroidered birds and flowers. The use of birds and flowers does not bear any hidden symbolism; rather, it reflects the continuous work of women on the land and hence their use of nature as a main source of inspiration for their embroidery, not only in Hebron but other regions of Palestine as well.
keywords: Traditional costume; Palestinian Textile; Dress; Clothing

en.name: The Mother of God Umilenie
description: The *Umilenie* (tenderness) Mother of God icons display touching images that depict the Virgin caressing her Child. The distinctive feature of this icon type is that the Christ Child has his face pressed against her cheek and one arm around her neck. Finely executed and balanced in line, color and composition, this icon, the earliest in the Museum of Russian Icons collection, is a particularly beautiful example of this motif.
keywords: Virgin Mary and Child; Religious iconography

en.name: *Interior of the Great Temple at Baalbec*
short_description: This view into the interior of the Temple of Bacchus at Baalbek, Lebanon originally formed appeared in 'Syria, The Holy Land, Asia Minor, &c', illustrated views printed in 3 series over 2 volumes (37 plates, 37 plates, and 48 plates for each series respectively) including maps and title pages. The publication resulted from the 1836-1838 collaboration between the painter William Henry Bartlett, the engraver Ebenezer Challis and the Publishers Fisher, Son and Co. The architectural and artistic details they recorded subsequently inspired European Neoclassical architects and artists such as Robert Adam, who based one of the ceilings at Osterley House on the ceiling of the Temple of Bacchus and the portico of St George's, Bloomsbury on its portico. Since the 1860s, many tourists visited the site, including, in 1898, the German emperor Wilhelm II. Struck by the magnificence of the ruins, he dispatched a German archaeological team, whose subsequent work resulted in a meticulous, illustrated publication that further popularised the site.
holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Authority
artist: Drawn by William Henry Bartlett; engraved by Ebenezar Challis

en.name: *Allegory of Sight* (Venus and Cupid in a Picture Gallery)
description:
From a series of paintings called the “The Five Senses”, this painting by Jan Brueghel the Younger is known as *The Allegory of Sight*. It displays a virtual treasure trove of Paintings, Sculpture, Scientific tools and more. At the center of the piece is Venus examining herself in a handheld mirror. A beautiful Turkish Carpet is draped over the table to the left of Venus. The fact that such a carpet is displayed among such a treasure trove of expensive and exquisite objects shows its importance.  
This painting shows an imaginary collection of art, scientific instruments, and curiosities of nature. It belongs to a popular genre of pictures developed by Antwerp artists in the 1600s that portray the cabinets, or rooms, collectors filled with art and wonders. The inclusion of Venus examining herself in a mirror reveals that this scene also doubles as an allegory of sight, and was part of a series of works depicting the five senses.  
Though an allegory, the scene contains artwork and objects based on real examples, including paintings by famous Flemish artist Peter Paul Rubens (1577–1640) and Jan Brueghel’s father, Jan Brueghel the Elder. The ancient and modern sculptures as well as the array of vessels, jewels, coins, measuring instruments, and shells strewn around the room can be matched with surviving items.  
The remarkable works depicted by Jan the Younger illustrate the types of objects the well to do collected in the 1600s to demonstrate their status and knowledge. Within the space around you are works of art and nature that represent the varied categories of collecting popular at this time.
artist: Jan Brueghel the Younger, Flemish (active Antwerp)
keywords: Painting; Breugal; Allegory

en.name: Arraiolos carpet
description:
Throughout the 17th century, the oriental pattern that characterised the pieces from the early production of Arraiolos carpets was progressively replaced by a traditional standard, though one that also derives from the Persian medallion- and animal-based carpets. Known as “animal pattern” carpets, due to the preponderance and protagonism of their animalistic motifs, this type of carpet best divulges and characterises the Arraiolos carpet-weaving industry of the 18th century.  
In this carpet, the large central, triple, concentric, and radiant medallion stands out, being that the last frame, with its blue background, is decorated with small cocks and Caucasian palm flowers. In the remaining field, organised according to a quarter-plan layout, the decoration is made up of vases of carnations and various animals. At each corner of the central field are grandiose and colourful peacocks, holding flowering branches in their beaks. In front of these elements appear rabbits, whereas above them there are deer, flanked by cypresses. Other small animals – parrots, ducks, birds of paradise and small dogs and cockerels – and tinted flowers fill the remaining space.  
With a green background, the border is decorated with continuous and zigzagging branches, whose stalks sprout small flowers and leaves, upon which are poised miniscule birds.
place: From a church belonging to the Convent of Louriçal (Order of St. Claire), Pombal, Portugal
keywords: rug; carpet; animal pattern; Arraiolos; birds; medallion
materials: Wool; embroidery; oblique or Slavic cross-stitch (known as *ponto de Arraiolos*)
tags: oblique or Slavic cross-stitch (known as ponto de Arraiolos)

en.name: Norman Castle
description:
The Normans’ military campaign for the reconquest of Sicily to the Latinity, was conducted through a patient and backbreaking war of position directed round some strongholds, whose function, once hostilities had ceased, was to control the territory which had just been won. Along the course of the River Simeto (a privileged way of access from the Ionian coast to the interior of the island), some fortified buildings were erected in response to the detailed reasoning of military strategy. These buildings had two purposes: they assured the safety of outposts for the cavalry employed along the borders against the enemy, guaranteeing control of the stronghold of Catania; they also safeguarded the Normans from possible insurrection from the local inhabitants. These structures, built in order to guard the Valley of the Simeto, still dominate the historic centres of Motta Sant’Anastasia, Paternò and Adrano today, with their impressive volumetry. They are simple quadrilateral towers of high-relief profile, erected in elevated positions and surrounded by a wall. The typology of solid keeps on inaccessible rocky heights (at one time completely isolated), and the quadrangular matrix of the structure that connects them with the donjons, were installed at the same time by the Normans on French and English territory. For his reason they are also known as *dongioni* a term that appeared in Italy from the middle of the 12th century, but with a difference from the original French *donjon*, the Italian term indicating a fortified citadel within a larger castled area.  
Founded, according to tradition, by Great Count Ruggero in about 1070, the castle stood on the edge of the medieval inhabited area. Probably the original structure on a quadrilateral plan was recast in the 14th century. It is halfway between the isolated *mastio*, in the French style, and the lordly palace, according to a residential variant of the fortified edifice already seen at Paternò. The massive towered building is accentuated by the few small openings and it becomes even more menacing by the low walls with which it is surrounded on all sides, dating from between the 15th and 16th centuries, and strengthened on the corners by polygonally leaning towers. The large elevation of the building (33.7 m.) is divided into five floors.  
Today the castle houses three important institutions within its walls: a historicalartistic- literary archive, the Regional Archaeological Museum, and the Pinacoteque. There are some interesting exhibits in the rich Archaeological Museum, finds from the history of the structure starting from the Neolithic period to the Arab and Norman eras. Architectonic elements of particular interest include those dating from the Norman era (kept in the basement of the building) and recovered during the restoration work on the castle, and some coins dating from the same period, valuable witnesses of Norman coinage in Sicily.

es.name: Castillo Normando
description:
La campaña militar de los normandos para devolver Sicilia a la cristiandad se llevó a cabo también mediante una paciente y extenuante guerra de posiciones articulada en torno a algunas plazas fuertes cuya función, al cesar las hostilidades, fue controlar el territorio apenas conquistado. A lo largo del curso del río Simeto (vía privilegiada de acceso desde la costa jónica hacia el interior de la isla) se habían erigido algunas de estas edificaciones fortificadas, que respondían a precisas razones de estrategia militar: por un lado, aseguraban puestos avanzados seguros para los caballeros que combatían al enemigo en la frontera, garantizando el control de la estratégica plaza fuerte de Catania; por otro, preservaban a los normandos de eventuales insurrecciones de los habitantes locales. Tales construcciones, edificadas para guardar el valle del Simeto, dominan aún hoy, con sus imponentes volúmenes, los centros históricos de Motta Sant’Anastasia, Paternò y Adrano. Son severas torres de cuatro lados de perfil descollante, levantadas en lugares elevados y circundadas por un recinto de murallas. La tipología de firmes torreones protegidos sobre ásperas alturas rocosas (antaño completamente aisladas) y la matriz cuadrangular de la planta los entronca con los conocidos *donjons* difundidos por los normandos en el mismo periodo en los territorios franceses e ingleses. Por ello son conocidos también como *dongioni*, término que aparece en Italia a mediados del siglo XII pero con una acepción ligeramente diferente respecto a la palabra original francesa, por cuanto el vocablo italiano designaba una ciudadela fortificada situada en el interior de un área castellana más vasta.  
Fundado, según la tradición, por el gran conde Ruggero alrededor de 1070, el Castillo surge en el margen del pueblo medieval. Probablemente el cuerpo original de fábrica, de planta cuadrada, fue alterado en el siglo XIV. El tipo es el intermedio entre el *mastio* aislado, a la francesa, y el palacio señorial, según una variante en clave residencial de edificio fortificado que se encuentra ya en Paternò. El macizo aspecto torreado, subrayado por las pocas aberturas, se vuelve aún más amenazante por la obra baja abaluartada que lo ciñe por todos los lados, reforzada en los ángulos por torres de escarpa poligonal, que puede datarse entre los siglos XV y XVI. La gran altura del edificio (33,7 m) está dividida en cinco pisos.  
Hoy, el Castillo alberga en su interior tres importantes instituciones: el Archivo Histórico-Artístico-Literario, el Museo Arqueológico Regional y la Pinacoteca. En el rico Museo Arqueológico se exponen interesantes hallazgos relativos a la historia del asentamiento, que van del neolítico a las épocas árabe y normanda. Resultan de especial interés algunos elementos arquitectónicos del periodo normando (están en el hueco bajo la escalera del edificio), recuperados durante los trabajos de restauración del Castillo, y algunas monedas del mismo periodo, preciosos testimonios de la acuñación normanda en Sicilia.

ar.name: شاهدة قبر.
description:
قاعدة الشاهدة مزينة بنحت، يمثل النباتات التي اختصت بشواهد مدينة باليرمو، كسرت أجزاء من طرفيها. النحت بالكتابة العربية بخط كوفي متطاول، يسمى: الخط الفاطمي، والعبارة هي: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم، صلى الله على النبي محمد وعلى آله أجمعين. ﴿ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذَآئِقَةُ الْمَوْتِ وَإِنَّمَا تُوَفَّوْنَ أُجُورَكُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ فَمَن زُحْزِحَ عَنِ النَّارِ وَأُدْخِلَ الْجَنَّةَ فَقَدْ فَازَ وَما الْحَيَاةُ الدُّنْيَا إِلاَّ مَتَاعُ الْغُرُورِ﴾(3/ آل عمران/185). هذا قبر أيوب بن مخلف النساج، الذي توفي يوم السبت أول رجب من سنة 517 (25/9/1123) رحمه الله.  
إن صناعة النسيج كانت منتشرة انتشارا واسعا في صقلية، تشهد بذلك كتابة أخرى من عام 462 / 1072 محفوظة في المتحف الإقليمي لصقلية ( الرقم المتحفي: قائمة القديس يوحنا 61) َتذّكر إبراهيم نساج "دباغ" و المقصود بهذه الصناعة صناعة النسيج الحريري.

قبر يحمل نقائش كوفية. وفي الغالب، يقدم القبر والشاهدة معاً عبارات مأخوذة من القرءان؛ تكون مرفقة في بعض الأحيان بذكر مناقب الميت. هنا تتواجد إحالة إلى مهنة الميت، وهو نساج، مما يشكل دليلا على حيوية فنون الحياكة التي كان يشتغل بها الحرفيون المسلمون في صقلية خلال تلك الفترة.
keywords: شاهدة قبر؛ عمارة عربية؛ نورمندية.

en.name: Sepulchral stele.
description: The stele has a shaped base decorated with an elegant frieze with plant volutes in a style exemplified by the funerary stelae of Palermo. Both edges have been damaged. The Arabic script is in elongated *kufic* characters in the Fatimid style. According to M. Amari (see Bibliography), it reads: ‘ In the name of God the compassionate … give peace. Each soul must savour its own ability, because the day of resurrection (now) whoever misses hell, barely, and makes it to Paradise, has attained a great triumph. The life of this world … illusion. The power … Prophet. This is the tomb of Ayyub (son of …) Mukhallaf, the fuller, who died on Saturday in the first ten days of Rajab of the year five hundred and seventeen \[25 August to 3 September 1123\]. God have mercy on him’. The textile industry was very widespread in Sicily, as attested by another inscription from AH 462 / AD 1072 still kept at the Regional Gallery of Sicily (San Giovanni list no. 61), which mentions Ibrahim, a *dibag* (silk cloth) weaver.

Tomb with *kufic* inscriptions. Tombs and stelae often bore formulas taken from the Qur’an, sometimes with expressions of the virtues of the deceased. In this case, the dead man’s trade is mentioned (weaver), evidence of the vitality of textile production by Muslim craftsmen in Sicily at that time.
holder: Regional Gallery of Sicily, Abatellis Palace
keywords: Arab-Norman; funerary object; calligraphy; gravestone; tombstone
partner: Regional Gallery of Sicily - Abatellis Palace

es.name: Estela sepulcral.
description:
La estela presenta una base silueteada, decorada con un elegante friso con volutas vegetales, un estilo muy extendido en las estelas funerarias de Palermo. Ambos bordes aparecen mutilados. La inscripción está en caracteres cúficos alargados, rasgo propio del estilo fatimí. Según la intepretación de Michele Amari, la inscripción reza: “En el nombre de Dios piadoso \[…\] conceda paz. Todas las almas deberán degustar su propia valía, porque el día de la resurrección \[entonces\] aquel que sea apartado del fuego y conducido al paraíso, aquel se salvará. La vida de aquí abajo / \[...\] engaño. El poder \[...\] Profeta. Esta es la tumba de Ayyub \[hijo de...\] Mujallaf, el batanero, que murió un sábado, en la primera década de *rayab* en el año quinientos diecisiete \[25 de agosto a 3 de septiembre de 1123\]. Que Dios se apiade de él”.  
La actividad textil estaba muy extendida en Sicilia, como demuestra otra inscripción del año 462 / 1072, conservada también en la Galería Regional de Sicilia (n.º de inventario Elenco San Giovanni 61), en la que se cita a Ibrahim, tejedor de *dibag*, es decir telas de seda.

Tumba con inscripciones cúficas. Tumbas y estelas suelen contener fórmulas extraídas del Corán, a veces junto con la exaltación de las virtudes del finado. En este caso, hay una referencia a la profesión del difunto, tejedor, lo cual da idea de la vitalidad del sector textil en manos de los artesanos musulmanes en la Sicilia de aquella época.
holder: Galería Regional de Sicilia Palacio Abatellis
keywords: arquitectura árabo-normanda; estela funeraria;  lápida funeraria
partner: Galería Regional de Sicilia - Palacio Abatellis

fr.name: Stèle funéraire.
description: Cette stèle présente une base façonnée décorée par une élégante frise à volutes végétales, dans un style que l'on retrouve fréquemment sur les stèles funéraires de Palerme. Elle est mutilée sur les deux bords. L'inscription arabe est en caractères coufiques allongés, comme le veut le style fatimide. Elle dit, d'après la lecture qu'en fait Michele Amari : “Au nom du dieu miséricordieux… qu'il donne la paix. Chaque âme devra savourer ses propres compétences, car le jour de la résurrection (alors) celui qui sera entraîné loin du feu, et introduit au paradis, celui-là sera sauvé. La vie d'ici-bas//… tromperie. La puissance … Prophète. Ceci est la tombe d'Ayyub (fils de …) Mukhallaf, le foulonnier, lequel mourut un samedi, dans la première décade du mois de *rejab* en l'an cinq cent dix-sept \[du 25 août au 3 septembre 1123\]. Que Dieu lui fasse miséricorde.” L'activité textile était très répandue en Sicile, comme l'atteste une autre inscription de 462 H / 1072 J.-C., toujours conservée à la Galerie régionale de la Sicile (n° d'inv. Liste san Giovanni 61), dans laquelle est cité Ibrahim, tisseur de *dibag*, c'est-à-dire d'étoffes de soie.

Tombe avec inscriptions coufiques. Tombes et stèles présentent souvent des formules tirées du Coran, parfois avec l'énonciation des vertus du défunt. Ici, il y a une référence au métier du défunt, un tisserand, preuve de la vitalité des arts textiles exercés par les artisans musulmans dans la Sicile de l'époque.
holder: Galerie régionale de la Sicile, palais Abatellis
keywords: architecture arabo-normande ; stèle funéraire ;pierre tombale

it.name: Stele sepolcrale.
description: La stele ha una base sagomata decorata da un elegante fregion a volute vegetali, secondo uno stile ben esemplificato dalla steli funerarie di Palermo. È mutila su entrambi i bordi. La scrittura araba è in caratteri cufici allungati, secondo lo stile fatimide. Recita, secondo la lettura di Michele Amari: “Nel nome del dio pietoso ……… dia pace. Ogni anima dovrà assaporare le proprie competenze, perché il giorno della resurrezione (allora) chi sarà tratto lontano dal fuoco, e introdotto nel paradiso, costui sarà salvo. La vita di quaggiù // …inganno. La potenza ………… Profeta. Questa è la tomba di Ayyûb (figlio di ……) Mukhallaf, il gualchieraio, il quale morì di sabato, nella prima decade di rajab nell'anno cinquecentodiciassette (25 agosto a 3 settembre 1123) Che abbia misericordia di lui Iddio”. L'attività tessile era molto diffusa in Sicilia, come attesta un'altra iscrizione del 462/1072, sempre conservata nella Galleria regionale della Sicilia (n. inv. Elenco san Giovanni 61), nella quale si cita Ibrahim, tessitore di dibag, ovvero panni di seta.

Tomba con iscrizioni cufiche; tombe e stele contengono spesso formule tratte dal Corano, a volte insieme all'enunciazione delle virtù dell'estinto. In questo caso, vi è un riferimento al mestiere del defunto, il tessitore, a riprova della vitalità delle arti tessili esercitate dalle maestranze musulmane nella Sicilia dell'epoca.
holder: Galleria Regionale della Sicilia, Palazzo Abatellis
keywords: architettura arabo - normanna; stele sepolcrale; calligrafia; pietra tombale
partner: Galleria Regionale della Sicilia - Palazzo Abatellis

en.name: Bust of a female saint
description: The bust, thought to resemble St. Barbara or St. Katharine, was originally positioned on a plinth and might have been part of a family altar. Both saints were especially known as objects of worship in Bavaria, a fact that is iconographically typified by the figure’s crowned head. She wears a blouse with collar, brooch and breastplate, partly covered by a coat across her left shoulder and right arm. Bright-eyed, and her head slightly turned to the left, she looks on with the utmost attention. Her hair is parted in the middle and falls down in undulating tresses across the shoulders. The remainder of the original polychrome coating, which was possibly enriched by gold leaf on the crown and breastplate, is found on her lips and eyes. The pale greyish-yellow colour of lime-wood dominates.

The intimate bust of a female saint with long, undulating hair falling down to her shoulders and a crown on her head shows traces of the original polychrome coating, which remains on her eyes and lips, and gives the face a living attitude.
artist: “Weilheim School of sculptors” (with H. Krumpper, H. Degler, G. Petel, B. Steinle, P. Dirr); one of Angermair’s most accomplished small sculptures
keywords: Religious object; sculpted wood
materials: Lime-wood, remains of original polychrome coating
tags: Lime-wood, remains of original polychrome coating

ar.name: طاولة صغيرة.
description:
طاولة مستطيلة الشكل مرتكزة على أربعة قوائم، ومؤلفة من صينية ملبسة ببلاط من زليج *دلفت* ذو الزخارف النباتية والمحاط برواق مفرغ.  
غُطّيتْ الوجوه الأربعة لهذه الطاولة الصغيرة بلوحات منحوتة، مبرومة ومفرغة حسب عناصر زهرية ونباتية.  
ونجد عند الزوايا وفي امتداد قوائم الطاولة وضمن نسق واحد زخارفَ على شكل إطارات بيضوية عمودية تضم نقائش كتابية ذات أحرف نسخية ، تتضمن إحداها اسم الحرفي ومكان صناعة القطعة وذلك حسب العبارة التالية: "صنعه ابن حاج البلاد الجزائر".  
طليت هذه القطعة بعدة ألوان، منها على الخصوص الأخضر، والبرتقالي والذهبي.

طاولة صغيرة، مستطيلة الشكل، ذات أربعة أرجل، مكونة من صينية مكسوة بمربعات من زليج دلفت ذات زخرف زهري محاط برواق مخرم. نقشت اللوحاتُ على الأوجه الأربعة؛ وتتواجد بالزوايا نقائش كتابية بأحرف نسخية؛ وطُلي الأثاث بالأخضر والبرتقالي والذهبي.

en.name: Small table.
description:
A small table, rectangular in shape and on four legs, which consists of a tray clad with Delft earthenware tiles that feature floral decoration and are surrounded by an openwork band.  
Four sides of this small table are covered by sculpted, turned and openwork panels featuring floral or vegetal motifs. In the corners, along the extension of the legs with which they form part, vertical cartouches feature inscriptions in cursive lettering; one of these reveals the name of the craftsman and the location of the object's manufacture through the phrase 'made by Ibn Hadj-la-B'lade al-Djazaïri'.  
The item of furniture is painted in a variety of colours, notably green, orange and gold.

Rectangular four-legged table consisting of a top covered with Delft earthenware tiles with floral decoration surrounded by an openwork railing. There are carved panels on all four sides, and inscriptions in cursive characters on each of the corners. The piece is painted green and orange, and gilded.

es.name: Mesita.
description:
Pequeña mesa rectangular con cuatro patas y tabla revestida de azulejos de Delft con motivos florales, con un reborde a modo de barandilla.  
Los cuatro lados de esta mesita están revestidos de paneles esculpidos, torneados y calados con motivos vegetales y florales. En los ángulos, como prolongación de las patas, con las cuales forman una sola pieza, hay unos cartuchos verticales con inscripciones en caracteres cursivos; una de ellas revela el nombre del artesano y el lugar de fabricación del objeto con la siguiente fórmula: “Hecha por Ibn Hayy al-Balad al-Yazair”.  
El mueble está pintado de varios colores, en particular verde, naranja y dorado.

fr.name: Petite table.
description:
Petite table de forme rectangulaire reposant sur quatre pieds, se composant d'un plateau revêtu de carreaux de faïences de Delft à décor floral et entouré d'une galerie ajourée.  
Quatre faces de cette petite table sont recouvertes de panneaux sculptés, tournés et ajourés selon des motifs floraux et végétaux. Aux angles, dans le prolongement des pieds avec lesquels ils font corps, des cartouches verticaux portent des inscriptions en caractères cursifs ; l'une d'entre elles livre le nom de l'artisan et le lieu de fabrication de l'objet selon la formule suivante : “fait par Ibn Hadj-la-B'lade el-Djazaïr”.  
Le meuble est peint de plusieurs couleurs, notamment le vert, l'orange et le doré.

en.name: High Choir, Organs
description:
The dioceses of Braga and its archbishops was very important within the Catholic Church since the early Middle Ages, before the foundation of the Kingdom of Portugal, as well as throughout the Portuguese history namely in the Baroque period.  
In the North of Portugal during the 18th century there was an active workshop that provided important clients in accordance with the splendour and dignity of the court and religious life. Facing the need to replace the old choir stalls from the 16th century, Braga Cathedral commissioned Marceliano de Araújo and Miguel Francisco da Silva to design the monumental High Choir, the choir stalls and the gilded, carved wood organ cases in 1737.  
The whole set of the choir stalls made of carved and gilded wood includes two rows of seats, the cathedra for the Archbishop and in the centre a remarkable choir stand with the same decorative programme. Due to the major role of music within the Baroque Roman Catholic liturgy, Simão Fontanes was commissioned to build the mechanics of two impressive Baroque organs (1737-1738) with thousands of copper pipes, which are encased in magnificent cases made by Braga's woodcarver Marceliano de Araújo.  
The ceiling painting also belonging to this phase of the cathedral redecoration was executed by Manuel Furtado de Mendonça.  
The organs of the Braga Cathedral, commonly included within the category of the Iberian organs, are installed in two balconies over the central nave. The abundance of sculpture ornaments distributed from the base of the building to the top of the Cathedral allows us to include this artwork as one of the finest examples of the Baroque woodcarving in Portugal.

The choir is located at the west end of the nave and includes two encased organs and choir stalls. They are an example of the work produced in the 18th century by the Northern Portuguese workshop to supply important clients in accordance with the dignity of the court and religious life.
dates: Marceliano de Araújo, early 18th century; Miguel Francisco da Silva, early 18th century; Frei Simon Fontanes, early 18th century; others unknown
artist: High Choir and stalls: Miguel Francisco da Silva (n.d. – Lisbon); Organ cases: Marceliano de Araújo (n.d. – Braga); Organ builder: Frei Simon Fontanes (n.d. – Galiza); Painting: Manuel Furtado de Mendonça.
keywords: Gilding; carved; wood; organ cases, organ; musical instruments
materials: Wood, carved and gilded with gold leaf
tags: Wood, carved and gilded with gold leaf

pt.name: *Coro Alto, Órgãos*
description:
A Igreja de Braga teve, desde antes da fundação da nacionalidade, uma posição de particular relevo na hierarquia da Igreja Católica, nomeadamente durante o período barroco. Com efeito, os prelados bracarenses foram, na sua cidade, os principais promotores da arte barroca. O arcebispo D. Rodrigo de Moura Teles (1704-1728) transformou a Sé de Braga não apenas num espaço de culto harmonioso mas também numa obra de arte que apelava aos sentidos dos crentes. Com a sua morte, ficou o Cabido - corporação de cónegos presentes nas catedrais - encarregado da administração e da gestão dos bens da Diocese.  
No final da década de 1730, os capitulares bracarenses, para abrilhantar a liturgia, resolveram substituir o antigo cadeiral, de finais do século XVI, que, apesar da sua qualidade artística, se encontrava bastante envelhecido. Em 1737, fecharam contrato com Miguel Francisco da Silva, arquitecto a residir no Porto.  
Este conjunto monumental, executado em madeiras nobres, sobressai pela sua opulência e pela qualidade de execução, onde se evidenciam os ornatos de talha dourada. É constituído por dois níveis de assentos e pela cátedra para o arcebispo. O centro do coro é ocupado por uma majestosa estante de coro, realizada de acordo com o restante programa decorativo do coro alto.  
A importância da música na liturgia não foi descurada pelo Cabido, que também mandou construir os dois órgãos monumentais (1737-1738). Para realizar esta magnífica obra, contratou artistas da maior nomeada. A parte mecânica dos órgãos foi entregue ao mestre organeiro Simon Fontanes, proveniente da Galiza. A decoração das caixas ficou a cargo do entalhador bracarense Marceliano de Araújo. A pintura do tecto, executada na mesma campanha de obras, foi da responsabilidade de Manuel Furtado de Mendonça. Os órgãos da Sé de Braga, incluídos na categoria de órgãos ibéricos, estão instalados em dois balcões sobre a nave central e formam um magnífico conjunto barroco, com uma profusão de ornamentos escultóricos que se anima da base do edifício até ao topo da Catedral.

O cadeiral do coro alto e os dois órgãos monumentais são um expressivo exemplo do trabalho desenvolvido pelo atelier nortenho setecentista para corresponder às encomendas de uma clientela que procurava conciliar o esplendor e a dignidade da corte com a vida religiosa.
dates: Marceliano de Araújo: século XVIII, início; Miguel Francisco da Silva: século XVIII, início; Frei Simon Fontanes: século XVIII, início; outros desconhecidos.
artist: Cadeiral do Coro Alto: Miguel Francisco da Silva (n.d., Lisboa); caixas dos órgãos: Marceliano de Araújo (n.d., Braga); mestre organeiro: Frei Simon Fontanes (n.d., Galiza); pintura: Manuel Furtado de Mendonça.
keywords: Talha dourada; órgãos.

en.name: Chelaberd (fragment)
description: Although the Chelaberd is clearly a type of rug from the Karabagh region, it is still sometimes referred to today as the so-called Sunburst Kazak - a trade name that alludes to the neighbouring Kazak region. The Dresden fragment is dominated by a massive medallion that fills the field. At the top, facing the head, the base of another medallion can be seen. A narrow-dotted line runs horizontally between the two. In contrast to numerous pieces with three or more medallions, no secondary motifs fill the field, the border here is narrow, and the wool and colours are of outstanding quality. It is a powerful piece, probably made for personal use. It is entirely plausible that this carpet originally had no more than two medallions, although it cannot be said with absolute certainty. In the 1920s, Heinrich Jakoby already pointed out similarities between the characteristic Chelaberd medallion ("sunburst medallion") and medallions on large-format Caucasian workshop carpets of the 18th century. Later on, the design-historical forerunner of the rural-village Chelaberd was identified in it.
holder: Museum für Völkerkunde Dresden (Ethnological Museum Dresden), Dresden State Art Collections
keywords: Fragment
materials: Wool, goat hair; pile weave, symmetrical knot
partner: Dresden State Art Collections, Museum für Völkerkunde Dresden (Ethnological Museum)

en.name: Portrait of emperor Shah Jahan, his three sons, and Asaf Khan
description: In this royal family portrait, Emperor Shah Jahan (r. 1628–58), sitting in haloed profile upon a gold-footed throne under a high white canopy, accepts a jewelled gift from his father-in-law, Asaf Khan. At his right are his three eldest sons—Dara Shikoh (1615–59), Shah Shija (1616–59), and the ill-fated Awrangzeb (r. 1618–1707), whose death effectively marked the end of the great Mughal Empire. All figures are resplendent in turbans decorated with jewels, pearl necklaces, different types of daggers (*khilanum*, *katar*, and *kard*), lavishly embroidered sashes, and gilded swords. An illuminated carpet lies underfoot.
