fr.name: Étalon de poids (mithqal).
description:
Cet étalon de poids (*mithqal*) en verre transparent de couleur verte est fragmenté en trois parties. La face supérieure présente en deux endroits, faiblement estampée, une inscription en caractères coufiques. L'inscription comporte cinq lignes en caractères coufiques, difficilement lisibles à l'œil nu. Toutefois, en recueillant des frottis des deux estampilles, G. Marçais a pu les déchiffrer et les transcrire comme suit : “*î Allah, mimma amara bihi / al amir Abd al-Rahman ben Habib / Masal ben Hammad wali Mila / ichroune ukiya, fi sanat / sabaa wa ichrine wa miaî”* (Au nom de Dieu. Parmi ce qu'a ordonné / le gouverneur Abd al-Rahman ben Habib / à Masal ben Hammad, préfet de Mila / vingt *ukiya*, en l'an / cent vingt-sept).  
  
D'après l'inscription, l'étalon pèse donc vingt *ukiya,* et cette valeur pondérale est validée par une estampille officielle. L'*ukiya* (once) équivaut à 69,338 grammes ; l'étalon pesait donc 1 386,76 grammes.  
  
C'est l'émir qui fixait la valeur pondérale des étalons de poids, et qui l'imposait à la population par l'intermédiaire des *wali* (préfets provinciaux) ; le nom de l'émir est mentionné : il s'agit ici d'Abd al-Rahman ben Habib, petit-fils d'Okba ben Nafi, fondateur de Kairouan. Quant au *wali* Masal ben Hammad, il semble inconnu des chroniqueurs, mais il est vraisemblablement sanhadjien, car son prénom et celui de son père, Hammad, figurent souvent dans les origines sanhadjiennes, en particulier chez les Zirides du Maghreb et d'al-Andalus.  
  
Ces trois fragments de verre constituaient un même ensemble représentant un disque troué au centre. Cet étalon servait d'unité de contrôle des poids utilisés dans les transactions commerciales.

étalon de poids, fragmenté en trois parties, portant une inscription coufique qui précise le poids, vingt *ukiya* ou 1386,76 g, et nomme le préfet responsable devant le wali, également cité, de la fixation du poids de l'étalon. Ces étalons étaient utilisés à des fins de contrôle commercial.

en.name: Uscibene
description:
One of the *sollazzi* intended for the temporary residence of the sovereigns within the great park, also called in ancient documents Xibene, Sirbene, Scibene and built in the 12th century, now rises in the area where the Palace of the Uscibene was erected, a modest agglomeration of the so-called Fondo De Caro, close to the Viale della Regione Siciliana. Leaning on rocky territory, the remains are accessible today from a depression below the level of the later filling-in and completely hidden from the surrounding buildings as well as those standing above. Only the chapel arose from the rocks, above ground level forming part of a faade, as in the more modern suburb.  
A careful survey, carried out by Adolf Goldschmidt in 1898, faithfully reproduces that which still remains today even though full of debris and completely covered over. The palace was probably comprised of several levels: what remains can easily be attributed to the areas of the ground floor of the main building. There is, in fact, part of the palace about 6-m. high, consisting of an *iwan*, which on one side is linked to two large interconnected lateral rooms of which only the perimeter walls remain. On the other side a rectangular space covered by a vault, which is perhaps the *camera dello scirocco*, communicates with an adjoining natural grotto. The *iwan*, which is still visible, consists of a rectangular space covered by a cross vault and with three rectangular niches. The vault of the niche facing the entrance was decorated with *muqarnas* in stone and stucco of which only a few pieces remain in the lower part; the umbrella-shaped vaults of the two lateral niches were covered with stucco and still recognisable. Goldschmidt also reproduces a gap in the end wall under the niche with *muqarnas*, from which there flowed a small stream of water across the space. Assuming, then, that behind the walls a spring rose from the rocks by way of a fountain and ran through the centre of the room in a small stream, from there it passed the main entrance and went on to feed a fishpond (imitating the only existing model of the fishpond of the Zisa).  
Two doors open up on both sides of the *iwan* leading to two square-plan areas covered with a cross vault. The chapel, a simple rectangular form, still retains part of a wooden roof in the form of inverted keel, but has, however, been transformed by the restoration carried out by Francesco Valenti in 1928. Still visible, although in ruins, is the faade and the lateral front moulded and patterned with simple ogival arches *a rincasso*. The inhabitants of the Fondo, proprietors of the monumental remains, have joined together to promote the restoration.

es.name: Uscibene
description:
En el lugar donde se levantaba el palacio de Uscibene, uno de los solaces destinados a residencia temporal de los soberanos en el interior del gran parque, citado también en documentos antiguos como Xibene, Sirbene o Scibene y levantado a mediados del siglo XII, surge hoy el modesto conglomerado urbano del llamado Fondo De Caro, próximo al Viale della Regione Siciliana. Al estar apoyado en un frente rocoso, a sus restos, situados por debajo del nivel de los sucesivos rellenos y totalmente ocultos por los edificios circundantes y más altos, se accede hoy por un declive. Sólo la capilla se alza por encima del nivel de la tierra, como parte del frente de la vía más moderna.  
Un cuidadoso alzado, hecho en 1898 por Adolph Goldschmidt, reproduce fielmente lo que existe aún hoy, si bien lleno de detritus y totalmente cubierto. El palacio tenía, seguramente, varios pisos; lo que queda se puede atribuir fácilmente a las salas de la planta baja del cuerpo principal. De hecho, hay un espacio de unos seis metros de altura formado por un *iwan* unido por un lado a dos amplias salas laterales (de las que sólo quedan los muros del perímetro), por el otro a un ambiente rectangular cubierto con una cúpula (quizá una *habitación del siroco*) que comunica con una gruta natural colindante. El *iwan*, todavía reconocible, está constituido por un ambiente con bóveda de crucería y tres hornacinas rectangulares. La bóveda del nicho que hay enfrente de la entrada está decorada con *mocárabes* de piedra y estuco, y de ellos sólo quedan trazas en la parte inferior; las bóvedas de los dos nichos laterales eran cascarones en forma de concha revestidos de estuco, todavía visibles. Goldschmidt reproduce también una abertura en la pared del fondo, bajo la hornacina de los *mocárabes*, de la que provenía un regato de agua que atravesaba la habitación, por lo que se ha pensado que de las rocas de detrás de la pared brotase un manantial y el agua, a través de una fuente, discurriese hasta el centro de la sala por un canalillo para ir a alimentar, pasada la puerta de entrada, un vivero (tomando como referencia el único modelo existente, el del estanque de la Zisa).  
A ambos lados del *iwan* se abren dos puertas que introducen en sendos espacios de planta cuadrada cubiertos por bóvedas de crucería. La capilla, de sencilla forma rectangular, conserva aún una parte de la cubierta de madera en forma de quilla invertida, pero está, de todos modos, transfigurada por las restauraciones de Francesco Valenti en 1928. Siguen a la vista, aunque muy arruinadas, la fachada principal y la lateral, delineada y pautada esta última por arcos ojivales rehundidos. Los habitantes del Fondo, propietarios de los restos monumentales, se han reunido en consorcio para promover su recuperación.

en.name: San Nilo Abbey, Chapel of the Founder Saints frescoes
description: The rectangular chapel has a marble mosaic floor, a carved wooden ceiling and a Serlian triumphal arch that stands on pairs of columns that divide the room from the sanctuary. The Chapel is surmounted by a small cupola on pendentives where the *Four Evangelists* reside, painted with mock white and gold stuccowork, with the *Eternal Father* in the centre. The iconographic scheme combines the stories of the *Founder Saints*, represented as paintings reproduced in the middle register, with the celebration of the Virgin, the patron saint of the church. The patron is also celebrated: with coats of arms and *fleurs-de-lis*, as well as by allegorical representations of his virtues and reputation, and the patron saints Eustace and Edward, on either side of the altar. All of the decoration is part of a mock architectural chiaroscuro division in perspective, comprising pilaster-strips, cornices, corbels and a long architrave that separates the two sections. The colours chosen are light and pale, with no strong contrasts, such as to highlight the sharp profiles of the architectural structure. The whole, which constitutes a profound reflection on the location, and which makes a feature of the natural light, reveals a considered narrative clarity in which the expressive gestures of the individuals does not adversely affect the spring-like joy of the chromatic range and the almost ingenuous freshness of the story. Furthermore, in an expression of classicism rendered with marked naturalness, it achieves remarkable balance, only apparently easy and spontaneous, between illusionism and abstraction, between the miraculous and the commonplace, and between commemoration and simple storytelling. In this work, Domenico Zampieri is revealed as a genuine exponent of the early 17th-century classicism that was rooted in Bologna. He presents a devotional historical tale, free of rhetoric, in which he tells a sober and austere story that has none of the heroic overtones that characterise paintings from the previous century.

The iconographic scheme of the frescos in the Chapel of the *Founder Saints* – which was probably designed by someone familiar with Basilian traditions – combines the stories of the Founder Saints (Nilus and Bartholomew) with the theme of the *Virgin Mary*, the patron saint of the church.
artist: Commendatory Cardinal Odoardo Farnese (1573, Parma– 1626, Parma)
Domenico Zampieri, known as Domenichino (1581, Bologna – 1641, Naples), in Rome from 1601, pupil of Annibale Carracci
history: Grottaferrata Abbey was founded in 1004 by the Basilian monks Nilus (c. 910–1004) and Bartholomew (981–1055) both of whom were from Rossano Calabro. Built on the foundations of a Roman villa where an apparition of the Virgin Mary had been witnessed, it is the only Byzantine-Greek monastery to have survived around Rome. The chapel beside the nave was reconstructed, re-consecrated and dedicated to the founding fathers by Cardinal Farnese who entrusted the decoration and probably also its architectural design, to the young Domenichino (whom it is known was in Rome from 1601) possibly on the recommendation of his master, Carracci.
keywords: Fresco, religious, decoration
partner: Province of Rome (Città metropolitana di Roma Capitale)

it.name: Abbazia di San Nilo, cappella affrescata con storie dei Santi Fondatori
description: La Cappella, rettangolare, con pavimento di commessi marmorei e soffitto in legno intagliato, presenta un arco trionfale in forma di serliana su coppie di colonne che divide l’aula dall’area del santuario sormontato da una piccola cupola su pennacchi - dove trovano posto i *4 Evangelisti* – dipinta con finti stucchi bianchi e dorati e al centro il *Padre Eterno*. Il programma iconografico coniuga il tema delle storie dei *Santi Fondatori* – rappresentate come quadri riportati nel registro mediano – con la celebrazione della Vergine, patrona della chiesa. Vi è poi anche la celebrazione del committente grazie alla presenza di stemmi e gigli nonché alle rappresentazioni allegoriche delle virtù, della fama e dei suoi santi patroni, Eustachio e Odoardo, ai lati dell’altare. Tutta la decorazione si inserisce in una finta partitura architettonica a chiaroscuro e in prospettiva composta da lesene, cornici, mensole e un lungo architrave che separa i due registri. I colori scelti sono chiari e tenui, senza forti contrasti, così da dare risalto ai nitidi profili della intelaiatura architettonica. L’insieme, che presuppone una riflessione approfondita sul luogo e sulle caratteristiche luminose naturali, dispiega una meditata chiarezza narrativa entro la quale la mimica espressiva dei personaggi non incrina la felicità primaverile della gamma cromatica e la freschezza quasi ingenua del racconto e, in un classicismo declinato con commovente naturalezza, raggiunge un notevole equilibrio, solo apparentemente facile e spontaneo, tra illusionismo ed astrazione, miracolo e quotidianità, memoria celebrativa e semplice racconto. L’artista si mostra in questa opera come un vero esponente della corrente classicista del primo Seicento di derivazione bolognese, mettendo in scena una rappresentazione storica di matrice devozionale, esente da accenti retorici, in un racconto sobrio e austero scevro dai toni eroici che contraddistinguevano la pittura del secolo precedente.

Il programma iconografico degli affreschi della Cappella, probabilmente dettato da un conoscitore delle tradizioni basiliane, intreccia il tema delle storie dei *Santi Fondatori* (Nilo e Bartolomeo) con quello della celebrazione della *Vergine*, patrona della chiesa.
artist: Cardinale commendatario Odoardo Farnese (1573, Parma – 1626, Parma)
Domenico Zampieri detto il Domenichino (1581, Bologna – 1641, Napoli), a Roma dal 1601, allievo di Annibale Carracci
history: L’Abbazia di Grottaferrata, fondata nel 1004 sul luogo della apparizione della Madonna, dai monaci basiliani Nilo (910ca.-1004) e Bartolomeo (981-1055) entrambi di Rossano Calabro, sulle fondamenta di una villa romana, unica di rito greco alle porte di Roma, conserva all’interno, adiacente alla navata della chiesa, una Cappella fatta ricostruire e riconsacrata dedicandola ai padri fondatori dal cardinale Farnese, che affidò al giovane Domenichino, a Roma dal 1601, su suggerimento forse del suo maestro Carracci, la decorazione ma probabilmente anche la stessa architettura dell’ambiente.
keywords: Decorazione a fresco di soggetto religioso
tags: Decorazione a fresco di soggetto religioso
partner: Provincia di Roma (Città metropolitana di Roma Capitale)

en.name: High altar
description: This altar is typically baroque with its elegant curved lines and its open shape, embracing the space. It is a good example of different artistic techniques (sculpture, architectural painting, architecture and figural painting) and of different materials (stucco, painted and gilded wood, fresco, and oil on canvas). It is perfectly in harmony with the space of the church blending the frescoes on the ceiling, the elegant balustrade, the organs and side pillars. This imposing altar frames a fresco fragment of the Virgin with Child, worshipped in the church of Santa Maria di Galliera since the fifteenth-century. The church was completely remodelled in the eighteenth-century and the main altar was rebuilt twice. Giuseppe Maria Mazza built the first version between 1691, when the Filippines fathers inherited a large sum of money in order to refurbish the main chapel, and 1706, when the decoration is mentioned in a guidebook for the first time. This altar, made of stucco, looked like great curtain suspended to the wall and held by two angels and some putti. Before 1739 the decoration was destroyed in order to build a new altar which was designed by Francesco Bibiena. This altar was decorated with two wooden statues of Justice and Peace, carved by the Tuscan Silvestro Giannotti, and two putti, moulded by Angelo Gabriello Piò. The central part of the altar is decorated with a picture by Giuseppe Rolli of angels carrying the medieval Madonna and Child, framed by a rich baroque carving.
artist: Francesco Bibiena, Giuseppe Maria Mazza, Giuseppe Rolli, Angelo Gabriello Piò, Silvestro Giannotti
partner: Musei Civici d’Arte Antica di Bologna in cooperation with the Province of Bologna

it.name: Altar Maggiore
description: Questo altare, con le sue eleganti linee curve e la sua forma aperta, che abbraccia lo spazio, è un tipico esempio di arte barocca. E' anche un ottimo esempio della combinazione di tecniche diverse (scultura, quadratura, architettura e pittura di figura) e di diversi materiali (stucco, legno dorato e dipinto, affresco e olio su tela). L'altare è perfettamente ambientato nella chiesa, in armonia con gli affreschi soprastanti, l'elegante balaustra, gli organi e i pilastri laterali. La struttura incornicia un affresco frammentario raffigurante la *Madonna col Bambino*, venerato in S. Maria di Galliera dal XV sevolo. La chiesa fu interamente ristrutturata nel XVIII secolo e l'altar maggiore fu rifatto due volte.  Giuseppe Maria Mazza realizzò una prima versione tra il  1691, quando i Filippini ereditarono un grossa somma di denaro per ristrutturare la cappella maggiore, e il 1706, quando la decorazione è citata per la prima volta da una guida di Bologna. Questo primo altare, fatto di stucco, era formato da un grande tendaggio appeso al muro, sostenuto da angeli e putti. Prima del  1739 la decorazione fu distrutta per costruire un nuovo altare, progettato da Francesco Bibiena e decorato con due statue di legno raffiguranti la Giustizia e la Pace, scolpite dal toscano Silvestro Giannotti, e due putti, opera di Angelo Gabriello Piò. La parte centrale dell'altare contiene un dipinto di  Giuseppe Rolli  entro una ricca incorniciatura barocca raffigurante  una gloria di angeli che trasportano l'antica Madonna.
artist: Francesco Bibiena, Giuseppe Maria Mazza, Giuseppe Rolli, Angelo Gabriello Piò, Silvestro Giannotti

en.name: *Mosaic from the Christian basilica*
partner: National Museum of Antiquities and Islamic Art

cs.name: Minoritský kostel sv. Janů a Loreta v Brně
description:
Rozlehlý komplex kláštera přiléhal k hradbám města. Na konkávně zvlněném trojosém průčelí jsou sochy patronů kostela sv. Jana Křtitele a sv. Jana Evangelisty (J. K. Pröbstl, J. J. Schauberger), Madony, nad římsou sv. František  
z Assisi a sv. Antonín Paduánský. Sochy sv. Judy Tadeáše a sv. Dismase jsou dílem J. L. Webera. Hlavní oltář jednolodního kostela je přepracováním mauzolea zde pohřbeného Jana Šembery z Boskovic a na Bučovicích, jímž vymřel slavný moravský rod po meči. Oltářní obrazy pochází od malířů vídeňské akademie –  
v Brně usedlého J. Sterna a F. I. Leichera (kolem 1760). Jednotně vybavený interiér dotváří původní varhany (1732).

Klenbu jednolodní stavby otevírá do nebeské sféry monumentální freska. Iluzivní architektura plynule přechází ve skutečné pilastry a štukovou výzdobu. Oltářní obrazy pochází od malířů vídeňské akademie. Pro brněnské publikum byly prvním setkáním s novým malířským stylem, čerpajícím z holandského a vlámského malířství 17. století. Jednotně vybavený interiér dotváří původní varhany (1732). Klášterní knihovna patří mezi nejdochovanější v českých zemích. Pozoruhodná je mysticky působící Loretánská kaple se Svatými schody.
artist: Mořic Grimm (1669 Achdorf – 1757 Brno), Anton Johann Ospel, Jan Christian Pröbstl, Jan Jiří Schauberger (?, před 1725 Vídeň, činný v Olomouci – 1744 Brno), Jan Scherz, Anton Schweigl (1700 Gaiming in Tirol – 1761 Brno), Jan Jiří Etgens (1691–1757, Brno), František Řehoř Ignác Eckstein (1689? Židovice u Žatce – 1741 Lvov), Josef Stern (1716 Štýrský Hradec – 1775 Brno), Felix Ivo Leicher (1727 Bílovec – 1812 Vídeň), Josef Ignác Havelka (1716 Ústí nad Orlicí – 1788 Brno), František Vavřinec Korompay (1723 Rohatec u Strážnice – 1779 Brno), Antonín Richter, Michele Fontana, Michael Ignác Gunst
history: Při barokizaci středověkého a v 16. století upravovaného kláštera byla přistavěna Loreta, sjednoceny fasády a kostel nově zaklenut.
keywords: Loreta, Santa Casa, grisaille

en.name: Minorite Church of Saints John and Loreto, Brno
names: Minorite Church of Saints John and Loreto
description: The vast monastery complex adjoined the town walls. A three-axis, concave frontage features statues of the patron saints of the church, St. John the Baptist and St. John the Evangelist (by J. K. Pröbstl and J. J. Schauberger), the Madonna and, over the ledge, St. Francis of Assisi and St. Anthony of Padua. The statues of St. Thaddeus Jude and St. Dismas are by J. L. Weber. The high altar of the single-nave church is the re-modelled mausoleum of Jan Šembera of Boskovice and Bucovice, who is buried here and whose death marked the end of the male line of a famous Moravian family. The altarpieces are by artists from the Vienna Academy: J. Stern, who settled in Brno, and F. I. Leicher (c. 1760). The uniformly furnished interior is complemented by an original organ (1732).

The vault of this single-nave building opens onto a celestial sphere with a monumental fresco. The illusionary architecture graduates into genuine pilasters and stucco decoration. The altarpieces, by artists from the Vienna Academy, provided for the people of Brno their first encounter with a new painting style that drew on Dutch and Flemish art of the 17th century. The uniformly furnished interior is complemented by an original organ (1732). The monastery library is among the best preserved in the Czech lands. The church highlights include the mystical Loreto Chapel with its Holy Stairs.
artist: Mořic Grimm (1669 Achdorf – 1757 Brno), Anton Johann Ospel, Jan Christian Pröbstl, Jan Jiří Schauberger (? before 1725 Vienna, active in Olomouc – 1744 Brno), Jan Scherz, Anton Schweigl (1700 Gaiming in Tirol – 1761 Brno), Jan Jiří Etgens (1691–1757, Brno), František Řehoř Ignác Eckstein (1689? Židovice u Žatce – 1741 Lviv), Josef Stern (1716 Graz – 1775 Brno), Felix Ivo Leicher (1727 Bílovec – 1812 Vienna), Josef Ignác Havelka (1716 Ústí nad Orlicí – 1788 Brno), František Vavřinec Korompay (1723 Rohatec u Strážnice – 1779 Brno), Antonín Richter, Michele Fontana, Michael Ignác Gunst
history: During the Baroque-period reconstruction of the medieval monastery, rebuilt in the 16th century, the Loreto Chapel was added and the frontages were unified. The church was provided with a new roof.
keywords: Loreto, Santa Casa, grisaille

en.name: City Walls and Gates
description:
Bab al-Jabiya was built by the Atabeg ruler, Nur al-Din Mahmud bin Zangi in 560/1164, re-using Roman stone blocks, and it was completed by the Ayyubid ruler, al-Malik al-Mu‘azzam, in 624/1227. The brackets of the defensive machicolations are visible from the exterior while on the interior is an Arabic inscription set in a tabula ansata (a rectangular frame with triangular edges) recording the patronage of Nur al-Din. The market, which extended out from Bab al-Jabiya, is closely related to the needs and trading activities of pilgrims and travelling merchants as it is considered to be the nearest extension of the pilgrimage route that heads southward to Mecca. Such economic activity oriented towards people passing through, as opposed to the inhabitants of the town, created order and security.  
  
Tower of Nur al-Din is located inside the courtyard of a small workshop/hotel called Funduq al-Islah and it features one of the bestpreserved inscription bands in Arabic, recording Nur al-Din’s refortification efforts of 568/1173.  
  
Bab al-Saghir Cemetery is venerated by all Muslims and it holds many important tombs, including those of the Prophet’s family, his companions and many of the city’s elite throughout the centuries. Some of the oldest existing tombstones date to the 5th/10th and 6th/11th century with distinctive floriated kufic epigraphy, testimony to the attention and restorations given to the cemetery during the Atabeg and Ayyubid period.  
  
It was rebuilt by Nur al-Din in 551/1156 on the foundations of the Roman Gate of Mars. It is the southernmost gate of the city. As the name indicates, its scale is small, more easily defensible, and it is equipped with machicolations.  
  
Bab Kisan is also based on an original Roman gate, dedicated to Saturn, its lower courses of large stone blocks still in place. It was rebuilt during the initial Arab conquests in the 1st/7th century, with remains evident inside the chapel, and again entirely refortified by Nur al-Din in 549/1154. As a city gate, Bab Kisan was again renovated by the Mamluks before it finally became incorporated into the church building.  
  
Bab Sharqi is the oldest extant standing monument in Damascus. It still preserves its original Roman form, attributed to the reign of Augustus (d. AD 14), during which it was called the Gate of the Sun, and mentioned in the Bible as the “Street Called Straight”. Bab Sharqi comprises a triple passageway, a large central arch and two flanking smaller arches. A single gate being more defensible, the two side entrances were blocked up during the Islamic period. The minaret is evidence of Nur al-Din’s reconstructions, as are the extensions of the wall, albeit with smaller stones, the arrow slits and the machicolations.  
  
The Tower of al-Salih Ayyub allocates the north-eastern corner of the city walls. It is part of the final refortification programme of the Ayyubid period under al-Salih Ayyub (d. 646/12478). Traces of the gardens that once bloomed along the northern stretches of the city wall and the Barada river are faintly echoed by the patches of greenery around the tower.  
  
Bab Touma, which was in Roman times the Gate of Venus, stands as a stately double gate, which underwent reconstruction during the Ayyubid period in 624/1227, and Mamluk defensive and decorative additions in 734/1333–4. The exceptionally well-preserved quality of this gate is exemplary. It features a guardroom and arrows slits above the arch, flanked by a pair of box machicolations.  
  
Bab al-Salam, known in the medieval period, Bab Salama – the Gate of Soundness, health and peace – it is one of the most beautiful gates of the city. There is a prominent monumental inscription on the gate’s lintel. This is a 7th-/13th-century Ayyubid reconstruction built by al-Salih Isma‘il, smoothly incorporating Roman blocks and Nur al-Din’s extensions of 561/1171–2. The attractive masonry along the arch of the gate is decorated with a pronounced ablaq motif of alternating limestone and basalt. Arrow-slits and box machicolations protrude around the corner to overlook the bend in the river as well as the communications routes beyond. Its riverside location made it a popular spot for tanneries which required water for the manufacture of leather goods.  
  
Bab al-Faradis, meaning Gate of Paradise, alludes to the once-blossoming district along the banks of the river. The structure dates from Nur al-Din’s period and it was originally constructed as a double gateway, as can be seen by the cross-vaulted ceiling in front of the gate.  
  
Bab al-Faraj, or the Gate of Deliverance, is the only gate that has no Roman precedent but is entirely the work of Nur al-Din, built in 549/1154. Located closest to the citadel, its name indicates the sense of optimism and triumph Nur al-Din was establishing in the city. This gate was also refortified by the Ayyubids and rebuilt again in the 7th/13th century.
keywords: Damascus; city walls; city gates; Bab al-Jabiya; Bab al-Saghir; Bab Kisan; Nur al-Din; Syria
partner: Ministry of Culture, Directorate General of Museums and Antiquities

ar.name: طبق
description: إن الزخرفة المورسكية تغطي كل الجانب الظاهر للطبق في ترتيب ذو تباعد متساوي. ويرى درع تذكاري في الوسط. والطبق الموقّع من قبل نيكولو غريكو ينتمي لنظام الأوعية النحاسية المتنوعة ذات الزخرفة المرتبطة والمنتجة من قبل حرفيي المعادن في منطقة المتوسط من أجل السوق الشرقية والأوربية. والطبق الآخر الموقّع من قبله موجود في مجموعة المتحف البريطاني في لندن (MLA 1855.12-1.3) ونظرا لأننا نعلم القليل جدا عن حياة الفنان – حيث كان يعمل في روما في عام 1542 – فإن التحديد الدقيق لمكان صنع الطبق غير ممكن.
materials: نحاس أصفر مع تزيين بتفنية النيلة
tags: نحاس أصفر مع تزيين بتفنية النيلة
partner: المتحف التمساوي للفنون التطبيقية / الفنون المعاصرة

de.name: Schauteller
description: Der Schauteller von Nicolò Greco steht in der Tradition diverser Messinggefäße mit verwandter Ornamentik, die von Metallhandwerkern des Mittelmeergebietes für den orientalischen und europäischen Markt hergestellt wurden.
holder: MAK – Österreichisches Museum für angewandte Kunst / Gegenwartskunst
partner: MAK – Österreichisches Museum für angewandte Kunst

en.name: Plate
description: The mauresque ornament covers the entire display side of the plate in evenly-spaced arrangement. An armorial shield is seen in the middle. The plate by Nicolò Greco belongs to the tradition of diverse brass receptacles with related ornamentation, produced by metal craftsmen in the Mediterranean region for the Oriental and European market. Another plate signed by him is in the British Museum collection in London (MLA 1855.12-1.3). Since we know very little about the artist’s life— he was working in Rome in 1542 —an exact identification of the plate’s provenance is not possible.
keywords: Plate; Brass; Nicolò Greco
partner: MAK – Austrian Museum of Applied Arts / Contemporary Art

de.name: Nischenteppich
description: Dieser Teppich zählt zu den berühmtesten der Berliner Sammlung. Bereits 1871 wurde er von Wilhelm von Bode für den Maler Heinrich von Angeli erworben, konnte aber erst 1905 von Bode von den Erben angekauft und dem Museum geschenkt werden. Von Angeli und einige seiner Kollegen bildeten diesen Teppich mehrfach ab. Der Teppich besticht durch seine Farbtiefe, den hohen, dichten Flor und den beeindruckenden Glanz der Wolle. Auf dunkelblauem Grund sind durch eine kräftige weiße Line zwei rotgrundige Zwickel nischenförmig abgetrennt. Ungewöhnlich ist, dass die Zwickel oben ineinander übergehen. Das eigentliche Nischenfeld wird in der unteren Hälfte mit einem hellblauen Wolkenband gefüllt in dessen Bogen eine große Blüte einen Fixpunkt bildet. Diese Wolkenband erinnert an Begrenzungen bei den so genannten Schlüsselloch- oder Bellini-Teppichen. Ihre oft eckig geführten Bogenformen werden mit Brunnen assoziiert, die für die rituelle Reinigung benötigt werden. Aufgrund der persisch anmutenden Blüten, des aus dem ostasiatischen Kulturkreis stammenden Wolkenbandes sowie der geschichteten Kette, wurde der Teppich gelegentlich dem persischen Kulturkreis zugeschrieben. Jedoch sprechen sowohl die Farbpalette, die Anlehnung an das Schlüssellochmotiv vor allem aber die Verwendung eines symmetrischen Knotens für einer Verortung in die Türkei.
holder: Museum für Islamische Kunst, Pergamon Museum

en.name: Niche carpet
description: This carpet is among the most famous in the Berlin collection. As early as 1871 it was acquired by Wilhelm von Bode for the painter Heinrich von Angeli, but it was not until 1905 that Bode was able to buy it from his heirs and donate it to the Museum. Von Angeli and some of his colleagues depicted this carpet several times. The charm of this carpet lies in its depth of colour, its high, dense pile and the impressive sheen of the wool. On a dark blue ground, two red-ground spandrels are separated in the form of niches by a strong white line. Unusually, the spandrels blend into each other at their tops. The lower half of the niche field is filled with a light blue cloud band, in whose arc a large blossom forms a fixed point. This cloud band is reminiscent of delimitations in the so-called keyhole or Bellini carpets. Their often angular arch forms are associated with fountains, which were needed for the ritual cleansing before prayer. Because of the Persian appearance of the blossoms, the origin of the cloud band from East Asian cultures, and the use of depressed warps, this carpet has occasionally been ascribed to Persia. However, not only the colour palette and the reference to the keyhole motif, but also the use of a symmetrical knot, speak in favour of a location in Turkey.
holder: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum
keywords: Carpet; Prayer Capet; Niche Carpet; Cloudband; painting; Wilhelm von Bode
materials: Wool; knotted pile carpet, symmetrical knot
partner: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums

en.name: Palazzo Doria Pamphili, frescoes
description:
Following acquisition of the estate, the majestic restructuring of the palace began immediately, and by 1657, the extensive decorative scheme for the rooms on the main floor was in progress. Four large rooms on the south side are known as Fire, Air, Water and Earth on account of the representations in them, and four smaller rooms on the other side contain images of the Four Continents (Africa, America, Asia and Europe) around the larger, rectangular Prince’s room, whose walls show a landscape opening onto a colonnade that supports a balustrade. At the centre of the vault in the Prince’s room the coat of arms of Pamphili Aldobrandini is clearly commemorative.  
Two more rooms intended for religious services display religious subjects. Many painters from different places were involved in the decorative scheme, all inspired by Cortona. First there is the Fire Room, created by Cozza between 1658 and 1659, with a continuous representation of Vulcan’s Forge, entirely free of architectural divisions. Next, the Air Room, the masterpiece of the cycle, painted in just 16 days by Preti in 1661 where the subject is rendered perfectly through the sense of “airiness” that pervades the entire composition, which shows allegories of *Dawn*, *Day*, *Evening* and *Night*. The Water Room, painted between 1658 and 1659 by Cortese, has four side panels and one central panel, divided by monochrome telamons that hold up *trompe-l’oeil* architecture, with mythological subjects related to Water. The similarly laid out Earth Room was painted by Tassi between 1657 and 1659, and is divided by pairs of caryatids with a personification of the Earth at its centre. In the smaller rooms, America and Africa have been attributed to Mola, Asia to Cozza, and Europe to Tassi, while the Prince’s Room was decorated by Dughet and Borgognone between 1658 and 1659.

The decoration consists of four large rooms on the south side of the building known as Fire, Air, Water and Earth on account of the representations in them, and four smaller rooms on the other side with images of the Four Continents (Africa, America, Asia and Europe) around the larger, rectangular Prince’s room. The entirety can be understood to be an extensive decorative scheme inspired by Cortona and intended to celebrate the family in space (the continents) and in time (the elements of human life).
artist: Camillo Pamphili (1622, Naples – 1666, Rome), cardinal and nephew of Pope Innocent X, son of Olimpia Maidalchini, put aside the purple cloth to marry Olimpia Aldobrandini

Guillaume Courtois (Cortese) known as Borgognone (1628–79) of French origin, in Rome around 1640, pupil of Pietro da Cortona; Francesco Cozza (1605–82), from Calabria, in Rome from 1631; Gaspard Dughet (1615–75), of a French father and brother-in-law of Nicolas Poussin, landscape artist who often worked with Courtois; Pier Francesco Mola (1612–66), born in Ticino but in Rome since childhood; Mattia Preti (1613–99), from Calabria, in Rome from the 1630s, active in Valmontone in 1661 just before leaving for Malta, where he died; Giambattista Tassi, the least well-known, between 1657 and 1681
history: The Valmontone estate was acquired by Camillo Pamphili, nephew of Pope Innocent X Pamphili (1644–55), in 1651, with the aim of undertaking a grand restructuring project for the entire village (the Pamphiljan Town) which was to be centred round the palace, the church and the square. The Pamphili family, from a small Umbrian patriciate, had lived in Rome since the 15th century and found recognition of its social ascent in particular with the appointment to the papacy of Giovanni Battista as Innocent X. A series of significant urban development projects, which can be dated to the mid-17th century, still characterise both the city of Rome and the surrounding area: including the palace in Piazza Navona, the palace on the Corso acquired through the marriage of Camillo and Olimpia, the Casino del Bel Respiro in the out-of-town villa San Pancrazio, and the ambitious restructuring program for the village of Valmontone.
keywords: Fresco, allegorical, commemorative, decoration, *trompe-l’oeil*
partner: Province of Rome (Città metropolitana di Roma Capitale)

it.name: Palazzo Doria Pamphili, affreschi
description: Dopo l'acquisto del feudo iniziò subito la ristrutturazione in forme maestose del palazzo e già a partire dal 1657 l'ampio programma decorativo delle sale del piano nobile, che si articolano in quattro grandi sale sul lato meridionale denominate del Fuoco, dell'Aria, dell'Acqua e della Terra in relazione alle raffigurazioni che vi compaiono e in altri quattro camerini più piccoli sull'altro lato con le immagini dei Quattro Continenti - Africa, America, Asia ed Europa – intorno alla più vasta sala del Principe, di forma rettangolare con alle pareti un paesaggio aperto su un colonnato che sorregge una balaustra e al centro della volta lo stemma Pamphili Aldobrandini con chiaro intento celebrativo. Altre due salette poi, destinate a funzioni religiose, ospitano soggetti sacri. Numerosi furono i pittori coinvolti nel programma decorativo, anche di origini diverse, ma tutti per lo più di matrice cortonesca. Per prima si trova la Stanza del Fuoco, realizzata dal Cozza tra il 1658 e il 1659, con la rappresentazione della *Fucina di Vulcano* in forma continua senza partiture architettoniche. Segue la Stanza dell'Aria, capolavoro del ciclo, dipinta in sole 16 giornate dal Preti nel 1661 dove il soggetto è reso perfettamente grazie al senso di "ariosità" che pervade l'intera composizione in cui vengono rappresentati in forma allegorica l'*Aurora*, il *Giorno*, la *Sera* e la *Notte*. La Stanza dell'Acqua, dipinta tra il 1658 e il 1659 dal Cortese presenta invece quattro riquadri laterali e uno centrale, divisi attraverso telamoni a monocromo che sorreggono una finta architettura, con soggetti mitologici legati all'acqua. Di impianto simile la Stanza della Terra dipinta dal Tassi tra il 1657 e il 1659, scompartita attraverso coppie di cariatidi e con al centro la personificazione della Terra. Nei camerini infine l'America e l'Africa sono state attribuite al Mola, l'Asia al Cozza e l'Europa al Tassi mentre il Salone del Principe venne decorato dal Dughet in collaborazione con il Borgognone tra 1658 e 1659.

La decorazione si articola in quattro grandi sale sul lato meridionale del palazzo denominate del Fuoco, dell’Aria, dell’Acqua e della Terra in relazione alle raffigurazioni che vi compaiono e in altri quattro camerini più piccoli sull’altro lato con le immagini dei Quattro Continenti - Africa, America, Asia ed Europa – intorno alla più vasta sala del Principe, di forma rettangolare. Si può considerare l’insieme un ampio programma decorativo di matrice cortonesca teso a celebrare il casato in ordine spaziale (i continenti) e temporale (gli elementi della vita umana).
artist: Camillo Pamphili (1622, Napoli - 1666, Roma), cardinal nipote di Innocenzo X, figlio di Olimpia Maidalchini, abbandonò la porpora per sposare Olimpia Aldobrandini

Guillaume Courtois (Cortese) detto il Borgognone (1628-79) di origine francese, a Roma intorno al 1640, allievo di Pietro da Cortona; Francesco Cozza (1605-82), calabrese, a Roma dal 1631; Gaspard Dughet (1615-75), di padre francese e cognato di Nicolas Poussin, paesaggista spesso attivo insieme al Courtois; Pier Francesco Mola (1612-66), di origine ticinese ma a Roma già da bambino; Mattia Preti (1613-99), calabrese, a Roma dagli anni ’30, attivo a Valmontone nel 1661 subito prima di partire per Malta, dove morì; Giambattista Tassi, il meno noto, di cui si hanno notizie tra il 1657 e il 1681.
history: Il feudo di Valmontone fu acquistato da Camillo Pamphili, nipote di Innocenzo X Pamphili (1644-55), nel 1651, con l’intento di realizzare un grandioso progetto di ristrutturazione dell’intero borgo – la città panfilia – che doveva trovare il suo fulcro proprio nel nodo costituito dal palazzo, dalla chiesa e dalla piazza. La famiglia dei Pamphili, proveniente dal piccolo patriziato umbro e trasferitasi a Roma fin dal ‘400, trovò il riconoscimento della sua ascesa sociale soprattutto in concomitanza con la nomina al papato di Giovanni Battista con il nome di Innocenzo X. Alla metà del ‘600 si possono infatti ricondurre una serie di interventi urbanistici di rilievo che ancora oggi connotano sia la città di Roma sia il territorio: dal palazzo in Piazza Navona, a quello sul Corso acquisito grazie al matrimonio di Camillo con Olimpia Aldobrandini, al Casino del Bel Respiro  nella Villa fuori porta San Pancrazio, fino appunto all’ambizioso programma di ristrutturazione del borgo di Valmontone.
keywords: Affresco; decorazione allegorica celebrativa
partner: Provincia di Roma (Città metropolitana di Roma Capitale)

ar.name: آخر خليفة عباسي المسعتصم (حكم خلال 42-1589 )
description: هذه الصفحة مع اثنتين أخريين في مجموعة متحف الآغا خان (AKM41 و AKM40) أتت من مخطوطة مجمعة في بلاط شهروخ (توفي عام 1447) وتم تفريقها من قبل تاجر قطع فنية هي إميلي طباخ في 1920 و 1930 ومحتوى المخطوطة بشكل أساسي هو من تاريخ العالم الموضوع من قبل رشيد الدين (توفي عام 1318) من أجل الحاكم المغولي إلخان أولجيتو في عام 1307 . وهي ليست ببساطة نسخة من عمل رشيد الدين ولكنها مخطوطة هجينة ذات تاريخ  متشابك حيث جرى تعقيده أكثر بسبب تناثرها وهذه الصفحة أتت من مجموعة من الصفحات التي حضِّرت تحت إشراف رشيد الدين ولاحقا تم تضمينها في المخطوطة التيمورية.

en.name: The last of the Abbasid Caliphs, Mustaʿsim (r. 1242–58)
description: This folio, along with two others in the Aga Khan Museum Collection (AKM40 and AKM41), comes from a manuscript assembled at the court of Shahrukh (d. 1447) and disassembled by the art dealer Émile Tabbagh in the 1920s and 30s. The manuscript’s content draws primarily from a world history prepared by Rashid al-Din (d. 1318) for the Mongol Ilkhan Oljeitu in 1307. It is not a simple copy of Rashid al-Din’s work, but rather a hybrid manuscript with a tangled history made even more complex by its dispersal. This folio is one of a group of folios that were originally prepared under Rashid al-Din’s own supervision and later incorporated into the Timurid manuscript.
keywords: Folio; work-on-paper; works-on-paper
materials: Ink, watercolour, and gold pigment on paper
tags: Ink, watercolour, and gold pigment on paper

en.name: Tekke panel
short_description: *Hüsn-i Hat* is a type of calligraphy. Turks probably started to get interested in calligraphy after their arrival to Anatolia. The brightest period was during the Ottoman era. Calligraphy developed well beyond its functional role; it almost played a similar role to the paintings in Western art in terms of the level of its aesthetics. The script *"Ya Hazreti Şeyh Sultan Yusuf Sümbül Sinan Kaddes Allahu sırrahu"* (religious text, untranslatable) is written on a black background with *Zerendud* (gilded) calligraphy and designed as the *sikke* (tall felt hat) of the Sünbüli order. It stands over a small table in Rococo style and there are hyacinth flowers on either corner of the upper part. The sides of the plate are surrounded by two borders that are Rococo in design.
holder: Vehbi Koç Foundation Sadberk Hanim Museum
keywords: Caligraphy; Hüsn-i Hat; plate
partner: Vehbi Koç Foundation Sadberk Hanim Museum

en.name: *The Citadel of Cairo, the Residence of the Pasha*
short_description: The citadel of Cairo, here captured by the Scottish artist David Roberts in the 1830s, was undergoing major changes under Muhammad Ali Pasha (1769-1849). Having overcome the Mamluks of Egypt in 1805, Muhammad Ali erased all traces of their rule, including remaining palace and administrative structures. He rebuilt most of the walls, erected four new palaces - his own royal residence in the northern enclosure, a courthouse, an expansive terrace and state-of-the-art accomodation for his army. At the heart of the citadel complex, Mohammad Pasha ordered a memorial mosque for his son Tusun in the Ottoman style. Building work on the mosque lasted from 1828 to 1848. Roberts incorporates the new structures existing in his time, like the palace on the right, cresting the hill - the ongoing building works on the mosque are concealed by the Mamluk structure in the foreground on the right.
holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department
keywords: Muhammad Ali Pasha

en.name: Palais Kasr el-Said
short_description: This palace is an excellent example of a typical beylical palace, with an architecture, décor and furnishings that show distinct signs of European, and particularly Italian, influences. The large, tall building is surrounded by trees and orchards. The grand staircase, the marble columns, the marble, ceramic and faience mosaics on the walls, the Italian-style window frames and the Andalusian-style carved stucco all contribute to the decorations' opulent and varied quality, which characterised the 18th and 19th centuries.
history: Located near the Bardo palaces, this palace had belonged to a noble of the Husainid court until 1867. It was then subject to a series of adjustments and expansions under the reign of Sadok Pacha Bey, who took up residence there once the works were completed. It was in this palace that, on 12 May 1881, Sadok Pacha Bey added his signature to the treaty which would impose a French Protectorate on his country, headed by General Bréart. The building was restored and taken over by l'Institut National du Patrimonie in 1988, and now houses the first landmarks of the Musée d'Histoire de la Tunisie Moderne et Contemporaine, whilst also preserving its Husainid foundations. It also holds many historically valuable paintings, thrones and coaches which had belonged to the bey.
keywords: Architecture; art; painting; stucco; mosaic; marble; ceramics
partner: Higher Institute for the Study of Contemporary History of Tunisia, University of Manouba

fr.name: Palais Kasser-Saïd
short_description: Exemple imposant de palais beylical, profondément marqué par les influences européennes et notamment italiennes tant au niveau de l’architecture que du décor et du mobilier. Entouré de jardins et de vergers, il s’agit d’une vaste et haute construction. Escalier d’honneur, colonnes et chapiteaux en marbre, revêtements muraux en mosaïque de marbre, céramique et faïence, encadrements de fenêtres italianisants, stucs de tradition andalouse… tout contribue à la somptuosité de ce décor composite qui s’est généralisé aux XVIIIe et XIXe siècles.
history: Situé à proximité des palais du Bardo, il a appartenu jusqu’en 1867 à un haut dignitaire de la cour des beys husseinites. Le palais subit d’importants travaux de transformation et d’agrandissement sous le règne de Sadok Pacha Bey qui l’habita ensuite. Et c’est dans ce palais que, le 12 mai 1881, Sadok Pacha Bey apposa sa signature au bas du traité que lui imposa le général Bréart établissant officiellement le protectorat français en Tunisie. Depuis 1988, restauré, le palais a été affecté à l’Institut national du Patrimoine. Il abrite les premiers jalons du Musée d’Histoire de la Tunisie moderne et contemporaine conservant le fonds beylical husseinite, dont, notamment, des peintures historiques, les trônes et les carrosses beylicaux.
keywords: Architecture; Art; Peinture; Stuc; Mosaïque; Marbre; Céramique
partner: Institut Supérieur d’histoire contemporaine de la Tunisie, Université de la Manouba

en.name: Monumental staircase
description: Commissioned by Earl Vincenzo Bargellini, the monumental staircase was realised by the architect Alfonso Torreggiani in 1730. The project represents the synthesis resulting from the combination of the designs suggested by various architects contacted by the Earl. Besides Torreggiani, one can see the hints of the work of Carlo Francesco Dotti and Antonio Conti, whose drawings are still preserved. The plastic decorations are the work of Giuseppe Borelli a member of an important Swiss family of stucco decorators, working in Bologna for many noble families. The staircase was recently restored.
partner: Musei Civici d’Arte Antica di Bologna in cooperation with the Province of Bologna

it.name: Scalone monumentale
description: Commissionato dal conte Vincenzo Bargellini, lo scalone monumentale, restaurato di recente, fu realizzato dall'architetto  Alfonso Torreggiani nel 1730. Il progetto è la sintesi delle due soluzioni proposte dagli architetti contattati dal conte oltre a Torreggiani, cioè Carlo Francesco Dotti e Antonio Conti, di cui si conservano ancora I disegni. Le decorazioni scolpite sono opera di Giuseppe Borelli, membro di una importante famiglia di stuccatori svizzeri che lavorarono a Bologanper numerose famiglie nobili.

ar.name: سجادة صلاة مزخرفة بصف من المحاريب.
description:
القطعة عبارة عن جزء من واحدة من ثلاث سجادات في مجموعة متحف الفنون التركية والإسلامية ما زالت باقية منذ القرن 9 / 15 حتى يومنا هذا. صمِّمت السجادة على شكل محاريب توفِّر مساحات محددة للمصلين كي يصلوا في المسجد في صفوف واضحة التحديد. لم يبقَ من السجادة سوى هذه القطعة، وبالتالي فإن أبعادها الأصلية الكاملة غير معروفة. أرضية القطعة من اللون الأصفر الشاحب. ويوجد ضمن الأقسام المؤطَّرة بحواشٍ زرقاء داكنة خمسة محاريب، اثنان منها باللون الأخضر وثلاثة باللون الأزرق الداكن. يمكن أن نلحظ في تصميم محاريب السجادة تأثير نمط الحواشي ذات الخط الكوفي البارز المستخدم في السجاد القوني خلال عهد سلاجقة الأناضول في القرن 9 / 13. تمَّ تتويج كل محراب بشكل مبسَّط لرأس كبش، بينما اتخذت الأطراف شكل زوايا أُلحقت بها رسوم زرقاء داكنة أشبه برقعة الشطرنج تتدلى منها "هوابط" حمر. كما يتدلى من كل محراب ثلاثة قناديل مسجد، واحد في الوسط واثنان على الجانبين. ويوجد تصاميم على شكل مُعيّنات في القسم السفلي لأربعة محاريب؛ زيّنت هذه المعيّنات بأسهم تشير إلى أربعة اتجاهات. أما المحراب المركزي فيحتوي قسمه السفلي على مُعيَّن غير مزين ربما قصِد به إبراز مركز سجادة الصلاة ذات التصميم المتماثل.  
  
إن الشكل الملوَّن بالأزرق المرسوم على خلفية حمراء الذي يوحي برأس كبش مزدوج يشكل الحاشية الرئيسية، واستُخدم في الوقت نفسه لفصل صفوف السجادة عن بعضها بعضاً. أما الأشكال الموزعة على الحواف ذات الأرضية الصفراء الضيقة التي تحيط بالحاشية الرئيسية فهي أشبه بسلسلة مضفرة من وريدات صفراء وزرقاء. كما أن الأنماط الهندسية تحاكي الأسلوب السلجوقي، خصوصاً زواياها ذات الرؤوس السهميّة المشابهة للكتابة الكوفية. هذه الأنماط، إضافة إلى أشكال النجوم ثمانية الرؤوس وقناديل المسجد، تمهِّد الطريق للانتقال إلى الأسلوب العثماني في صناعة سجاد الصلاة.

أقدم بُسُط الصلاة العثمانية، ذوات المحاريب المُتعدِّدة، تعود إلى القرن التاسع الهجري/ الخامس عشر الميلادي. كان يتمُّ إنتاجها للاستخدام في المسجد، لمساعدة المُصلِّين على الاصطفاف في خطوط مستقيمة. إن بُسُط (سجاجيد) الصلاة العائدة لهذه الفترة تُشكِّل، بتصاميمها التشكيلية الهندسية، وحواشيها النقشية الكوفية، نقلة إلى سجاجيد الصلاة العثمانية الكلاسيكية.
keywords: حبكة تركية مزدوجة؛ جيردس؛ سجادة؛ سجادة صلاة؛ سيفريهيسار؛ شيخ يوسف بابا.
materials: صوف مركَّب منسوج بواسطة الحبكة التركية المزدوجة، وتعرف بحبكة جيردس.

en.name: Prayer rug with a row of niches.
description:
This is one of three 'row' carpets of an early date in the collection of the Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts which have survived from the 9th / 15th century to the present day. The composition has been organised into *mihrab* niches which provide a distinct space for worshippers in the mosque to pray in well-defined rows. It has survived as a fragment; the original dimensions of the complete rug are not known. The ground is white (cream). Within the sections outlined by dark-blue borders are five *mihrab* niches, two of them green and three dark-blue. The influence of the monumental *kufic* borders of AH 7th- / AD 13th-century Konya rugs of the Anatolian Seljuq period can be seen in the design of the rug's *mihrab*s. Each of the *mihrab* niches are crowned with a stylised ram's-head motif, while their corners have corner-pieces with dark-blue chequer patterns and red 'stalactites' hanging off them. In each *mihrab* there are three mosque-lamp motifs, one in the centre and two at the sides, hanging downwards. Four of the *mihrab* niches have diamond-motifs in their lower section, ornamented with motifs like arrowheads pointing in four directions. In contrast, the central niche has a diamond-motif in its lower section which is plain, as if the element of symmetry is meant to show the centre of the prayer rug.  
  
The pattern reminiscent of a double ram's-head in blue on a red ground, while it makes up the main border, is at the same time used to separate the rows from each other.  
  
The motifs on the narrow yellow-ground border which surrounds the main border resemble a chain of plaited yellow and blue rosettes. The geometric motifs carry on Seljuq tradition, especially their arrowhead-like corners which resemble *kufic* script. These, as well as the mosque-lamp and eight-pointed star motifs, prepare the way for the transition to Ottoman prayer rugs.

The earliest Ottoman prayer rugs with multiple niches are dated to the AH 9th / AD 15th century. They were produced for use in the mosque to help the congregation to pray in straight lines. The prayer rugs (*seccade*) of this period with their geometric compositions and *kufic* borders are a transition to classical Ottoman prayer rugs.
holder: Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts.
keywords: Prayer rug; rug; Sivrihisar; Gördes; Sheikh Yusuf Baba
materials: Wool on wool, woven with the Turkish double knot also known as the Gördes knot.
tags: Wool on wool, woven with the Turkish double knot also known as the Gördes knot.
partner: Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts

es.name: Alfombra de oración con hilera de *mihrab*.
description:
Esta es una de las tres alfombras de “hileras” del siglo IX / XV que se conservan en la colección del Museo de Arte Turco e Islámico. La composición está dispuesta en recuadros, que evocan nichos del *mihrab*y que ofrecen un espacio delimitado para que los fieles oren ordenadamente en las mezquitas. Sólo se ha conservado un fragmento de la alfombra, por lo que se desconocen sus medidas originales. El fondo es de color crema. En el interior de los recuadros, delimitados por bordes en azul oscuro, hay imágenes de cinco *mihrab*, dos verdes y tres azul oscuro. La influencia de los bordes cúficos monumentales de las alfombras de Konya del siglo VII / XIII durante el periodo selyuqí de Anatolia resulta evidente en el diseño de los *mihrab*. Los nichos están coronados con una cabeza de carnero estilizada; los ángulos están adornados con esquineras a cuadros azul oscuro y estalactitas rojas. Dentro de cada *mihrab* hay, además, tres lámparas de mezquita colgantes, una central y dos laterales. Cuatro de los nichos tienen rombos en la parte inferior, adornados con puntas de flecha que señalan en cuatro direcciones. El nicho central, sin embargo, presenta en la parte inferior un rombo exento de adornos, lo que quizá indique que era el centro de la alfombra.  
La figura que evoca una doble cabeza de carnero de color azul sobre fondo rojo cumple una doble función: constituye el borde superior y, al mismo tiempo, separa unas filas de otras. Los motivos que se aprecian en el borde estrecho de fondo amarillo que rodea el borde principal de los *mihrab* componen una cadena de florones trenzados, de color amarillo y azul. Los motivos geométricos están inspirados en la tradición selyuqí, especialmente los ángulos en punta de flecha, que recuerdan la escritura cúfica. Estos motivos, al igual que las lámparas de mezquita y las estrellas de ocho puntas, anuncian la transición hacia las alfombras de oración otomanas.

Las primeras alfombras de oración otomanas con varios nichos datan del siglo IX / XV. Servían para que los fieles orasen en hileras en las mezquitas. Las alfombras de oración *(seccade)* de este periodo, con adornos geométricos y bordes cúficos, son la transición hacia las alfombras otomanas clásicas.

fr.name: Tapis de prière avec une rangée de niches.
description:
L'un des trois tapis à “rangs” du IXe siècle H (XVe siècle J.-C.) figurant dans la collection du musée. Le tapis nous étant parvenu sous forme de fragment, les dimensions de la pièce d'origine sont inconnues. Sa composition fait appel à un motif de niches de *mihrab* qui délimitent les emplacements pour prier en rangées alignées. Sur un fond rectangulaire crème se détachent cinq niches de *mihrab* à bordures bleu foncé, deux vertes et trois bleu foncé. L'influence des bordures monumentales en pseudo-coufique des tapis de Konya du VIIe siècle H (XIIIe siècle J.-C.) de la période des Seldjoukides d'Anatolie est notable dans le dessin des *mihrab*. Chaque niche est couronnée d'une tête de cerf stylisée et ses angles sont ornés de triangles à motif de damier bleu foncé d'où pendent des stalactites. Dans le champ intérieur figurent trois lampes de mosquée suspendues, une centrale, deux latérales. Quatre des niches présentent en partie inférieure des motifs en diamant d'où partent des pointes de flèches dans les quatre directions. Celle du centre ne comporte qu'un unique motif en diamant, comme pour marquer le centre du tapis.  
Le motif en bleu sur fond rouge qui évoque une double tête de cerf de la bordure principale sert en même temps à isoler les niches l'une de l'autre. Les motifs de la bordure étroite à fond jaune qui entoure la bordure principale évoquent une chaîne de rosettes jaunes et bleues tressées. Les motifs géométriques sont inspirés de la tradition seldjoukide, en particulier les angles en pointe de flèche, motif qui rappelle l'écriture coufique. Comme les lampes de mosquée et les étoiles à huit branches, ils annoncent la transition vers le tapis de prière ottoman.

Les plus anciens tapis de prière ottomans à niches multiples sont datés du IXe siècle H (XVe siècle J.-C.). Ils étaient destinés aux mosquées pour aider les fidèles à prier alignés. Les compositions géométriques et les bordures en coufique des tapis de prière de cette période font la transition avec le tapis de prière de style classique ottoman.
holder: Musée des arts turcs et islamiques.
dates: IXe siècle de l’Hégire (XVe siècle J.-C.).

tr.name: Saf Seccade.
description:
Türk ve İslam Eserleri Müzesi koleksiyonunda 9. / 15. yüzyıldan günümüze ulaşabilen erken tarihli üç saf seccadeden biridir. Camilerde Müslümanların düzgün birer saf halinde namaz kılabilmesi için her kişiye ayrı bir alan yaratan mihrap nişleri halinde düzenlenmiştir. Asıl boyutları bilinmeyen seccade günümüze fragman halinde ulaşmıştır. Seccadenin zemini beyaz (krem) renklidir. Lacivert renkli bordürlerin çevrelediği bölümler içinde ikisi yeşil, üçü koyu mavi toplam beş mihrap nişi yer alır. Seccadenin mihrap tasarımında 7. / 13. yüzyıla tarihlenen Anadolu Selçuklu Dönemi Konya halılarının kufi desenli anıtsal bordürlerinin etkisi görülür. Mihrap nişlerinin alınlığına birer stilize koçbaşı motifi ile mihrap köşeliklerine içleri lacivert damalı kırmızı sarkıtlı köşebentler yerleştirilmiştir. Her bir mihrapta biri ortada, ikisi yanlarda olmak üzere aşağı doğru sarkıtılmış üç kandil motifi yer alır. Mihrap nişlerinin dört tanesinin alt bölümünde yer alan baklava motifleri, dört tarafa yönelmiş ok ucuna benzer motiflerle bezelidir. Buna karşılık orta nişin alt bölümünde yer alan baklava motifi, adeta seccadenin merkezini belirleyen simetri unsuru olarak yalın halde verilmiştir.  
  
Kırmızı zemin üzerinde mavi renkte dizilmiş çifte koçbaşını andıran desen ana bordürü oluştururken, aynı zamanda safları birbirinden ayırıcı özelliktedir.  
  
Ana bordürü çevreleyen sarı zeminli ince bordür üzerindeki motifler sarı ve mavi renkli rozetlerden oluşan bir zincir örgüsü görünümündedir. Selçuklu geleneğini devam ettiren özellikle kufi yazı karakterindeki ok ucuna benzer geometrik köşeli motifler, kandiller sekiz köşeli yıldız motifleri daha sonraki Osmanlı seccadelerine geçişi hazırlamıştır.

Osmanlı sanatında bilinen en erken tarihli saf seccadeler, 9. / 15. yüzyıla tarihlenmektedir. Camide namaz kılan cemaatin düzgün bir saf oluşturması amacıyla üretilmişlerdir. Bu dönem seccadeleri, geometrik kompozisyonları ve kufi hatlı bordürleriyle klasik Osmanlı seccadelerine geçişi sağlamışlardır.
keywords: Gördes; saf seccade; seccade; Şeyh Yusuf Baba; Sivrihisar

en.name: Dish with Foliated Rim and Design of Cypress Tree with Flowering Plants
description: An Iznik dish of glazed white ground ceramic has a scalloped edge and a broad rim with stylized rock and wave pattern decoration; cloud-shaped areas of white glaze alternate with clusters of royal blue glaze circles filled with thin, dark spiral designs. There are also evenly-spaced wing-like decorations in turquoise glaze. The main ground of the bowl is glazed with a "cypress tree" motif. A tall, vertical cypress in gray-green glaze is surrounded by winding leafy stems bearing dark blue blossoms, rust-collared carnations, and long sprays of blue blossoms. The exterior of the dish, also in white glaze, is decorated with alternating pairs of blue tulips and blue rosettes with turquoise centers.
dates: Hegira Mid 10th to early 11th century / AD second half 16th century

en.name: Dish
description:
A few types of the AD 17th century Persian ceramic ware, painted in a free expressive style and covered with cracks, were traditionally known as “*Kubachi*” ceramics. This conventional name came from a village in Daghestan, where in the 19th century huge amounts of Iranian Safavid pottery were concentrated. However, the Iranian production centres of "*Kubachi*" wares are still to be defined.  
Ceramic ware painted in black under transparent turquoise glaze belongs to a distinctive and possibly the earliest type of the “*Kubachi*” group. Turquoise has a special benevolent semantics in Persian culture due of the homonymy of Persian words *firuza* – turquoise (gemstone) and *firuzi* - victory, prosperity.  
The decorative idea of the combination of black and turquoise originated in Iranian pottery in the late 12th century. The Timurid black-on-turquoise ware of the 15th century was the development of the tradition. In the 17th century, the style of black painting became noticeably lighter and freer. The very movement of the artist’s hand revealed the experience of a calligrapher.
keywords: Ceramics; stonepaste; Iran; Safavid
materials: Stonepaste; painted with black under a transparent turquoise glaze
tags: painted with black under a transparent turquoise glaze
partner: The Bohdan and Varvara Khanenko National Museum of Arts

en.name: A 'Lotto' rug probably Ushak
description: A particular group of the endless repeat patterned early Ottoman pieces is represented by the “Lotto” carpets, named after an Italian painter Lorenzo Lotto (1480–1557). The "Lotto" design was a development of the "small pattern Holbein" design, opening it up to become an overall pattern. The design possibly developed from the much earlier Turkish tradition of two-tone overall lattice carpets, such as those of the thirteenth and fourteenth centuries. The largest examples with this border design tend to have complete cartouches in the border while the medium sized and smaller examples have the part-cartouches, as seen here. Ch. G. Ellis distinguishes three main trends of the "Lotto" pattern: 'Anatolian', 'Kilim' and 'Ornamented'. This "Lotto" carpet was in the property of a noble Italian family.
place: West Anatolia, Turkey; Possibly received as a diplomatic gift by Pope Alexander VII and then by descent
materials: Weaving, Sewing, Stitching on wool and cotton

en.name: Revolver
description:
According to the engraving on the barrel, this revolver was manufactured by J. Nikittis Erben in Constantinople. Erben was a revolver-maker and retailer who sold Colt firearms. Another engraving also reads ""POUCARTOUCHE NAGANT"". The serial number was engraved on the left side of the revolver right under the cylinder. Only the last two digits (76) can be seen. The revolver is fitted with wooden grips and fixed to the frame by a screw. This  
revolver is similar to the Swiss revolver of 1882, but not identical. It might be a variation of that revolver.

description: إن سجادة سيمونيتي سميت كذلك بسبب مالكها الإيطالي في القرن العشرين والتي حيكت في القاهرة حوالي نهاية الحكم المملوكي أو بعد وقت قصير من غزو العثمانيين للمدينة في 1517 . وهي تستخدم صبغات المستمدة من الحشرات ذات اللون الأحمر والأزرق والأخضر والأصفر مع قليل أو بدون طبقة بيضاء غير مصبوغة  بواسطة الصوف المحاك بشكل حرف إس s-spun wool والذي نادرا ما يوجد خارج مصر ويشير للإنتاج المملوكي بالرغم من أن التاريخ الدقيق للإنتاج مجهول . وإن تصميم الحجرات الخمس يجعل هذه السجادة الأكبر من نوعها وهي معروفة بالتأثيرات المرئية المبهرة المنتجة مثل الشدات اللونية للجواهر والأشكال الهندسية والتصاميم المتألقة والسجاد المملوكي يحمل صور مثل الزهور ثلاثية البتلات وأشجار السرو ونباتات البردي التي تشبه المظلات الصغيرة . والسجادات مثل هذه ذات قيمة كبيرة في التجارة المتوسطية وتظهر في لوحات فينيسية منذ أوائل القرن السادس عشر.

en.name: The 'Simonetti' Carpet
description: The Simonetti Carpet, so named for its twentieth century Italian owner, was woven in Cairo toward the end of Mamluk rule or shortly after the city’s Ottoman conquest in 1517. The use of insect-derived red, blue, green, and yellow dyes with little or no undyed white, together with the s-spun wool, rarely found outside of Egypt, points to Mamluk production, although the precise date of production is not known. The five compartment design makes this carpet one of the largest of its type. Known for dazzling visual effects produced by jewel-like tones, geometric forms and radiating designs, Mamluk carpets bear motifs such as three-petalled flowers, cypress trees and papyrus plants that resemble tiny umbrellas. Carpets like this one figured significantly in Mediterranean commerce and appear in Venetian paintings as early as the sixteenth century.
keywords: Mamluk; Cairo; Egypt; wool; furnishing; geometric design; geometric decoration; geometric patterns; medallion; textile
materials: Wool (warp, weft, and pile); asymmetrically knotted pile

ar.name: صحن يصور طائرين بين نباتات مزهرة
description: هذا النوع من الفخار المطلي تحت الزجاج انتج في إزنيق وهي مركز مهم لإنتاج الخزف العثماني . والنوع الروماني Rhodian (أصله من جزيرة رودس ) يشكل المرحلة الثالثة والأخيرة من خزف إزنيق والتي دامت تقريبا من 1570 إلى 1700 وهذه القطع تتميز باستخدام شمع الختم المضاف بشكل ثخين على الزجاج الأحمر الذي يجسد بشكل نافر والطبق يتميز بطائرين يستندان على نباتات  تتمايل بشكل رفيق والتي تحمل القرنفل ، التوليب ، والمكحلة الحدقية وبالرغم من أن شكل النباتات المزهرة متمسك به في فخار إزنيق في القرنين السادس عشر والسابع عشر  فإن صور الطيور والحيوانات نادرة ونموذج الموجة والصخرة التقليدي بشكل كبير يحيط بورقة الحدود لهذا الطبق فإن مثل هذه التصاميم التي استلهمت من خزف مينج في القرن الخامس عشر هي أكثر شيوعا في هذه المرحلة من إنتاج إزنيق.

en.name: Dish depicting two birds among flowering plants
description: This type of underglaze-painted pottery was produced in Iznik, an important centre of Ottoman ceramic production. The Rhodian type constitutes the third and final phase of Iznik ceramics, lasting from c. 1570 to 1700. These objects are characterized by the use of a thickly applied "sealing-wax" red glaze that stands out in relief. This plate features two birds resting on gently swaying plants bearing carnations, tulips, and hyacinths. Although the motif of flowering plants is pervasive in Iznik pottery of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, depictions of birds and animals are rare. A highly conventionalized wave-and-rock pattern circumscribes the broad foliate rim of this plate. Such designs, which were inspired by fifteenth-century Chinese Ming ceramics, enjoyed much popularity in this phase of Iznik production.

ar.name: نرجيلة (قليان)
description: الجسم الخزفي ذو الفتحتين يذكر بشكل ما يعرف بالكندي (وهي أوعية سكب صينية ذات عنق طويل و مسكبة) وكانت تصدّر منذ بداية عصر مينج (1368-1644)والتي كانت تقلد لفترة قصيرة من قبل صناع الفخار الفرس. وربما في القرن التاسع عشر كان الكندي يزود بقاعدة فضية و يحول إلى نرجيلة (باللغة الفارسية : قليان) وبالتالي يجعل فحصها الكامل مستحيلا. ولكن المناطق المرئية تعطي معلومات ذات صلة التي تسمح بتحديد الطراز الدقيق والمقارنة الموضوعية مع أمثلة مشابهة. والتزيين تحت الزجاج من الطراز الصيني المطلي بظلين من اللون الأزرق ومؤطر بالأسود موضوع في خمس حجرات ،أربعة منها تحتوي حيوانات وطيور مقابل خلفية من النباتات الخصبة. و العلامة من الطراز الصيني على القاعدة تذّكر بالعلامات الأخرى على الكندي الفارسي.
dates: النصف الأول من القرن 11 الهجري /النصف الأول من القرن 17 الميلادي(الجسم الخزفي) ، القرن 13 هجري /القرن 19 ميلادي(؟)(قاعدة فضية)

en.name: Water pipe (*qalyan*)
description: The ceramic body, with two openings, recalls the shape of the so-called *kendis* (Chinese pouring vessels with a long neck and a spout), exported ever since the beginning of the Ming dynasty (1368-1644), and which were briefly copied by Persian potters. It was probably in the nineteenth century that this *kendi* was fitted with a silver mount and turned into a water pipe (Pers. *qalyan*), thus making its thorough examination impossible. However, the visible areas provide relevant information which allows for a pertinent stylistic assessment and a meaningful comparison with similar examples. The Chinese-style underglaze decoration, painted in two shades of blue and outlined in black, is placed in five compartments, four of which feature animals and birds against a lush vegetal background. The Chinese-type mark painted on the base is reminiscent of other marks used on Persian *kendis*.
holder: The National Museum of Art of Romania
dates: Hegira first half of the 11th century / AD first half of the 17th century (ceramic body); Hegira 13th century / AD 19th century (?) (silver mount)
keywords: Qalyan
materials: Fritware, underglaze painting; silver mount, engraved, openwork decoration
partner: National Museum of Art of Romania

en.name: *Bayt al-Barudi steamship murals, Damascus*
names: Mural in the main reception hall of the Barudi House at the quarter of Qanawat
short_description: The steamships are of one of the most important technical innovations in the nineteenth-century, because they introduced new modern possibilities of transport and trade and hence contributed to the economic transformation of the Ottoman Empire. Because of this new transportation, cities on the Euphrates or Tigris experienced drastic changes and flourished even more. This impact lead to numerous depictions of steamships in artwork, such as this mural from Bayt al-Qabbani (Damascus, built at the turn of the 19th/20th century) shows. As symbols of the new time they represent global exchange of goods, ideas and people.
holder: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums
partner: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums

en.name: Spouted bowl (*sahlah bu mirzab*)
description: Bowls are among the most important copper artifacts in Omani hospitality. They are usually either wholly circular or circular with a channel and include various decorative designs. They may serve to either hold the cups in which Omani coffee is served, or as basins for guests to wash their hands.

en.name: Ancient Egyptian Agricultural museum main entrance pathway and garden
short_description: The museum of Ancient Egyptian Agriculture is the most interesting section of the Agricultural Museum and it contains the most valuable displays. Tourist groups must receive permission beforehand in order to visit this museum. It represents the first section of the development of agriculture in Egypt ‎and it illustrates the ‎history of Egyptian agriculture from the prehistoric period till the late Pharaonic ‎period. ‎The first floor of the museum of Ancient Egyptian Agriculture hosts all sorts of ‎displays that illustrate how the ancient Egyptians cultivated their lands. The displays ‎include ancient tools and equipment that were used in the days of the Pharaohs and descriptions of ‎how the ancient Egyptians created these tools.
history:
King Fu\`ad I chose the palace of Fatma Ismail, the daughter of Khedive Ismail, ‎to host the displays of the Agricultural Museum. The ‎palace was chosen due to its location near the Egyptian Ministry of Agriculture in the ‎neighborhood of Dokki in Cairo.  
The museum, which was first called "The Agricultural Museum of King Fu\`ad I", was officially opened for the public on the 16th of January 1938 in a big ceremony that the king himself attended.
keywords: Agricultural museum; Dokki, Agriculture Palace; Khedive Ismail; King Fu`ad I; Princess Fatma; Khedivial palaces; Khedivial Egypt; Ancient Agriculture; Pharaonic Agriculture
partner: Centre for Documentation of Cultural and Natural Heritage (CULTNAT)

en.name: *Turkish ladies buying jewellery*
short_description: This watercolour, completed in 1873, shows three elegantly dressed society ladies, their faces concealed by a light veil, visiting the shop of a jeweller, his wares displayed in a small multi-tiered glass case placed on the low platform in front. While one of the ladies is seated on a carpet at the entrance to the shop to examine a pearl necklace that the old, bespectacled proprietor has offered her, her two companions wait outside and shield her to some extent from curious eyes. Vittorio Amadeo, 5th Count Preziosi (1816-1882) was an artist of Maltese origin, who left for the Middle East in the early 1840s. He settled in Istanbul as a diplomatic translator and artist, specialising in touristic scenes, vistas and types
holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Department

en.name: Castle
description:
From whichever direction one approaches Monsanto, it is easy to understand how the hill gained its name (Monte Santo - Sacred Hill).  
This is a hill that stands out from the rest, a hill that draws people to it, a hill that deserves to be made sacred!  
The excellence of this particular site first began to attract settlers a long time ago. These early inhabitants ended up fortifying the hilltop, probably in pre-Roman times, and the dominion of this site was thereafter much coveted by Romans, Goths, Arabs and the Knights Templar.  
Names such as those of the Roman praetor Lucius Emilius Paulus, Gualdim Pais and the Count of Lippe, are linked to this castle, which continued to maintain its strategic importance from ancient times to the period of the Peninsular Wars in the 19th century. This is borne out by the description and survey carried out by Eusébio Furtado, a Major of the Royal Engineering Corps (1813), which shows us a military fortress that was still perfectly operational at the time.  
The site remained important during different historical periods and the castle clearly shows this evolution in the successive transformations that it has undergone. The mediaeval settlement spread around the citadel, which in this particular case had been given the name of Alvacara, and this area too was later encircled by walls. In the 16th century, Duarte D’Armas – author of a remarkable book that illustrates a few cities and fortified castles in Portugal – presented a settlement that was moving progressively closer to the cultivated fields at the foot of the hill. A mediaeval fortification that underwent several adaptations in its transitional phase and was later strengthened with bulwarks, the castle remains as a testimony to all its many transformations. Towers, mediaeval walls and battlements from the transitional phase coexist with the earthworks, gunpowder store and embrasures of the modern fortifications. The Pião watchtower and the Chapels of São-Pedro de Vir-a-Corça and São Miguel are the finest mediaeval testimonies to survive the explosion that destroyed the gunpowder store in 1815, along with a significant part of the structures that existed between the walls. In common with most citadels, the Church of Santa Maria do Castelo marks the passage from one form of worship to another, underlining the perpetuation of the site’s sacredness and remaining as the symbol of the military victory of Christianity.

es.name: Castillo
description:
Por cualquier parte que se aproxime uno a Monsanto, no le será difícil percatarse de por qué ese monte solo puede ser santo: es un monte que destaca, que atrae, un monte sacralizable.  
Desde muy pronto las excelencias del lugar llamaron la atención de los primeros pobladores, que terminaron por fortificar la cima del monte, probablemente en la época de los castros, y romanos, godos, árabes y templarios codiciaron más tarde su dominio.  
Nombres como los del pretor romano Lucio Emilio Paulo, de Gualdim Pais y del conde de Lippe aparecen asociados a este castillo, que mantuvo su importancia estratégica desde la Antigüedad hasta las Guerras Peninsulares (contra los franceses), en pleno siglo XIX, como resulta patente por la descripción y el levantamiento de mapas hechos por el mayor Eusebio Furtado del Real Cuerpo de Ingeniería (1813), que nos muestran una plaza bélica todavía operativa.  
La importancia del sitio pasó de época en época, y el castillo registra la evolución y las transformaciones que se efectuaron sucesivamente para mantenerlo en activo. El pueblo medieval debió de crecer alrededor de la *alcazaba*, aquí denominada Alvacara, y fue cercado posteriormente, también él, con una línea de murallas.  
Duarte D’Armas, autor de un célebre libro que representa algunas ciudades fortificadas y castillos de Portugal, muestra, ya en el siglo XVI, una población que se iba aproximando poco a poco a los campos cultivados de la base del monte. Fortificación medieval, adaptaciones en la fase de transición y construcciones-baluarte, el castillo registró y atestigua todas las transformaciones que van de la neurobalística a la pirobalística. Torres, murallas medievales y troneras de la fase de transición coexisten con los terraplenes, el polvorín y las cañoneras de las fortificaciones modernas. La torre-atalaya del Pião, la capilla de São Pedro de Vir-a-Corça y la de São Miguel son los mejores testimonios medievales que sobrevivieron a la explosión que en 1815 destruyó el polvorín y una parte importante de las estructuras que subsistían extramuros.  
La iglesia de Santa Maria do Castelo, a semejanza de lo que ocurre con gran parte de las *alcazabas*, marca el paso de un culto a otro, señala la persistencia y la perpetuación de lo sagrado en el mismo lugar, es el símbolo de la victoria militar del cristianismo.

en.name: Medal to commemorate the inauguration of Ma'an station
short_description: A nickel medal issued in AH 1322 / AD 1904 to commemorate the inauguration of Ma'an station along the route of the Hijaz Railway. On the obverse is the *tuğra* of Sultan ‘Abd al-Hamid II with the inscription “al-Ghazi” and the image of a locomotive. On the reverse is the date (AH) 1322.
