it.name: Palazzo dell’Archiginnasio
description:
L'Archiginnasio fu costruito in un anno e mezzo e inaugurato il 21 ottobre 1563, per ospitare l'Università di Bologna.  
L'architetto, Morandi detto il Terribilia, progettò una facciata su due piani con portico; i mattoni e l'arenaria sono materiali  edilizi locali.  
L'edificio sorge su case di età precedente e su una porzione di terreno irregolare a sviluppo prevalentemente orizzontale; fronteggia la fiancata destra di S. Petronio e Piazza Galvani.  
Il vero cuore dell'edificio, il cortile, con il suo doppio loggiato, fu fortemente influenzato dall'architettura dei collegi universitari (per esempio il Collegio di Spagna) e allo stesso tempo richiama i cortili dei palazzi gentilizi.  
Il cortile, tutte le stanze e le pareti del palazzo sono completamente ricoperti di stemmi, dipinti o scolpiti, assemblati secondo schemi specifici. La maggior parte appartiene a studenti che ricoprirono cariche all'interno dello Studio. La decorazione araldica è isolata o circonda memorie dedicate ai professori più stimati che lavorarono all' Archiginnasio o alla autorità ecclesiastiche legate alla sua storia.  
Al centro dell'ala est del cortile, di fronte all'ingresso principale, si trova la cappella dedicata alla Madonna, che ancora conserva frammenti di affreschi di un ciclo dedicato alla vita della Vergine, dipinto dal pittore bolognese  Bartolomeo Cesi, uno degli artisti più importanti del suo tempo (1591–1594). Sfortunatamente solo alcuni frammenti di questi affreschi sopravvivono, dopo il pesante bombardamento del 1944, quando l'intera ala fu distrutta.  
Le antiche aule di lezione al primo piano, che seguono l'intera lunghezza della facciata, sono oggi occupate dai depositi librari più antichi.

L'università di Bologna ebbe sede in questo palazzo dal 1563 al 1803.  
L’edificio è caratterizzato da un lungo portico con 30 archi; il cortile è delimitato su entrambi i piani da portici e decorato da lapidi commemorative e stemmi, circondati da decorazioni scolpite e dipinte: alcune di esse furono eseguite da celebri artisti attivi in età barocca. Al primo piano si trova il Teatro Anatomico, risalente al XVII secolo, completamente ricostruito dopo il bombandamento della Seconda Guerra Mondiale. La maggior parte delle statue furono scolpite da Silvestro Giannotti nella seconda metà del XVIII secolo.
artist: Architetto: Antonio Morandi detto il “Il Terribilia” (Bologna, ?–1568)
history: Il palazzo dell' Archiginnasio fu costruito tra il 1562 e il 1563 per volere del Legato pontificio, cardinale Carlo Borromeo e del suo vice legato Pier Donato Cesi per raccogliere in un solo edificio l'Università (“Studio”), a quel tempo ancora sparsa in città. Fu progettato dall'architetto bolognese Antonio Morandi detto il Terribilia. Dal 1803 l'università fu trasferita e dal 1838 l'edificio ospita la Biblioteca comunale dell' Archiginnasio.

en.name: Chigi Tower (Torrione Chigi)
description:
Among Ariccia's archaeological heritage there are also several burials and funerary monuments. These include: a square-plan sepulchre in peperino blocks at the so-called Tomb of the Horatii and Curiatii, and the funerary monument with a rectangular plan and in *opus latericium*, both on via Appia Antica; a rupestrian tomb on via della Costa and one on via del Pometo; a sepulcher *in opus latericium* at Palombara Tower, and two on Via Appia Antica near the Chigi Tower; one circular burial in *opus caementicium* on via della Polveriera; one at the end of the Substructure of via Appia Antica.  
(Bibliography: E. Lucidi, 1796; G. R. Florescu, 1925; R. Lefevre, 1977; M. Lilli, 2002; G. Gazzetti, 2002; M. Leoni, 2008)

cs.name: Zámek Jaroměřice nad Rokytnou
description: Dvoupatrová budova se skládá z trojtraktového středního křídla, k němuž se směrem do náměstí napojuje dvojice dvoutraktů zakončených čtyřbokými pavilony, uzavírajícími čestný dvůr. Na východní straně vystupuje někdejší divadlo. Scénografii zde vytvářeli i proslulí Galli-Bibienové. boloňští scénografové působící ve Vídni. Nadokenní římsy zdobí reliéfní busty K. Obera, na bocích je architektonické členění iluzivně namalováno. K terase přiléhá francouzský parter ukončený regulovaným korytem říčky Rokytné. Zámek tvoří urbanistickou dominantu města, od přilehlého náměstí je oddělen příkopem s klenutým mostem.

Komplex barokní rezidence propojené s městem byl významným centrem barokní kultury na Moravě. Proslulé bylo zejména divadlo a hudební představení, v nichž účinkovali i poddaní. Zazněla zde první česká opera (1730). Počtem místností uspořádaných ve třech podlažích patří zámek k největším ve střední Evropě. Projekt barokní přestavby vypracoval přední rakouský architekt J. Prandtauer. Současně s budovami vznikla i zámecká zahrada francouzského typu.  Ve 20. a 30. letech 18. století zde pracovala řada italských umělců, usazených ve Vídni.
artist: Jacob Prandtauer (1660 Stanz – 1726 St. Pölten), Domenico d´Angeli, Johann Lucas Hildebrandt (1668 Janov – 1745 Vídeň), Josef Emanuel Fischer von Erlach (1656 Vídeň – 1742 Vídeň), Konrad Mathias Albrecht, Nicolas Milich (činný 1627–1736), Joseph Munggenast (1680–1741) Giovanni Michele Fontana, Giuseppe Camone, Tobias Gravani, Johann Gottfried Auerbach (1679 Mühlheim – 1743 Vídeň), Johann Baptist Glunck, Domenico Francia, Alessandro Ferretti, Giovanni Battista Pellizuoli, František Antonín Findt, Frans Stampart (1675 Antverpy –1750 Vídeň), Martin Meytens (1695 Stockholm – 1770 Vídeň), Karel František Tepper (1682–1738), Kaspar Ober
history: Po ukončení studií na univerzitě procestoval hrabě Questenberk západní Evropu. Podle vzoru Versailles hodlal postavit svou rezidenci a prezentovat svůj zájem o umění, zejména hudbu. Projekt barokní přestavby renesančního zámku vypracoval přední rakouský architekt J. Prandtauer, současně s budovami vznikla i zámecká zahrada francouzského typu. V 18. století zde fungovalo neobvyklé centrum kultury: byla zde velká knihovna, galerie, divadlo a kapela, jejímiž členy byli i poddaní. Vedoucím zámecké kapely byl známý skladatel František Václav Míča, autor první české opery “O založení města Jaroměřic” (1730). Od r. 1945 je zámek majetkem státu. Nachází se zde významná kolekce obrazů italských a nizozemských mistrů 17. století, částečně svezených z okolních zámků (Luka nad Jihlavou, Budíškovice).

en.name: Jaroměřice nad Rokytnou Chateau
description: The two-storey building consists of a three-wing central section adjoined, in the direction of the town square, by a pair of double-wings finished with quadrilateral pavilions that close a ceremonial courtyard. The former theatre is on the east side. The stage design for the theatre was created by, among others, the famous Galli da Bibiena family of artists from Bologna who were active in Vienna. Ledges over the windows feature relief busts by K. Ober. The architectural segmentation on the sides is illusionary paintwork. The terrace is adjoined by a French parterre ending in a regulated stream coming off the River Rokytná. The chateau, dominating the town, is separated from an adjacent square by a moat with a vaulted bridge.

This Baroque residential complex, closely linked with the town, was a major centre for Baroque culture in Moravia. The chateau theatre was particularly renowned, with local people featuring in musical performances. The first Czech opera was held in the chateau in 1730. With its rooms arranged on two floors, the chateau is one of the largest in Central Europe. The Baroque reconstruction was devised by the distinguished Austrian architect, J. Prandtauer. The design included a garden landscaped in the French style. In the 1720s and 30s a number of Viennese-Italian artists worked on the chateau.
artist: Jacob Prandtauer (1660 Stanz – 1726 St. Pölten), Johann Friedrich Praetorius, Domenico d´Angeli, Johann Lucas Hildebrandt (1668 Genoa – 1745 Vienna), Josef Emanuel Fischer von Erlach (1656– 1742 Vienna?), Konrad Mathias Albrecht, Nicolas Milich (active, 1627–1736), Joseph Munggenast (1680–1741) Giovanni Michele Fontana, Giuseppe Camone, Tobias Gravani, Johann Gottfried Auerbach (1679 Mühlhausen – 1743 Vienna), Johann Baptist Glunck, Domenico Maria Francia, Alessandro Ferretti, Giovanni Battista Pellizuoli, František Antonín Findt, Frans Stampart (1675 Antwerp – 1750 Vienna), Martin Meytens (1695 Stockholm – 1770 Vienna), Karel František Tepper (1682–1738), Kaspar Ober, Johann Wenzl Bergl (1718 Hradec Králové – 1789 Vienna)
history: After university, Count Questenberk travelled around western Europe. He planned to model his residence on Versailles and demonstrate his interest in the arts, especially music. The Baroque reconstruction of a Renaissance chateau was devised by the distinguished Austrian architect, J. Prandtauer. The design included a garden landscaped in the French style. In the 18th century the chateau functioned as a centre of high culture: there was a large library, a gallery, a theatre and a musical ensemble in which local people performed. The ensemble was led by the composer František Václav Míča, who wrote *The Establishment of the Town of Jaromerice* in 1730, the first Czech opera. The chateau has been the property of the state since 1945. It houses an important collection of paintings by 17th-century Italian and Dutch artists, partially gathered from neighbouring chateaux (Luka nad Jihlavou and Budíškovice).

en.name: Reconstruction of Ancyra Temple at the Rome International Exhibition, 1911
short_description: Over the centuries the Baths of Diocletian, sacked by the barbarians of Alaric, were abandoned and restored several times. In 1563, Pope Paul IV commissioned Michelangelo to transform it into a church “Santa Maria degli Angeli”. In 1749 the architect Vanvitelli rebuilt it again. For the International Exhibition of Rome in 1911, the complex of the "Baths of Diocletian” was restored again under the direction of Rodolfo Lanciani for the International Exhibition of Rome in 1911, to host the Archaeological Exhibition dedicated to Roman culture in the Imperial Era with a particular interest for its positive influence on the "ex provinces". The most incredible reconstruction on display was the Temple of Ancyra (ancient capital of Galatia, in the centre of Minor Asia) dedicated to Augustus and the goddess Roma, based on casts taken by the archaeologist Azeglio Berretti. Included in the display are the famous engraved inscription on bronze tablets, the so-called "Res Gestae” that represents the testament of emperor Augustus.

en.name: Tell Minis bowl
description:
Like its Fatimid, Egyptian models, Syrian Tell Minis pottery was experimental. It comprised tin-glazed earthenware, fritware with an opaque, white glaze, and fritware under a clear glaze that let the ware’s pale-pink color shine through.  
The frontally positioned Mediterranean figure and splendid palmettes also point the way to Fatimid lusterware.

en.name: Bowl
description:
The brass apodal bowl features an exterior decoration with a dense vegetal weave and large inscriptions in thuluth on a foliate background, interrupted by circular medallions with peonies.  
The inner base of the cup is decorated with a school of engraved fish following a circular pattern and a potentiated cross, the latter likely added when the object arrived in Europe.  
The inscription reads: "The high, lordly, sovereign, wise, active, just, ordering, zealous, Treasure, Help, Support, Assisted, \[official\] of Al-Malik an Nasir, may his victory be glorious."  
The epigraph follows the typical formula of Mamluk protocol for high-ranking figures. Although neither his name nor his specific function are indicated, the inscription suggests that the owner was an official of Sultan al-Malik al-Nasir al-Din Muhammad ibn Qulawun. This is the sultan who owned the large Borgia Collection Basin, also in the museum's collections. From this, it can be deduced that the bowl was made by 1341, that is, during the sultan's lifetime, according to the customary formula used in the inscription, which ends with the phrase "may his victory be glorious."  
The bowl, as also underscored by the decorative motif of engraved fish within, was used to hold drinking water or for ritual purposes.  
The bowl entered the museum collections thanks to Mario De Ciccio's donation to the Italian state in 1958, consisting of 1,300 pieces. These primarily consist of applied art objects from various periods and typologies, collected by the collector over a period of over 50 years, first in Palermo, his hometown, then in Naples, his adopted home since 1906, and also on the most highly regarded international art markets.

en.name: Flask
description:
Reddish clay vessel, flattened spherical in shape. It has two ribbon handles that extend from the middle of the vessel to its upper part. The two flattened sides are asymmetrical, one inverted truncated cone-shaped and the other convex with an incised decoration of several small concentric circles inserted in turn within a larger circle. The neck is not too high, cylindrical and slightly flared. The entire body is decorated with a schematic red design consisting of thick parallel brushstrokes in groups of three. The entire piece is fractured.  
  
Historically, this type of container was very common not only during the medieval Islamic period, but also in different eras and cultures, even today. Its function, carrying small amounts of water for consumption, is essential for everyday work in rural areas. In addition, the use of unglazed pottery allows the flask to breathe, keeping the water cool. Even today, cork stoppers and ropes tied to the handles are generally used for transport.
keywords: water flask, Córdoba, caliphate
materials: ceramics, pigments / moulding, incision, firing, hand painting
tags: ceramics, pigments / moulding, incision, firing, hand painting

es.name: Cantimplora
description: Recipiente de barro de color rojizo, de forma esférica achatada. Tiene dos asas de cinta que parten desde la zona media del recipiente hasta su zona superior. Las dos caras achatadas son asimétricas, una de forma troncocónica invertida y la otra de forma convexa con una decoración incisa de varios círculos concéntricos de pequeño tamaño insertos a su vez dentro de un círculo mayor. El cuello no es demasiado alto, cilíndrico y ligeramente exvasado. Por todo el cuerpo hay una decoración esquemática en color rojo a base de pinceladas gruesas paralelas en grupos de tres. Toda la pieza presenta fracturas.
materials: Cerámica, pigmentos; moldeado, inciso, cocción, pintado a mano
tags: moldeado, inciso, cocción, pintado a mano

en.name: Turkey. Inside view of the Scutari Hospital during the Crimean war.
names: *One of the Wards of the Hospital at Scutari*
short_description: Florence Nightingale (1820–1910), a British nurse famous for her commitment to and improvement of the health service, was sent to on a humanitarian mission to Scutari in the middle of the Crimean war. With a team of about 30 nurses, she cleaned the hospital and reorganised the wards in order to prevent the outbreak of epidemics. In this image she is pictured in the sick ward, taking various measures to improve its hygiene.
keywords: Hospital; Crimean war; Turkey

fr.name: Turquie. Vue intérieure de l'hôpital de Scutari pendant la guerre de Crimée
short_description: Florence Nightingale (1820-1910), infirmière britannique célèbre pour son engagement et les améliorations qu’elle apporta au service de santé, obtint d’être envoyée en mission humanitaire à Scutari en pleine guerre de Crimée. Avec une équipe d’une trentaine d’infirmière, elle nettoya l’hôpital et réorganisa les soins afin de lutter contre les épidémies. Cette image la montre dans la salle des malades en train de prendre différentes mesures pour que l’hygiène soit améliorée.
keywords: Hôpital; guerre; Crimée; Turquie

en.name: Textile from the Prince Felipe of Castile burial
names: Fragmento de tejido de la tumba del Infante D. Felipe
description: This fragment came from the set of garments wore by the Castilian Prince Phillip in his burial at Villalcázar de Sirga (Palencia). The fragment is a very good example of the richness of the textile from al-Andalus. The textile has an inscription in Arabic that could be translated as “Glory to our Lord the Sultan”. This an early example of the interest in collecting important textiles, even before the important research made by Gómez-Moreno in the Royal Convent of the Huelgas (Burgos).
keywords: Nasrid art; islamic influence; orientalism; collectionism

en.name: *Ruins of Troy: general excavation plan by Mr Schliemann*
short_description: Heinrich Schliemann (1822–1890) was a German businessman who discovered his passion for archaeology whilst travelling. In 1870 he decided to direct an archaeological campaign in Turkey where he discovered the ruins of Troy. Various scandals (stolen objects, scientific errors) quickly destroyed his reputation, and today he is credited only with having created sites which led to important advances in the field. However, this plan of Troy is evidence for Schliemann's efforts to direct the excavations in a rigorous scientific manner.
keywords: Greek antiquities; archaeological excavations; Schliemann; Turkey; plans

fr.name: *Ruines de Troia (Troie): plan général des fouilles faites par Mr Schliemann*
short_description: Heinrich Schliemann (1822-1890) est un homme d’affaires allemand qui au fil de ses voyages se passionne pour l’archéologie. En 1870, il décide de mener des fouilles en Turquie et découvre les ruines de Troie. Plusieurs scandales (objets dérobés, erreurs scientifiques) éclaboussent bientôt sa réputation. Il lui reste le mérite d’avoir mis à jour des sites importants et d’avoir fait progresser l’archéologie. Ce plan de Troie témoigne en effet des efforts de Schliemann pour mener les fouilles archéologiques avec rigueur.
keywords: Antiquités grecques; fouilles arhéologiques; Schliemann; Turquie; plans

ar.name: كِسرة من زبدية.
description: كِسرة من زبدية مصنوعة من عجينة بيضاء كوارتزية مزينة بزخارف زرقاء فضية وسوداء تحت تزجيج شفاف، لا لون له. وهذه الكِسرة عبارة عن قعر صحن مزيَّن بدائرة تحتوي على خط عربي متضافر مع سويقات وأوراق متناسقة. ويحيط بالدائرة طوق من الزخارف الملوَّنة بالأسود والأبيض. ولأن تصميم هذه الزبدية وأسلوب صناعتها كانا شائعين في كلٍ من سوريا ومصر، فمن الصعب جداً تحديد مكان الصنع بدقة. وتكمن هذه الصعوبة في واقعة أن الخزَّافين في كلٍ من مصر وسوريا، إبان العصر المملوكي، كانوا يتنقلون بين مدن هذين الإقليمين بحثاً عن العمل. أما نمط الرسم بالأسود والأبيض تحت طبقة مزججة فقد بدأ في إيران خلال أواخر القرن السابع / الثالث عشر، وسرعان ما امتدَّ إلى سوريا ومصر. وتتميَّز العلامات الفارقة الرئيسية بين الأواني المصنوعة في إيران أو سوريا أو مصر باختلاف أشكال القطع وأحجامها.

كان الخطّ العربي ُيوظَّف لتزيين سلسلة طويلة ومتنوعة من السطوح. ومع أن مقداراً كافياً من النص لا يبقى، لتيسير فكّ الألغاز وإدراك المعاني، فإن أمثالاً، وأبيات شعر، وأدعيات، كثيراً ما كانت تتكرَّر. إن الخطوط العمودية القوية للخطّ النسخي طاغية على المركز الأزرق الكوبالتي لهذه الطاسة السوداء.
holder: متحف وصالة فنون كيلفينغروف، متاحف غلاسكو.
dates: القرن السابع- الثامن / الثالث عشر- الرابع عشر.
place: صُنعت في سوريا، ووُجدت في الفسطاط، في مصر.
keywords: تجارة؛ زخرفة كتابية.
materials: عجينة بيضاء كوارتزية، مزينة بزخارف زرقاء فضية وسوداء تحت تزجيج شفاف، لا لون له.
tags: عجينة بيضاء كوارتزية، مزينة بزخارف زرقاء فضية وسوداء تحت تزجيج شفاف، لا لون له.

en.name: Bowl fragment.
description: A fragment from a stone-paste (fritware) bowl decorated in cobalt-blue and black under a transparent colourless glaze. This fragment, from the centre of the dish, is decorated with a roundel within which is Arabic calligraphy intertwined with organic stems and leaves. A band of black and white decoration surrounds the roundel. The design and technique of this bowl was common in both Syria and Egypt, making identification of the place of production very difficult. The difficulty lies in the fact that the potters of both Mamluk Egypt and Syria migrated in search of work between the cities of the two regions. The fashion for painting in black and blue under a transparent glaze started in Iran during the late AH 7th / AD 13th century, and spread quickly to Syria and Egypt. The main distinguishing features between wares made in Iran, Syria or Egypt are the different shapes and sizes of the pieces.

Arabic calligraphy was employed to decorate a wide variety of surfaces. Although not enough of the text survives to be deciphered, proverbs, poetic verses and prayers were frequently used. The strong vertical lines of the *naskhi*\-style script dominate the centre of the cobalt-blue and black bowl.
holder: Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum, Glasgow Museums.
place: Produced in Damascus, Syria; found at Fustat, Egypt.
keywords: Commerce; calligraphy
materials: Stone-paste (fritware) with black and cobalt-blue decoration under a transparent, colourless glaze.
tags: Stone-paste (fritware) with black and cobalt-blue decoration under a transparent, colourless glaze.

es.name: Fragmento de cuenco.
description:
Fragmento de cuenco de pasta de piedra (frita) decorado en azul cobalto y negro bajo vidriado transparente. Este fragmento corresponde a la parte central del plato y está decorado con un medallón con caligrafía entrelazada con decoración orgánica de tallos y hojas. Rodea el medallón una banda ornamental negra y blanca.  
Es difícil saber con seguridad dónde fue producido, ya que tanto el diseño como la técnica fueron comunes en Siria y Egipto. Durante el periodo de dominio mameluco, alfareros egipcios y sirios transitaron entre ciudades de ambas regiones en busca de trabajo. A finales del siglo VII / XIII, en Irán empezó a pintarse en negro y azul bajo vidriado transparente, y esta tendencia se extendió rápidamente a Siria y Egipto. Lo que distingue las cerámicas de Irán, Siria y Egipto entre sí son las diferentes formas y tamaños de las piezas.

La caligrafía arábiga se utilizaba como motivo decorativo sobre muchas clases de superficies. Aunque no se han conservado demasiados textos que puedan ser descifrados, en la mayoría de los casos se trata de proverbios, versos y oraciones. En el centro de este cuenco azul y negro, el motivo que más destaca son las marcadas líneas verticales de la escritura *nasji*.
holder: Galería de Arte y Museo Kelvingrove, Museos de Glasgow.
dates: Siglo VII o VIII de la Hégira / XIII-XIV d. C.
place: Damasco (Siria), aunque se halló en Fustat (Egipto).
keywords: comercio; caligrafía.
materials: Pasta de piedra (frita) decorada en negro y azul cobalto bajo vidriado incoloro transparente.
tags: Pasta de piedra (frita) decorada en negro y azul cobalto bajo vidriado incoloro transparente.

fr.name: Fragment de coupe.
description: Fragment de coupe en céramique frittée à décor bleu de cobalt et noir sous glaçure incolore transparente. Partie centrale de la coupe, ce tesson est orné d'un rondeau contenant une inscription calligraphique arabe entrelacée de tiges et de feuilles. Un bandeau à décor noir et blanc entoure cette partie. Ce type de dessin et cette technique étaient courants aussi bien en Syrie qu'en Égypte, rendant l'identification du lieu de production très difficile. Les potiers de l'Égypte et de la Syrie des Mamelouks se déplaçaient en effet aisément entre les villes de ces deux provinces, à la recherche de travail. La mode de peindre en noir et bleu sous glaçure transparente débuta en Iran à la fin du VIIe siècle H (XIIIe siècle J.-C.) et se répandit rapidement en Égypte et en Syrie. Les caractéristiques distinctives des productions iraniennes, syriennes ou égyptiennes tiennent aux formes et aux dimensions des pièces.

La calligraphie arabe fut employée pour décorer une grande variété de surfaces. Bien que le texte qui reste soit insuffisant pour être déchiffré, il est établi que des proverbes, versets poétiques et prières étaient souvent utilisés. Les vigoureuses lignes verticales de l’écriture de style *naskhi* dominent le centre de cette coupe en bleu cobalt et noir.
holder: Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum, Glasgow Museums.
dates: VIIe-VIIIe siècle de l’Hégire (XIIIe-XIVe siècle J.-C.).
place: Production syrienne, trouvé à Fustat, Égypte.
keywords: commerce ; calligraphie
materials: Céramique frittée à décor noir et bleu de cobalt sous glaçure incolore transparente.
tags: Céramique frittée à décor noir et bleu de cobalt sous glaçure incolore transparente.

ar.name: طبق
description:
تشكل الزخارف الزهرية والطيور الصينية إطارًا لهذه اللوحة الخزفية الفارسية مع مشهد مركزي لبلاط ملكي يشاهد أداء مبارزة. تحمل اللوحة التاريخ الهجري لعام 1309 هـ الموافق 1891 م ، واسم حاكم سلالة الزند محمد صادق خان من شيراز في إيران. ربما يمثل المتفرجون في المبارزة الحاكم مع عائلته وأصدقائه المقربين.  
  
خلال القرن التاسع عشر ، زادت واردات البورسلين من ألمانيا وإنجلترا والصين بسبب الذوق الفاخر لإيران قاجار. دخل البورسلين الأوروبي السوق الإيراني عبر تركيا ، بينما قام الصينيون بتصدير الأواني الخزفية إلى جانب القهوة والشاي والزجاج عبر الهند وبخارى عبر طريق الحرير.  
  
على الرغم من ظهور لوحات الخزف الصيني مع الأنماط الإسلامية والأسماء والتواريخ بالفارسية (الفارسية) ، استمرت الزخارف الصينية والبوذية مثل طائر الفينيق وزهرة اللوتس. أصبح خزف تشينغ متعدد الألوان مثل هذه اللوحة شائعًا في القرن الثامن عشر. في إيران ، عانت صناعة الفخار من عواقب تفضيل أدوات المائدة الأجنبية على الحرف المحلية. بحلول أوائل القرن العشرين ، تحول الخزف بتكليف من المحاكم الفارسية الملكية من الأصل الصيني والألماني إلى العناصر الإنجليزية ذات الأسعار المعقولة.  
  
تتضمن المجموعات المعاصرة أطباق فارسية وفيرة من بيوت البورسلين الأجنبية الذين ما زالوا يصنعون أواني الطعام حتى يومنا هذا.
holder: متحف الشيخ فيصل بن قاسم ال ثاني
partner: متحف الشيخ فيصل بن قاسم ال ثاني

en.name: Plate
description:
This elegant plate was crafted in Guangzhou (formerly Canton) in AH 1309 / AD 1891-1892, exemplifying the refined artistry of Chinese export porcelain during the late Qing Dynasty. The intricate design showcases scenes of daily life, featuring pagoda-style architecture and traditional Chinese elements, capturing the cultural essence of the period.  
  
A particularly intriguing feature of this piece is its inscription. Written in Arabic-Persian script, it bears the phrase هو الباقي (He \[Allah\] is the Everlasting), emphasising divine permanence. Additionally, the inscription includes the word فرمايش (ordered), indicating that the plate was specially commissioned for Mohamed Sadiq Khan, who is most likely Sarwar al-Malak, a renowned musician from the courts of Shah Naser al-Din and Shah Muzaffar al-Din. This suggests that the plate may have been part of the Persian royal court’s cultural or artistic exchanges.  
  
At the lower part of the plate, we can also notice the marking "ص 92". While its exact meaning remains uncertain, it may indicate the production year (1892) or serve as a workshop code or inventory mark.  
  
This plate stands as a remarkable testament to the artistic and cultural exchanges between China and the Persian-speaking world, seamlessly blending Chinese craftsmanship with Persian artistic and literary influences.
holder: Sheikh Faisal Bin Qassim Al Thani
keywords: China; Plate; Iran; Persian; Farsi; Porcelain
partner: Sheikh Faisal Bin Qassim Al Thani Museum (FBQ Museums)

en.name: Cadillac Series 62 Convertible
description:
In 1954, the Belgian Royal Palace’s car fleet expanded significantly with the addition of this Cadillac Series 62 convertible, which became the official parade vehicle. Featuring specifications ahead of its time for 1955, it proudly bore the Belgian number plate “1” and was predominantly used by King Baudouin. This impressive limousine embarked on a historic mission in 1955: During King Baudouin’s first trip to Congo, where he was welcomed as “Bwana Kitoko,” the Cadillac covered part of the 10,000-km journey.  
  
In 1959, the Series 62 served as the bridal car for Prince Albert and Paola’s wedding. A year later, King Baudouin and Queen Fabiola also celebrated their marriage in this Cadillac. To withstand the harsh winter weather during the latter wedding, coachbuilder "Vesters & Neirinck" constructed a transparent plexiglass dome, ensuring the newlyweds could sit warmly in the spacious rear seat while remaining visible to the many well-wishers.  
  
The car underwent several modifications to fulfill its royal duties. Notably, the front bench was divided into two sections, allowing the passenger side to slide back, enabling the occupant to stand upright and greet the crowd. Additionally, a handle was mounted on the windscreen pillar to facilitate standing without mishaps.  
  
After being sold by the royal family, the Cadillac’s missions became less historic. At one point in Paris, it was even used for public sightseeing tours. Autoworld is delighted to have been able to reunite the royal Cadillac Series 62 with other cars from the former royal fleet.
keywords: Iconic fins; V8 engine; chrome trim; convertible

en.name: Renault Type X1 Coupé de Ville
description: A gorgeous "Coupé de ville" with coachwork by Bernin from Tours, this car is in its original condition. The driver, protected only by a windscreen and a roof, received instructions from their passengers via a horn.
keywords: Brass era; leather interior; chauffeur-driven; luxury

en.name: The Mother of God Smolenskaya with Oklad
description:
This is a *Hodegetria* (Greek for “one who shows the way”) Mother of God icon, recognizable by the solemn expression of the Mother of God and the frontal position of the Christ Child delivering a blessing. The Christ Child sits on his Mother’s left knee and holds a tightly rolled scroll. The original icon was brought from Byzantium in the 12th century and kept in the Assumption Cathedral in the city of Smolensk. In the 15th century, the icon was transferred to Moscow before being returned to Smolensk.  
This icon has four additional figures, two on each border: a guardian angel and Venerable Basil the Confessor on the left, and Saint John the Baptist and Saint Anne the Prophet on the right. The *oklad* (covering) is solid silver under mercury gilding with no apparent hallmark. The *oklad* has a large nimbus containing sculpted angels with openings for their faces and hands, as well as many gems and a raised floral and fruit design. An inscription on the bottom border reads as follows:  
  
At the Alenskiy-Skete in the area of Kerzhenets, the Schemamonk Filaret the icon painter, had painted this icon for the Schemamonk Iosif. At the year 7250 \[1740\] this icon was given to the treasury of the Schemanun Irinarkha. The Abbess, the nun Anafoliya donated this icon in the year 7376 \[1868\], at the third day of February to the Archbishop Antonij of Moscow and Vladimir.
keywords: Virgin Mary and Child; Religious iconography

en.name: An old exhibition from Tiled Kiosk
short_description: The Tiled Kiosk is a pavilion set within the outer walls of Topkapı Palace and dates from 1472. It was built by the Ottoman sultan Mehmed II as a pleasure palace or kiosk. The building was used as the Imperial Museum between 1875 and 1891. In 1953, it was opened to the public as a museum of Turkish and Islamic art, and was later incorporated into the Istanbul Archaeology Museums. The collections of the Tiled Kiosk Museum consist of about 2000 artefacts belonging to the Seljuk and Ottoman eras, dating from the 11th-20th centuries. These artefacts include those that existed when the museum was incorporated into the İstanbul Archaeological Museums due to its closeness and those acquired through excavations, purchases, donations and confiscations.
keywords: Istanbul Archaeological Museum; Tiled Kiosk

en.name: Mashhad al-Hussein
description:
Aleppo is a city of shrines, of which two important Shi‘ite examples have survived about 2 km west of Bab Antakiya, at the foot of Jabal Jawshan. Mashhad al-Hussein is the larger and more important of the two; in fact, it is the most important medieval Shi‘ite structure in the whole of Syria and continues to function as a pilgrimage shrine attracting thousands of visitors. Nevertheless, it is a thoroughly Ayyubid building that was constructed over several interrelated phases between the late 6th/12th and early 7th/13th centuries. In 1920, a massive explosion  
damaged the shrine badly. It remained in ruins for about 50 years, until methodically and scientifically restored to its original appearance by 1983. Briefly used as a local mosque, there was  
a sudden transformation a few years later, that saw it change from an exquisite Ayyubid-style building into a modern Shi’ite shrine with a covered courtyard and a glittering cenotaph inserted into its main *iwan*.  
The original shrine, measuring 70 m by 40 m, consists of two parts: an unfinished enclosure surrounded by small rooms and, a few steps higher, the main courtyard. The main entrance to the shrine is from the east, through an elaborate *muqarnas* portal framed by a wide arch with radiating stonework. The foundation text above the door,  
framed within a splendid braided design, has above it a frieze of tiny lamps suspended within a continuous arcade. It is likely that the light imagery alludes to the radiance that is often  
associated with Imam Hussein.  
The central part of the shrine is disposed around an almost-square courtyard, which is focused on an elevated western *iwan* and flanked by two  
smaller arches surmounted by an interlace motif. A large panel with a Shi‘ite inscription that gives the names of the 12 Imams crowns the *iwan*. The south side has a five-domed  
prayer-hall, balanced on the north side by four domed bays. Also contributing to the balance and unity of the courtyard is a cornice raised on brackets that surrounds the courtyard on three  
sides.  
North of this courtyard are two independent units, added in the early 7th/13th century, each consisting of two vaulted chambers. The western unit consists of two adjoining  
chambers covered by exquisite domes, one resting on eight squinches, and the other on a halo of *muqarnas* cells. It seems likely that the first of these chambers was for study and  
meditation, while the second served as a residence for the sheikh of the shrine, since it includes a small latrine hidden discretely in a corner. The eastern unit, which has its own entrance, was entirely utilitarian, including a kitchen and a set of seven latrines. These functions are entirely in keeping with the character of a pilgrimage shrine.

en.name: Tile Cup
description: The drinking vessel is composed of a white clay and slip with polychrome decoration beneath a transparent colourless glaze. The composition features a series of tulips and stylised carnation branches of varying sizes rising vertically from separate roots on a white ground. The red, green and blue motifs are outlined in black. Beginning in the second half of the 16th century, it appears that the emerald green glaze, which was used extensively, would run during the firing process. It is posited that the quality of ceramics began to decline in tandem with the deterioration of the economy. Examples from the 16th century demonstrate that the naturalistic floral motifs, which were widely employed in Classical Ottoman style, were still being used during this period.
dates: Hegira late 10th century / AD late 16th century

en.name: High Altar
description:
The sculptor, António Bellini of Pádua, was responsible for the decoration of the chancel. He endowed it with a sense of immateriality and a subtle notion of “suspension” seen in, for example, the main altar where angels worship on top of the white marble pediment flanking the cedar sculpture of Christ by Manuel Dias.  
In the central panel is the *Assumption of the Virgin*, signed and dated 1731 by Agostino Masucci. This is surrounded by other paintings of the *Nativity,* *Conception*, *Adoration of the Shepherds* and the *Coronation,* all of which were painted in his workshop.
artist: The angels, the *Four Virtues*, the pediment over the main arch and busts of *St. Peter and St. Paul* are by João António Bellini de Pádua (active 1725–1748); the paintings are by the workshop of Agostino Masucci
partner: Institute for the Administration of Architectural and Archaeological Heritage -  IGESPAR

pt.name: Altar-mor
description:
António Bellini de Pádua introduziu os temas barrocos que distendem a arquitectura, dotando-a de imaterialidade e de um subtil efeito de “suspensão”, obtido, no altar-mor, pelos anjos em adoração assentes no topo do frontão interrompido, de mármore branco, que ladeiam o *Cristo* de madeira de cedro, de Manuel Dias.  
No painel central, a pintura a óleo sobre tela, de Agostini Masucci, *Assunção d*a *Virgem,* que ele assina e data de 1731, e dos lados, as telas sobre a *Natividade*, a *Conceição*, a *Adoração dos Pastores* e a *Coroação,* executadas na sua oficina.
artist: António Bellini de Pádua: esculturas dos anjos, das *Quatro Virtudes*, do frontão sobre o arco-mestre e dos bustos de S. Pedro e de S. Paulo; Agostino Masucci (oficina): pintura.

en.name: Masnad
description:
The carpets used at Islamic courts were most often produced by court workshops and intended to convey very different messages from those found in private homes. Court carpets belonged to the whole ensemble of objects that helped assert the right to rule and shaped the ruler’s public image, namely the throne, crown, royal ceremonial robe, regal standards with their pennants, scepter, and ring.  
  
Spread either in front of or beneath the ruler or religious leader, a carpet, like a throne, served to designate the privileged space around the most highly esteemed individual and to present him regally to his audience. As a special object, it helped to maintain the dignity and authority of the ruler enthroned upon it.  
  
Through its design, a carpet is clearly isolated from its surroundings by its well-defined borders. It immediately creates an independent space within its own environment. Thus the design of the carpet frames and emphasizes the individual who sits on it and serves almost as an aura filling the immediate space around him.  
  
Stepping on this carpet was possible only with the ruler’s permission and was regarded as a great honour, an act of mutual confidence, obedience, or the subject's unconditional support of the ruler. In some cases it recalls the act of bestowing a robe of honour upon the most loyal subject.
keywords: Silk; wool; Mughal
materials: Silk (warp and weft), pashmina wool (pile); knotted pile; asymmetrical knot
partner: The George Washington University Museum and The Textile Museum

en.name: Madrasa Hafiziyya
description:
The layout of this *madrasa* is very irregular, constructed in different phases and in a transitional cusp-period straddling the late Ayyubid to early Mamluk periods. It belongs to Arghun al-Hafiziyya, a freed slave woman of al-Malik al-‘Adil. She became very rich and her surname, al-Hafiz, refers to al-Malik al-Hafiz lord of Qal’at Ja’bar (VIII.3.) on the Euphrates, whom she brought up. She died in 648/1250 and was buried within the mausoleum.  
The *madrasa*’s mausoleum is of a typical square plan, while the prayer hall attached to it follows a miniature cruciform plan with a vaulted courtyard, similar to that of Madrasa al-Rukniyya. The main artistic feature is the peculiar entrance: a narrow bay covered by a conch-shaped vault. The ribs of the conch stretch over the whole vault and form a lobed arch at the front. The gate opens from a side wall of the bay. This strange entrance, together with the asymmetry of the general layout reveals the extent of manoeuverability that Syrian architects exhibited in adapting the Eastern-inspired Seljuq prototype.

en.name: Medallion carpet fragments
description:
Two 16th century Safavid pile carpet fragments from a very large classic Persian medallion carpet, showing parts of the centre-field and part of one of the long borders of the carpet. The background colour of the field is a wine red. Imposed on it is a vegetal network of floral arabesque stem patterns baring rosettes and palmettes. Over this vegetal stem network are placed multi-coloured medallions, with a large yellow one dominating the centre, and smaller ivory coloured and dark-blue coloured pendent-like cartouches at either end of it. The large yellow medallion holds a red star-shape cartouche in the centre and turquoise blue and dark blue cartouches radiating out. All the cartouches are filled with multi-coloured vegetal-stem-and-palmette arabesque compositions. The border has a dark blue background and is decorated with two intertwined leaf-stem scrolls, one turquoise and one yellow.  
  
The smaller of the two fragments, no. 9.28, consists of two large lobed cartouches, one with a dark blue background and one with a turquoise background, on a the yellow field of the central medallion. Each of the dark and light blue and the yellow areas is filled with a vegetal network of multi-coloured floral arabesque patterns baring rosettes and palmettes.  
  
The large yellow medallion and its pendant cartouches is reminiscent of the “shamsa” medallions painted in illuminated manuscripts and on book covers. The term shamsa, from the Arabic shams, which means sun, here used to name this type of radiating arabesque medallion.
place: Iran; possibly the city of Tabriz
keywords: medallion; vegetal arabesque; palmette
materials: Cotton warp and weft; wool pile

ar.name: الفردوسي، الشهنامة (كتاب الملوك)
description: ألّف أبو القاسم منصور، الملقّب بـالفردوسي (تاريخ. 411هـ / 1020–1021م)، القصيدة الملحمية الشهيرة والواسعة المعروفة باسم الشهنامة (Shahnama، «كتاب الملوك») نحو عام 1000م. كُتبت هذه النسخة بخط النستعليق على يد الناسخ ابن أبو البركات أسد الله في 1025–1026هـ / 1616–1617م، ويُرجَّح أنها نُسخت في منطقة قريبة من أصفهان، إيران. ووفقًا لختمي النسخ الواردين في الصفحة 251a والصفحة 447a، أتمّ الناسخ نسخ الجزء الثاني من الملحمة قبل الجزء الأول. وتكشف أختام ثلاثة من المُلّاك أن المخطوط كان ضمن مجموعة محمد بن محمد هاشم سنة 1029هـ / 1619م، ثم محمد ناصر سنة 1051هـ / 1641م، ثم جوزيف فون هامر-بورغستال سنة 1223هـ / 1808–1809م. وبعد ذلك أصبحت المخطوطة جزءًا من المكتبة الوطنية النمساوية عام 1842م. وتدل اللوحات الأربع والأربعون المتنوّعة في أحجامها وأساليبها الفنية وجودتها، على أنّ المخطوطة صُنعت على الأرجح في عاصمة إقليمية استلهمت فنونها من المركز الفني في أصفهان، إيران.
keywords: افراسياب. بهرام; شعبة; ملحمي; فريدون; فردوسي; جارشاسب. اسفنديار; اسكندر; رستم; شاهناما; سام; سيمورج. زال
materials: حبر، ألوان  وذهب على الورق. خط  نسخ نستعليق مزخرف،  25 سطرًا في الصفحة الواحدة.
tags: حبر، ألوان وذهب على الورق. خط نسخ نستعليق مزخرف، 25 سطرًا في الصفحة الواحدة.

en.name: Ferdowsi, *Shahnama* ('The Book of Kings')
description: Abu'l-Qasim Mansur, called Ferdowsi (died 411 AH / 1020-1 AD) wrote the renowned, extensive epic poem called *Shahnama* (‘The Book of Kings’) around 1000 AD. This copy was written in *nasta’liq* script by the scribe Ibn Abu'l-Barakat Asadallah in 1025-1026 AH / 1616-17 AD, possibly near Isfahan, Iran. According to the two colophons (fol. 251a, 447a), the scribe completed the second part of the epic before the first. Stamps of three owners reveal that the manuscript was in the collection of a Muhammad b. Muhammad Hashim in 1029 AH / 1619 AD, of a Muhammad Nasir in 1051 AH / 1641 AD, and of Joseph von Hammer-Purgstall in 1223 AH / 1808-9 AD. The manuscript then became part of the Austrian National Library in 1842. Its 44 paintings of various sizes, artistic styles, and qualities reveal that it was likely made in a provincial capital that drew inspirations from the artistic centre of Isfahan, Iran.
keywords: Afrasiyab; Bahram; Div; epic; Faridun; Ferdowsi; Garshasp; Isfandiyar; Iskandar; Rustam; Shahnama; Sam; Simurgh; Zal
materials: Ink, colour and gold on paper. Calligraphic *nasta'liq* script of 25 lines per page.
tags: Ink, colour and gold on paper. Calligraphic nasta'liq script of 25 lines per page.

en.name: Archaeological Museum
description:
**Pair of Iron Armlets**  
During the Ottoman era, soldiers used equipment like armour, armlets, and shields during war to protect their bodies from sword and arrow blows. The armlet worn by the warriors was a kind of armour designed to protect the part of the arm between the wrist and the elbow. Basically, it is made up of two side wings tied with chain hoops to the main body that goes over the arm. Because most of the extant examples are products of fine quality workmanship and are richly decorated, it leads one to believe that armlets were tools used by high-ranking soldiers. The examples displayed in the Manisa Museum consist only of the main parts, as the wings are missing. The surfaces of both armlets are decorated with engraving and gold gilding. Although they look a lot alike, the armlets exhibit differences regarding decoration. For this reason, it is thought that the two pieces belong to different pairs of armlets. The armlets are decorated with engraved large sunbursts (şemse), cartouches, and tulip designs, while the area between the motifs is filled with a gilded plant composition exhibiting even finer workmanship. These two armlets are dated to the 15th century. There are contemporary examples of armlets similar to these at the Military Museum in İstanbul.  
  
**Manisa Great Mosque’s Minbar Door Wings**  
The Manisa Great Mosque’s *minbar* was made by a master named Hacı Mehmed Ibn Abdülaziz from Antep in 1377 at the order of İshak Çelebi, one of the Saruhan Beys; today it is being restored and its doors are protected in the Manisa Museum. The *minbar* door wings, made of ebony wood, exhibit quite careful workmanship. Ornamental panels and panels with inscriptions are symmetrically arranged on the door. The large rectangular panels surrounded by ornamental and inscribed strips are the most interesting components of the composition. Star and polygonal shapes formed with long and narrow strips of wood are decorated with mother-of-pearl, ivory, and wood components of various types and colours. We learn from the inscriptions on the door wings that the decorative composition was prepared by a master craftsman named Fakih Ibn Yusuf.

es.name: Museo Arqueológico de Manisa
description:
**Par de brazales de hierro**  
En la época otomana, los soldados usaban armaduras, brazales y escudos en las batallas, para protegerse de las espadas y las flechas. El brazal que llevaban los guerreros servía para proteger el antebrazo. Estaba formado por dos alas, unidas por anillas a un cuerpo principal que iba sobre la armadura. El hecho de que las piezas existentes sean de excelente factura y estén ricamente decoradas hace pensar que eran objetos utilizados por militares de alto rango. Los brazales que se exponen en el Museo de Manisa solo poseen la parte principal; las alas han desaparecido. Aunque son muy parecidos, su decoración presenta diferencias, por lo que se cree que pertenecieron a distintos pares de brazales. Las superficies de estas piezas están decoradas con incisiones de soles (şemşe), cartelas y tulipanes, y los espacios entre las incisiones se han rellenado de composiciones vegetales en oro que muestran un trabajo aún más refinado. Estos dos brazales datan del siglo XV. En el Museo Militar de Estambul hay ejemplos de brazales contemporáneos y similares.  
  
**Postigos de la puerta del mimbar de la mezquita Mayor de Manisa**  
El *mimbar* de la mezquita Mayor de Manisa fue creado en 1377 por un maestro artesano llamado Hacı Mehmet Ibn Abdülaziz, de Antep, por orden de İshak Çelebi, uno de los beyes saruhaníes; está siendo restaurado y sus puertas se conservan en el Museo de Manisa. Los postigos, de madera de ébano, muestran una esmerada elaboración. Los ornamentos y filacterias están dispuestos simétricamente en la puerta. Los grandes paneles rectangulares, rodeados de bandas ornamentales y caligráficas, son el elemento más interesante de la composición. Las estrellas y figuras geométricas formadas con largas y estrechas tablillas están adornadas con madreperla, marfil y madera de varias clases y colores. Por las inscripciones sabemos que estos postigos fueron obra de un artesano llamado Fakih Ibn Yusuf.

en.name: Shallow Dish
description: This dish has a shallow wall with a narrow everted rim and stands on a ring-like foot. Its decoration consists of an allover pattern. A five-pointed star with enclosed triangles around the base and the lower part of the wall continues with a row of large lozenges containing smaller lozenges. The pattern can be seen when viewed from the exterior as well as on the interior if seen against light. This decoration was produced by blowing the glass into a dip mould; taken out of the mould it was further blown and tooled with great accuracy. A large pontil mark (from a hot metal rod with some glass attached to it) in the exterior center of the foot remains from shaping and tooling the dish.
materials: Glass, deep blue, thin brownish weathering; mould-blown, tooled, worked on the pontil
tags: Glass, deep blue, thin brownish weathering
mould-blown, tooled, worked on the pontil

ar.name: لوحة شخصية للسلطان العثماني أحمد الأول.
description:
يمثل هذا الرسم المنمنم المنفذ بألوان الغواش على قطعة من الورق لوحة شخصية للسلطان العثماني محمد الأول (1012-26/ 1603-17)، وقد كانت في يوم من الأيام جزءاً من ألبوم يتضمن منمنمات عثمانية تركية وفارسية، جمعت على ما يبدو في القرن الثاني عشر/ الثامن عشر. لقد تم تمثيل الحاكم الشاب، المعروف بمؤسس الجامع الأزرق في اسطنبول، جالساً على عرش كبير مزين بكثافة تحت قوس مدبب، وقد استند على وسادة مزخرفة، وهو يلبس عمامة بيضاء مزينة بريشتين طويلتين تنبثقان من شكل كأسي مرصع. لثوبه الواسع المصنوع من البروكار الأخضر والذهبي أزرار ذهبية كروية تحت الصدر، وقد تم دعمه بحزام ذهبي مرصع مع ثلاث قطع دائرية مدببة في الأمام، ويظهر منه إلى اليمين مقبض خنجر مرصع. يرتدي السلطان معطفاً من اللون البرتقالي المحمر ذا أزرار ذهبية صغيرة من الأمام، وهو محلى بالفرو من أطرافه، ويظهر من تحت الثوب خف ذهبي اللون. يحمل السلطان أحمد في يده اليسرى، التي يزين خنصرها خاتم ذهبي ذو حجر مستدير، منديلاً تشريفياً ذا تفاصيل مذهبة، أما في يده اليمنى فيحمل كتاباً من الشعر من النوع الذي يتم ربط صفحاته من الجانب الأعلى الضيق. يظهر على الغلاف المذهب رصيعة مركزية مرسومة بإتقان محاطة بإطار متطاول قوسي الشكل.  
تعلو لوحة السلطان كتابة متصلة ضمن إطارين متطاولين مستدقي الأطراف مكتوبة على أرضية زرقاء ومزينة بتفاصيل زهرية بيضاء، وهي تذكر العبارة التالية: "حضرة سلطان أحمد بن السلطان محمد خان"، أما الكتابة الصغيرة الموجودة في الجهة اليسرى السفلى فتذكر أسماء الرسام "الفقير سليمان". تمت إحاطة اللوحة بإطار داخلي أخضر وآخر خارجي برتقالي بالإضافة إلى إطارات زرقاء وحمراء وذهبية وخضراء بينهما وحول الإطار الخارجي.

هذه الصورة المنمنمة هي للسلطان العثماني أحمد الأول، الذي اشتُهر ببناء المسجد الأزرق في استنبول. قيل إن هذه الصورة نُفذت في ورشات البلاط بقصر توب قابي في استنبول خلال العقود الأولى من القرن الحادي عشر الهجري/ السابع عشر الميلادي.
holder: المتحف الملكي، المتحف الوطني في اسكتلندا NMS.
dates: النصف الأول من القرن الحادي عشر/ النصف الأول من السابع عشر.
keywords: الفقير سليمان.

en.name: Portrait of the Ottoman Sultan Ahmed I.
description:
This miniature painting executed in gouache on paper is a portrait of the Ottoman Sultan Ahmed I (AH 1012–26 / AD 1603–17) and once formed part of an album that contained both Ottoman Turkish and Persian miniatures, apparently assembled in the AH 12th / AD 18th century. The youthful ruler, best known as the founder of the Blue Mosque in Istanbul, is seated on a large, richly decorated throne beneath a cusped arch. He is leaning against a decorated bolster wearing a white turban enhanced by two tall plumes issuing from bejewelled sockets. His green and gold-brocade caftan has large, gold globular buttons down the front. The garment is secured by a jewel-studded gold belt, which incorporates three cusped, circular units at the front. A bejeweled dagger handle can be seen protruding from Sultan Ahmed’s belt on the right. He wears a red-orange overcoat with small gold buttons down the front; the coat is lined with ermine. A gold-coloured slipper protrudes from underneath his garments. In his left hand, the fifth finger of which is enhanced by a gold ring with circular stone, Sultan Ahmed holds the *mandil*, a ceremonial handkerchief with gold detailing. In his right hand he holds a volume of poetry bound in the so-called *sefine* format (with the vertically oriented pages bound at the top, narrow end). The gilt binding shows a delicately drawn, central medallion enclosed within an elongated, arched cartouche.  
Above the portrait of the sultan runs a cursive inscription contained within two elongated cusped cartouches, written in white against a blue background and enhanced by white floral detailing, it reads: ‘Hasrat Sultan Ahmad \[Ahmed\] ibn Sultan Muhammad \[Mehmed\] Khan’. A tiny inscription on the lower left-hand side of the work names the painter ‘al-fakir Süleyman’. The portrait is surrounded by a green inner frame and an orange outer frame with additional ruled frames in blue, red, gold and green in between and around the outside of the outer border.

This miniature painting shows the Ottoman Sultan Ahmed I, best known as the founder of the Blue Mosque in Istanbul. It has been suggested that this portrait was executed in the court workshops of the Topkapı Saray in Istanbul during the early AH 11th / AD 17th century.
dates: Hegira first half of the 11th century / AD first half of the 17th century
keywords: Ahmed I; Al-fakir Suleyman

es.name: Retrato del Sultán otomano Ahmed I
description:
Retrato en aguada sobre papel del sultán otomano Ahmed I (r. 1012-1026 / 1603-1617) que formó parte de un álbum de miniaturas otomanas y persas, recopilado aparentemente en el siglo XII / XVIII. El joven gobernante, conocido como el fundador de la Mezquita Azul de Estambul, aparece sentado en un gran trono ricamente decorado bajo un arco lobulado apuntado, recostado sobre un almohadón bordado. Va tocado con un turbante blanco realzado con dos enjoyados alfileres rematados con plumas y viste un caftán verde brocado en oro con botones globulares también de oro, ceñido por un cinturón de oro con piedras engarzadas del que sobresale la empuñadura de una daga, también con piedras preciosas. Se cubre con un sobretodo naranja con el borde de armiño. El único pie visible va calzado con una babucha dorada. En el dedo meñique de la mano izquierda lleva un anillo de oro con una piedra circular; con esa misma mano sostiene el *mandil*, pañuelo ceremonial adornado con detalles en oro. En la mano derecha sujeta un volumen de poesía en formato *sefine*, es decir con páginas escritas verticalmente y cosido por el margen superior. En la decoración de la encuadernación se aprecia el delicado dibujo de un medallón enmarcado por un cartucho alargado y arqueado.  
En los dos largos cartuchos lobulados situados encima del retrato se lee una inscripción cursiva en letra blanca sobre fondo azul y adornada con detalles florales: “Hasrat Sultan Ahmad \[Ahmed\] ibn Sultan Muhammad \[Mehmed\] Jan”. Una inscripción más pequeña en el ángulo inferior izquierda nos da el nombre del pintor: “al-fakir Suleyman”.  
El retrato está rodeado de una sucesión de marcos de color verde, rojo, naranja, dorado y azul.

Esta miniatura es un retrato del sultán otomano Ahmed I, conocido como el fundador de la Mezquita Azul de Estambul. Se cree que este retrato se pintó a principios del siglo XI / XVII en los talleres de la corte del palacio Topkapi de Estambul.
dates: Primera mitad del siglo XI de la Hégira / XVII d. C.
keywords: Ahmed I; al-fakir Suleyman

fr.name: Portrait du sultan ottoman Ahmed Ier.
description:
Cette miniature exécutée à la gouache sur papier est un portrait du sultan Ahmet Ier (r. 1012-1026 H / 1603-1617 J.-C.) qui faisait jadis partie d'un album contenant des miniatures turques et perses, sans doute assemblé au XIIe siècle H (XVIIIe siècle J.-C.). Le jeune souverain, à qui l'on doit la Mosquée bleue d'Istanbul, est assis sur un important trône richement décoré et placé sous une arche lobée. Il s'appuie sur un luxueux traversin et porte un turban à deux grandes plumes jaillissant de manchons ornés de pierres précieuses. Sa robe est fermée par une ceinture dorée piquetée de joyaux et comportant sur le devant trois médaillons circulaires lobés. À droite, une poignée de dague sertie de pierres précieuses sort de sa ceinture. Il est revêtu d'un manteau doublé d'hermine à petits boutons d'or sur le devant. Une babouche de couleur or pointe sous ses vêtements. Dans sa main gauche, dont le cinquième doigt porte un anneau d'or à pierre ronde, il tient le *mandil*, mouchoir de cérémonie à décor de fils d'or. Dans sa main droite se trouve un volume de poésie de format *sefine* (pages orientées verticalement, reliées par le haut). La reliure dorée comporte un médaillon central délicatement dessiné dans un cartouche arqué allongé.  
Au-dessus du portrait, dans deux longs cartouches lobés, court une inscription blanche sur fond bleu et rehaussée d'un décor floral blanc, qui se lit “Hasrat Sultan Ahmad ibn Sultan Muhammad Khan”. Une petite inscription dans la partie inférieure gauche de l'œuvre donne le nom du peintre, “al-fakir Suleyman”. Le portrait est entouré d'une succession de bordures de couleur bleue, rouge, or et verte.

Miniature peinte représentant le sultan ottoman Ahmed Ier, plus connu comme le fondateur de la Mosquée bleue d’Istanbul. Ce portrait a pu être exécuté dans les ateliers de la cour du palais de Topkapı à Istanbul au début du XIe siècle H (XVIIe siècle J.-C.).
dates: Première moitié du XIe siècle de l’Hégire (première moitié du XVIIe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: Ahmed Ier ; al-fakir Suleyman

ar.name: سيف فارس.
description:
سيفٌ مكونٌ من مقبضٍ ونصل حديدي ذي حدَّين وثلم قليل الوضوح حتى الوسط، رُسِمت عليه دمغة محاطة بنجمتين مكونتين من أربعة فروع، ويُحتمل أنها – الدمغة - نصرية، لكن هويتها غير معروفة. يتشكل المقبض المصنوع من النحاس الأصفر من تُفيحَة دائرية بدوائر جرى إبرازها من الوجه والظهر؛ ويعلو المقبضَ زرٌّ، ويتسعُ في الوسط. الواقية مُفرغة؛ والمقطع العلوي متعدد الفصوص؛ كما تقدم الأذرع المنتهية على شكل معقوف دوائرَ مُخرَّمة على وجهها الخارجي. أُنجِزَت الزخرفةُ المخرمةُ بشرائط دائرية مجدولة، تتراكبُ مع شرائط أخرى طولانية وعرضانية تتضمن زخارف كتابية تشير إلى الله. أما الفضاءات الفارغة فأُشغِلت بزخارف نباتية على المقبض، وسعيفات نخيلية على الواقية؛ في حين تتشكل خلفيةَ المجموعة من خطوط صغيرة مائلة مُطعمة بالذهب. واعتماداً على الدوائر غير المكتملة المزينة لأذرع الواقية، فإن الغمد الذي فُقِد في فترة غير مُحددة، كان يبدي الزخرفة نفسها.  
وبالرغم من أنه لم يصلنا إلا القليل من الأسلحة الأندلسية، فإنه يجب أن نستخرج من بينها مجموعة من السيوف النصرية المعروفة تحت تسمية "سيوف الفرسان"؛ والتي تكمن أهميتها إلى حد كبير في أصالة مقابضها، دون نموذج معروف عن تلك الفترة، وفي كونها نتاج نصري لأسلحة البذخ فقط.  
إن هذه القطعة، التي تبقى تحفة كمالية، تنتمي إلى فصيلة تفتقر زخرفتَها، المعتمدةَ على النحاس الأصفر والترخيم، إلى الغنى الذي يميز سيوفاً فرسانية أخرى مشغولة من العاج أو من المينا.

نسمي "خينيتا" السيف الذي يتميز بواقية ملتوية جدا. يُزيَّنُ المقبضُ الذي يُصنعُ بشكل عام من معدن نفيس بزخارف غنية، مما يرفع من قيمته كدلالة على المكانة الاجتماعية. وبالرغم من بقائها كقطعة كمالية، فإن هذه القطعة ذات المقبض المصنوع من النحاس الأصفر المطعم تفتقد إلى اللمعان مقارنة مع سيوف أخرى من صنف "الخينيتاس".
keywords: غرناطة؛ سلاح؛ نصريون.
materials: صلب؛ نحاس أصفر؛ ذهب؛ فضة؛ انسكاب؛ تخريم؛ تطعيم.

en.name: *Jineta* Sword.
description:
Sword consisting of a steel hilt and double-edged blade with a superficial axial groove up to the middle, bearing its hallmark beside two four-pointed stars, probably Nasrid but of unknown origin. The hilt, made of brass, is formed by a spherical pommel with obverse and reverse circles, with a button at the end; a hilt that widens in the middle; a hollow quillon (arms of cross guard) with a poly-lobed upper profile and arms finished in the shape of a hook with fretwork circles on the outside. The niello decoration consists of intertwined circular bands that are superimposed on other longitudinal and traversal bands with inscriptions alluding to God. The intermediate spaces are filled with plant arabesques on the hilt and palmettes on the quillon. Small oblique damascene lines in gold make up the background of the whole piece. The scabbard, lost at an unknown time, would have had the same decoration, judging by the unfinished circles on the arms of the quillon.  
Surviving Andalusian armaments are rare and a set of Nasrid swords known as *jinetas* is particularly noteworthy. Their importance lies as much in the originality of their hilts, without equal in the period, as in the fact of being a genuine Nasrid production of luxury arms. This piece, while still a sumptuary object, belongs to a variety whose decoration, based in brass and niello, lacks the richness that characterises other *jineta* swords made of ivory or enamel.

Swords with horseshoe-shaped quillons were known as *jineta* swords. The hilts were usually made of precious metals and richly decorated, accentuating their value as symbols of prestige. This piece, with its brass and niello hilt, was a luxury item but is not as rich as other *jineta* swords.
keywords: Weapon; Nasrids; Granada; weaponry; arms; armours; military object
materials: Steel, brass, gold, silver; cast, nielloed, damascene.

es.name: Espada jineta.
description:
Espada compuesta de empuñadura y hoja de acero de doble filo con canal axial no muy acusado hasta la mitad, sobre el que se dispone la marca flanqueada por dos estrellas de cuatro puntas, probablemente nazarí pero de identidad desconocida. La empuñadura, de azófar, está formada por: un pomo esférico con círculos realzados en anverso y reverso, y un botón como remate; un puño ensanchado en el centro; un arriaz hueco, con perfil superior polilobulado y brazos rematados en forma de gancho con círculos calados en su parte externa. La decoración, nielada, está realizada con bandas circulares entrelazadas que se superponen a otras bandas longitudinales y trasversales con inscripciones alusivas a Dios. Los espacios intermedios se llenan con ataurique en el puño y con palmetas en el arriaz. Pequeñas líneas oblicuas damasquinadas en oro constituyen el fondo del conjunto. La vaina, perdida en época incierta, debió de contener la misma decoración, a juzgar por los círculos inacabados de los brazos del arriaz.  
  
Aunque el armamento andalusí conservado es muy escaso, hay que destacar un conjunto de espadas nazaríes conocidas como “jinetas”. Su importancia radica tanto en la originalidad de sus empuñaduras, sin parangón en la época, como en el hecho de ser una producción genuinamente nazarí de armas de lujo. Esta pieza, sin dejar de ser un objeto suntuario, pertenece a una variante cuya decoración, basada en el azófar y el nielado, carece de la riqueza que caracteriza a otras espadas jinetas, realizadas en marfil o esmalte.

Se denomina “jineta” a la espada con arriaz ultra-semicircular. Suele tener empuñadura de metales preciosos y rica decoración, lo cual acentúa su valor como signo de prestigio. Esta pieza de empuñadura de azófar y nielada, sin dejar de ser suntuaria, carece de la riqueza de otras espadas jinetas.
keywords: arma; nazaríes; Granada
materials: Acero, azófar, oro, plata; fundición, nielado, damasquinado.

fr.name: Épée.
description:
Épée composée d'une poignée et d'une lame de fer à double tranchant à gouttière assez peu accusée jusqu'au milieu, sur laquelle est disposée la marque flanquée de deux étoiles à quatre branches, probablement nasride mais à l'identité inconnue. La poignée, en cuivre jaune, est formée d'un pommeau sphérique avec des cercles rehaussés à l'avers et à l'envers, et surmontée d'un bouton ; elle s'élargit au centre. La garde est creuse, le profil supérieur est polylobé et les bras terminés en forme de crochets présentent des cercles ajourés sur leur face externe. La décoration, niellée, est réalisée avec des bandes circulaires entrelacées qui se superposent à d'autres bandes longitudinales et transversales comportant des inscriptions faisant allusion à Dieu. Les espaces intersticiels sont meublés d'atauriques sur la poignée et de palmettes sur la garde. De petites lignes obliques, damasquinées d'or, constituent le fond de l'ensemble. La gaine, perdue à une époque indéterminée, devait présenter la même décoration, si l'on en juge par les cercles inachevés des bras de la garde.  
Bien que peu d'armes andalouses soient parvenues jusqu'à nous, il faut en détacher un ensemble d'épées nasrides connues sous l'appellation d'épées *jinetas*. Leur importance réside tant dans l'originalité de leurs poignées, sans modèle connu à l'époque, que dans le fait qu'elles sont une production purement nasride d'armes de luxe.  
Tout en restant un objet somptuaire, cette pièce appartient à une variante dont la décoration, fondée sur le cuivre jaune et sur le niellage, manque de la richesse qui caractérise d'autres “épées cavalières” en ivoire ou en émail.

On appelle *jineta* l'épée à la garde extrêmement recourbée. Sa poignée, généralement en métal précieux, est rehaussée de riches décorations, ce qui renforce sa valeur comme signe de prestige. Cette pièce à poignée en cuivre jaune et nielle, tout en restant un objet somptuaire, manque d'éclat par rapport à d'autres épées *jinetas.*
keywords: arme ; Nasride ; Grenade
materials: Acier, cuivre jaune, or, argent ; coulage, niellage, damasquinage.

de.name: Neues Schloss Schleißheim und Schloss Lustheim
description:
Das gen Westen achsial auf das Alte Schloss Schleißheim ausgerichtete Schloss Lustheim im Stil einer italienischen Villa besitzt einen zentralen rechteckigen Festsaal, vorspringende Seitenflügel mit Wohnräumen sowie ein Belvedere über dem Mitteltrakt. Von der ursprünglich reichen und farbigen Innenausstattung ist neben den Fresken und Gemälden nicht viel erhalten. Entsprechend der Konzeption als Jagdschloss zeigen die Deckenfresken den Diana-Mythos, von denen die Darstellung der Erhebung Dianas zur Göttin der Jagd im Festsaal, mit weiteren mythologischen Szenen und Scheinarchitektur in den Randzonen, die imposanteste ist. Heute befindet sich in Schloss Lustheim eine große Sammlung Meißner Porzellans.  
Das imposante Neue Schloss, das offensichtlich mit Versailles und Schönbrunn in Konkurrenz tritt, beherbergt im Sinne der sich ausweitenden Machtansprüche Max Emanuels zahlreiche prächtige Wohn- und Festräume und beeindruckt bereits mit seiner pompösen Fassade im römischen Barockstil.

Die imposante Sommerresidenz des bayerischen Kurfürsten Max II. Emanuel zählt zu den bedeutendsten profanen Barockbauten Bayerns und umfasst das Alte und Neue Schloss Schleißheim, das Jagdschloss Lustheim, sowie Park- und Kanalanlagen. In Konkurrenz zu Versailles und Schönbrunn ließ der Kurfürst ein prächtig ausgestattetes Schloss erbauen und scheute sich trotz der damals finanziell und politisch schwierigen Lage nicht, namhafte Künstler hinzuzuziehen. Zu den Höhepunkten gehören der Weiße Saal oder die Große Galerie, welche im Sinne ihres Erbauers Meisterwerke der europäischen Barockmalerei zeigt.
artist: Bayerische Kurfürsten: Maximilian II. Emanuel (reg. 1680-1726); Karl Albrecht (reg. 1726-45); Max III. Joseph (reg. 1745-1777)
history:
Der Baubeginn Lustheims erfolgte 1684 unter Kurfürst Max II. Emanuel, wohl im Hinblick auf seine Hochzeit mit der Kaisertochter Maria Antonia 1685. Vollendet wurde der Bau 1689. Während der Errichtung Lustheims fertigte Enrico Zuccalli Entwürfe für das Neue Schloss Schleißheim; nach Um- und Neuplanungen erfolgte 1701 die Grundsteinlegung.  
1704 wurden die Bauarbeiten aufgrund des Spanischen Erbfolgekrieges unterbrochen. Nach der Rückkehr Max Emanuels aus dem Exil 1715 begann der neue Hofbaumeister Joseph Effner 1719 mit der Innenausstattung nach französischem Vorbild. Der von Enrico Zuccalli entworfene neuartige Typus des Zeremonialtreppenhauses wurde beibehalten. Da sich die Finanzlage zunehmend verschlechterte, musste man die Planungen einschränken. Nach dem Tod Max Emanuels 1726 wurde der Bau nie vollendet.
keywords: Residenz; Stuck; Festsaal; Zeremonialtreppenhaus; Deckenmalerei; Galerie; Schloss; Schlosspark

en.name: New Schleissheim Palace and Lustheim Palace
description:
Lustheim Palace, designed in the style of an Italian villa and axially aligned with the Old Palace in a westward direction, has a rectangular ballroom, protruding side-wings with residential rooms, as well as a belvedere above the central wing. The frescos and paintings are all that remain of the originally richly furnished and colourfully decorated interior. According to the concept of a hunting residence, the myth of Diana is illustrated in a number of the ceiling frescos. Her elevation to goddess of the hunt is illustrated on the ceiling of the Banqueting Hall, complemented by other mythological scenes related to her, and surrounded by impressive illusionary architectural features. Today the palace holds a large collection of Meissen porcelain.  
The New Palace was designed to provoke comparison with Versailles and Schönbrunn Palace, incorporating numerous splendid residential rooms and festivity halls, and with its pompous Roman Baroque façade, corresponding to Max Emanuel’s ever-growing claim to power.

The impressive summer residence of Elector Max II Emanuel ranks among Bavaria’s major secular Baroque buildings incorporating the Old and New Schleissheim Palace, the hunting seat Lustheim, as well as the palace park and canal system. Competing against Versailles, near Paris, and Schönbrunn Palace, near Vienna, the Elector ordered the construction of a sumptuously decorated palace for which he commissioned famous artists, despite the difficult financial and political situation at that time. Among the highlights are the Great Hall and the Great Gallery. In the latter, according to the patron’s intentions, are displayed masterpieces of European Baroque painting.
type: Secular architecture (palace, hunting seat and summer residence)
artist: Bavarian Electors: Maximilian II Emanuel (gov. 1680–1726); Karl Albrecht (gov. 1726–1725); Max III Joseph (gov. 1745–1777)

Lustheim Palace architecture: Enrico Zuccalli (c. 1642–1724); frescos: Antonio Bernardi \[n.d.\], Francesco Rosa \[n.d.\], Giovanni Antonio Trubillo (d. 1721), Johann Anton Gumpp (1654–1719)  
New Schleissheim Palace architecture: Enrico Zuccalli (c. 1642–1724), Joseph Effner (1687–1745); stuccowork: Johann Baptist Zimmermann (1680–1758), Charles Dubut (c. 1687–1742), Giuseppe Volpini (d. 1729); fresco and fireplace painting: Jacopo Amigoni (c. 1682–1752), Thomas Christian Wink (1738–1797); joinery/ornamental carving: Johann Adam Pichler (c. 1690–1761); battle-scene paintings: Joachim Beich (1665–1748)
history:
Construction of Lustheim Palace began in 1684 under Bavarian Elector Max II Emanuel probably in anticipation of his marriage to the Emperor’s daughter, Maria Antonia, in 1685. The structure was complete by 1689. During construction of Lustheim Palace, Enrico Zuccalli began drawing the plans for the New Palace, and after redesign, the cornerstone was put in place in 1701.  
Building work stopped briefly in 1704 because of the War of the Spanish Succession. After Max Emanuel’s return from exile in 1715, the new court architect, Joseph Effner, began decoration of the interior in 1719 following French models. Enrico Zuccalli’s design for a novel type of ceremonial staircase was maintained, but then, as the financial situation worsened, plans had to be restrained. The construction was never completed following the death of Bavarian Elector Max II Emanuel in 1726.
keywords: Mythology; Odysseus; Calypso; Diana; hunting residence; palace; summer residence; illusionary architectural features; *trompe-l’oeil*; fresco; stucco; marble; ballroom; War of the Spanish Succession
partner: University of Munich, Institute of Art History

en.name: *St. Sebastian Tended by Pious Women*
description:
The painting is first documented in the Borghese collection in 1650 although it is possible Cardinal Scipione acquired it directly during the artist's short stay in Rome (1624–1625) shortly before his early death on his return home.  
The painting shows a subject particularly common in the early 12th century: a pious women removing the arrows that martyred St. Sebastian and tending his wounds. According to a hagiographic account, Sebastian, an officer in Emperor Diocletian's Praetorian Guard who had converted to Christianity, was executed by archers who left him for dead. Tended by Saint Irene and her assistant, he returned to the Emperor with a new profession of faith, and was beaten to death with a club and his body left in the Cloaca Maxima.  
The cult of this saint reached its height thanks to the writings of Cesare Baronio in the late 16th century, and his iconography included elements similar to that of Christ. In 1607, Scipione Borghese began the restoration of the old Paleo-Christian Basilica of St. Sebastian outside the town walls on the Via Appia as part of a building policy promoted by the Counter-Reformation that encouraged a revival of the cult of martyrdom. He entrusted the commission to Flaminio Ponzio, who was also the architect for the Villa Borghese.  
The painting shows sentimentality in the face of the saint that inspires compassion in the viewer. The pose of the body is inspired by statues, and the twisting motion resembles one of the most well known ancient sculptures in Rome at that time, the *Lacoonte*.  
Rustici handled this subject on several occasions. In his skilful modulation of light on the body of the martyr he demonstrates his knowledge of the innovations of Caravaggesque painting, although he did not adhere to them completely, accentuating the suggestion of the hagiographic account with the expressiveness of Bolognese painting.

St. Sebastian’s iconography is often associated with that of Christ. At the beginning of the 17th century the martyr is frequently represented at the moment he is found by the noblewoman, Irene, who takes care of him, in this way arousing the spectator’s feelings of compassion.  
The martyr is said to be buried in the early Christian basilica of St. Sebastian on the Via Appia, which was restored by Cardinal Scipione Borghese.
keywords: Christian themes; Counter-Reformation; cult of martyrdom; movement; classical model; anatomy; ancient art

it.name: *San Sebastiano curato dalle pie donne*
description:
Il dipinto è documentato nella collezione Borghese a partire dal 1650, ma è possibile che il cardinale Scipione l'abbia acquistato direttamente durante il breve soggiorno romano dell'artista (1624-25), di poco antecedente alla precoce morte sopraggiunta al rientro in patria. Il dipinto raffigura un soggetto particolarmente diffuso all'inizio del XVII secolo: quello delle pie donne che estraggono le frecce del martirio a San Sebastiano, curandone le ferite. Secondo il racconto agiografico Sebastiano, ufficiale della guardia pretoria dell'imperatore Diocleziano, convertitosi al Cristianesimo, fu giustiziato dagli arceri, che lo abbandonarono  credendolo morto. Curato da Sant'Irene e dalla sua aiutante, si ripresentò all'imperatore rinnovando la sua professione di fede. Giustiziato a bastonate, fu abbandonato nei pressi della Cloaca Massima. Il culto di questo santo era stato riportato in auge dagli scritti di Cesare Baronio alla fine del sec. XVI e la sua iconografia presentava elementi che lo accostavano a quella di Cristo. Nel 1607 Scipione Borghese, secondo una politica edilizia promossa dalla Controriforma che privilegiava il ritorno al culto dei martiri, aveva intrapreso il restauro dell'antica basilica paleocristiana di San Sebastiano fuori le mura sulla via Appia, affidandolo a Flaminio Ponzio, lo stesso architetto di Villa Borghese.  
Il dipinto evidenzia nel volto del santo il patetismo capace di indurre la compassionevole partecipazione dello spettatore. La posa del corpo è ispirata a modelli statuari e ricorda, nella torsione, una delle sculture antiche allora più celebrate a Roma, il Lacoonte.  Nella sapiente modulazione della luce sul corpo del martire, Rustici, che eseguì più versioni dello stesso soggetto, dimostra di conoscere le novità della pittura caravaggesca, cui non aderisce tuttavia completamente, accentuando la suggestione del racconto agiografico con l'espressività della pittura bolognese.

L’iconografia di San Sebastiano è spesso associata a quella di Cristo. All'inizio del XVII secolo il martire è spesso rappresentato nel momento in cui viene trovato dalla nobildonna Irene, che si prende cura di lui, suscitando in questo modo sentimenti di compassione nello spettatore.  
Il martire è sepolto nella basilica paleocristiana di San Sebastiano sulla Via Appia, che fu fatta restaurare dal cardinale Scipione Borghese.
keywords: Tematiche cristiane; Controriforma; culto del martirio; movimento; modello classico; anatomia; arte antica
