en.name: Maghrebi *rab’a*.
description:
A *rab’a*, a Qur'anic manuscript divided into 30 parts, each of which has an independent binding. The *rab’a* was preserved in a square wooden box covered on the outside with leather and embellished by four embossed decorative bands that incorporate geometric patterns outlined with silver thread. In between the four bands are three silver belts which reach from the back to the front of the box to support it. Each belt is decorated with three star-like shapes made from silver and overlaid with blue enamel. In all, the box bears 10 decorative forms in the same style; on the four corners of the box, for example, there are geometric shapes inlaid with mother-of-pearl and red and blue enamel.  
The bindings of all 30 parts are made from embossed red leather, with both the front and back embellished with ornamentation and text, which is identical on all the volumes. On each cover there are four inscription bands that form a square, and which are encircled by silver thread. The text is gilded, and in the middle of each front cover there is a silver-braided circle. Within the circle in gilded text is a Chapter from the Qur'an (14: 52), which tells the story of Ibrahim (Abraham). It reads: “Here is a message for mankind. Let them take warning there from, and let them know that he is (no other than) One God. Let men of understanding take heed”.On the back cover there is another quote from the Qur'an “al-Baqara” (“the Cow”, 2: 181), which reads: “If anyone changes the bequest after hearing it. The guilt shall be on those who make the change. For Allah hears and knows (All things)”.  
Each part of the *rab'a* begins with two identical illuminated panels that differ in design from one volume to the next. Most of the square-shaped panels are surrounded by broad illuminated frames and contain decoration consisting of lines, circles and squares painted in more than one colour, but predominantly in gold. The *rab'a* is written in Maghrebi-style script with black ink, with five lines to each page. Verses are divided from each other by the word “verse” written in gold and surrounded by three circles. The *waqf* charter of the *rab'a,* written in an illuminated *kufic* script within a square that is also illuminated, is on the last two pages of each volume.

A *rab’a*, a Qur’anic manuscript in 30 parts, preserved in a wooden box covered with leather and decorated with silver bands. The texts are in Maghrebi *kufic* script, written with saffron water on gazelle parchment. The *rab’a* is filled with decorative motifs, colours and illumination. This is one of three *rab’a* written for Mecca, Medina and Jerusalem; only the last copy has come down to us.
holder: Islamic Museum, al-Aqsa Mosque / al-Haram al-Sharif.
keywords: Abu al-Hasan al-Marini; illumination; kufic script; Maghrebi script; parchment; Qur’an; mashaf; religious manuscript
materials: Black ink on gazelle parchment; binding of illuminated leather.

es.name: *Rab’a* magrebí.
description:
*Rab´a*, Corán manuscrito dividido en treinta partes, cada una de las cuales está encuadernada de manera independiente. Se guardaba en una caja de madera cuadrada forrada por fuera de cuero repujado con cuatro cenefas decorativas compuestas por diseños geométricos silueteados con hilo de plata. Entre las cuatro cenefas hay tres cinturones de plata que sujetan la caja de atrás adelante. Cada uno está decorado con tres estrellas de plata esmaltadas en azul. En total, la caja consta de diez adornos del mismo estilo; en las cuatro esquinas, por ejemplo, hay formas geométricas decoradas con incrustaciones de nácar y esmalte rojo y azul.  
Las encuadernaciones de las treinta partes son de cuero rojo repujado, decorado con motivos ornamentales y un texto que es idéntico en todas. Las cubiertas presentan cuatro bandas de inscripciones que forman un cuadrado, rodeadas de una línea en plata. En el centro de cada portada se aprecia un círculo de hilo de plata trenzado. En el interior de este círculo hay un texto dorado que reproduce un fragmento del Corán (14:52) que narra la historia de Ibrahim (Abraham): “He aquí un mensaje para la humanidad. Que estén avisados y que sepan que sólo hay un único Dios. Que los hombres sensatos presten oídos”. La contraportada está decorada con una cita de la sura “La vaca” (2:181): “Si alguien modifica su legado tras oírlo, la culpa será de quienes hagan el cambio. Porque Alá lo oye y lo sabe \[todo\]”.  
Cada parte de la *rab'a* comienza con dos paneles iluminados idénticos que varían de un volumen a otro. La mayoría de estos paneles cuadrados poseen anchos marcos iluminados y están decorados con líneas, círculos y cuadrados pintados de varios colores, pero sobre todo de dorado. El manuscrito está escrito con tinta negra en letra de estilo magrebí, con cinco renglones por página. Los versículos están separados unos de otros por la palabra “aleya”, escrita en oro y rodeada de tres círculos. La escritura del *waqf* de este Corán, escrita en letra cúfica iluminada en el interior de un cuadrado también iluminado, ocupa las dos últimas páginas del volumen.

Manuscrito coránico dividido en treinta partes, conservado dentro de una caja de madera, recubierta de cuero y decorada con bandas de plata. Los textos están escritos en letra magrebí, cúfica. Se utilizó agua de azafrán sobre pergamino de gacela. El manuscrito incluye motivos decorativos, varios colores e iluminación. Es una de las tres *ra’ba* escritas para La Meca, Medina y Jerusalén, de las que sólo conservamos esta copia.
keywords: Abu al-Hasan al-Marini; iluminación; escritura cúfica; escritura magrebí; pergamino; Corán; mashaf.
materials: Tinta negra sobre pergamino de gacela; encuadernación de cuero iluminado.
tags: Tinta negra sobre pergamino de gacela
partner: Museo islámico en la mezquita de Al-Aqsa

fr.name: Maghrebi rab’a.
description:
*Rab'a*, Coran manuscrit divisé en trente parties, chacune dotée d'une reliure indépendante. L'ensemble était conservé dans un coffret en bois carré gainé de cuir et orné de quatre bandeaux décoratifs estampés à motifs géométriques rehaussés de fils d'argent et séparés par quatre brides d'argent cerclant le coffret. Chacune de ces reliures est ornée de trois étoiles d'argent à décor d'émail bleu. Au total, le coffret est orné de dix éléments décoratifs de même type, dont quatre aux angles, incrustés de nacre et décorés à l'émail bleu et rouge.  
Les reliures de ces trente parties sont en cuir estampé rouge, dont les plats recto et verso sont décorés d'ornements et de textes identiques sur tous les volumes. Sur chaque couverture figurent quatre inscriptions disposées en carré, entourées d'un filet d'argent. Le texte est doré. Le centre de chaque couverture est marqué par un cercle en tresse argentée. à l'intérieur figure le texte à l'encre d'or d'une sourate du Coran (XIV, 52) sur l'histoire d'Ibrahim (Abraham), qui se lit : “Tel est l'avis adressé aux hommes. Qu'ils y puisent leurs enseignements et sachent que Dieu est Un, et que les hommes de sens y réfléchissent.” Sur le dos de couverture figure une autre citation extraite de la sourate “al-Baqara” (La vache, II, 181) : “Celui qui, après avoir entendu les dispositions du testament au moment de sa mort, les aura dénaturées, commet un crime. Dieu voit et entend tout.”  
Chaque partie du *rab'a* débute par deux cartouches dont les enluminures sont identiques mais de forme différente sur chaque volume. La plupart des cartouches carrés sont entourés d'un important cadre enluminé à décor de lignes, de cercles et de carrés peints de plusieurs couleurs, mais à dominante dorée. Le texte est rédigé en style maghrébin à l'encre noire, chaque page contenant cinq lignes. Les versets sont séparés les uns des autres par le mot de “verset” écrit à l'or et entouré de trois cercles. La charte *waqf* en écriture coufique enluminée, à l'intérieur d'un carré également enluminé, figure sur les deux dernières pages de chaque volume.

*Ra’ba*, coran manuscrit divisé en 30 parties, conservé dans un coffre en bois gainé de cuir et orné de bandeaux d’argent. Les textes sont rédigés en style coufique maghrébin, écrits à l’eau de safran sur parchemin de gazelle. Ce rab’a est couvert de motifs décoratifs, de couleurs et d’enluminures. C’est l’un des trois corans écrits pour la Mecque, Médine et Jérusalem ; seule la dernière copie nous est parvenue.
holder: Musée islamique, mosquée al-Aqsa / Haram al-Charif.
keywords: Abou al-Hasan al-Marini ; enluminures ; écriture coufique ; écriture maghrébine ; parchemins ; Coran
materials: Encre noire sur parchemin de gazelle ; reliure en cuir enluminé.
tags: Encre noire sur parchemin de gazelle

en.name: Amulet
description: Tear-shaped pendant with a silver openwork border of twisted wire and granulation. It is inscribed on both sides with Arabic repoussé invocations and Qur’anic texts. The invocations in *thuluth* script on the scrolling ground at the centre are surrounded by epigraphic bands with verses in *naskhi* calligraphy: ‘*Ma sha’ Allah!*’ (‘God willing’) is encircled by the verses of Sura CXIII (*Al-Falaq*/ *The Daybreak*) and ‘*Ya Hafiz!*’ (‘O Preserver!’), by the verses of Sura CXIV (*Al-Nas* / *Mankind*). These last two chapters of the Qur’an, very short and intensely evocative, referred to as *al-mu‘awwidhatan* (the two protecting ones), appear quite frequently on amulets.
holder: The National Museum of Art of Romania
keywords: Amulet
partner: National Museum of Art of Romania

en.name: Parish Church of St. Michael, Osijek
description: The ground plan and architectonics of the Church of St. Michael consist of a cross-vaulted nave flanked by two pairs of barrel-vaulted chapels from which a somewhat narrower chancel ending in a polygon continues. The form of the sanctuary and the way it connects with the nave indicates that the intention was a more simple church building. However, during the course of building, a skilled, Central European architect added the side chapels, and the church's stylistic expression changed from Early to High Baroque. The construction of the wall columns in the nave – *Wandpfeiler* – which while dividing off the chapels also support the vault, was a concept broadly accepted in Early Baroque Central European architecture, particularly in Jesuit buildings. However, when the dimensions of the chapels increased – as they were in Osijek – there was space to place the altars below the windows (and not alongside the wall columns) in a typically High Baroque manner. The introduction of transverse axes enhanced the dynamics of the space. In accordance with this tradition, the facade was also enriched with a pair of incorporated *campanile*s or bell towers, a device that was a re-interpretation of a model seen 100 years earlier in, for example, Jesuit churches in Vienna and Trnava, and in the unrealised plans for the towers of the Academy Church of St. Catherine in Zagreb. The bell towers offer a certain austerity, appropriate to a fortress city. With its stylistic and typological characteristics, the Jesuit Church in Osijek is unique to the area, showing parallels in contemporary Central European architecture including productions of the architectural Carlone family in Austria to the very distinctive Paulist church in the Habsburg part of Istria – in Sv Petar u Šumi.

Building began on the Jesuit Church of St. Michael in 1725. The church is distinctive for its facade with two bell towers (*campanile*s), a common feature from the Early Baroque period particularly in Jesuit architecture (churches in Vienna, Trnava and Leoben), and also envisaged for the Jesuit Academy Church of St. Catherine in Zagreb.  
The Church of St. Michael is, however, still notable, for it brought a new and innovative form of church architecture to the region, its interior marking the transition from the Early Baroque *Wandpfeiler* construction to the High Baroque. This transformation is marked by enlarged chapels between the wall columns and the placement of an altar below the window, bringing additional transverse axes into the longitudinal space of the nave.
type: Religious architecture: a High Baroque nave church with interior buttresses and side chapels
artist: Unknown architect; painters: Franz Xaver Wagenschon (1726–1790), workshop of Paulus Antonius Senser (c. 1718–1758)
history: The Jesuits arrived in Osijek immediately after the city's liberation from the Turks in 1687, at which time it became the main Habsburg redoubt for further offensives against the Ottoman Empire. The city's strategic importance saw a transformation in town planning: from 1712–1721 a Baroque city with wide streets and a central square was built, opening up a picturesque vision from the square onto another square where the Jesuit complex was situated, and where building began on the monumental Jesuit Church of St. Michael (a parish church) in 1725. The church was in use by 1734 and the bell towers erected in 1741–2; but works on the interior furnishing continued until the 1770s.
keywords: Osijek, Church of St. Michael, Society of Jesus, High Baroque, nave church with interior buttresses and side chapels faced with two bell towers

en.name: Workers of the steel company Fonderia Donato Bastanzetti (Arezzo, Italy)
Vase Carpet
description:
This splendid carpet is laid out with a floral design of surprising complexity, against a pink-red field. The overall design is a triple-plane lattice, composed of three independently-composed trellis grids of different colours: blue-black, thorny white and leafy blue. These three grid systems are not immediately apparent because of the grand scale of the multiple flowerheads and medallions along each trellis. Furthermore, “behind” the three trellis systems are flowering plants and shrubs, also distracting the eye. This ordered design is greatly enlivened by the wonderful detail and variety in the colourful flowers and plants. Towards the top of the central axis, the white trellis features a striped vase of flowers, also repeated in the lower borders as “half-vases”: this motif gives its name to the wider category of Vase Carpets. The upper border is missing, and the original carpet was certainly even longer.  
  
The carpet belongs to a well-known group generally attributed to Kirman in southeast Iran, and to the seventeenth century. These are referred to as “Vase technique” carpets, as they often include a vase motif in their complex lattice designs, but more uniformly, the group shares the same triple-weft technical structure. There are many examples of Kirman vase carpets (and fragments) in national collections across the world. This carpet was bought in 1897 from the estate of the British designer, poet, craftsman and socialist William Morris, who supported the South Kensington Museum (today the V&A) with collections advice over many years, and was a formidable influence on the institution. During his lifetime, Morris had kept this large carpet hanging lengthways on the wall of his home, with the top section overhanging from the ceiling rather like a medieval canopy. He enjoyed it as one of his household furnishing, but more specifically, the complex planar design must have pleased him as a designer.  
  
[V&A online catalogue link](http://collections.vam.ac.uk/item/O98834/carpet-unknown/)
keywords: Iran; Kerman; trellis; vase; lotus, lattice
materials:
Wool; knotted pile; cotton warps; cotton first and third wefts; silk second weft.  
Wool pile on cotton warp and triple weft of cotton, silk and cotton; depressed warps, asymmetrical knots open to the left.

ar.name: دير سانتا أورسولا (القديسة أورسيل).
description:
على الرغم من كل التحسينات والتعديلات التي خضع لها هذا الدير على مدى قرون، لازال يحتفظ بإبداعات هامة لعهد المدجنين، تتمثل في الكنيسة الأولية وفي السياج الديري. إن بصمة المدجنين بادية سلفاً من الخارج مع الصدر والحائطين المجاورين اللذين يطابقان، من الداخل، الخورُس القديم ومصلى القديس نيكولا دي طولينتينو. الصدر طليطلي النموذج، ويجب أن ينتمي إلى الثلث الأخير من القرن الرابع عشر، بالرغم من أن خاصياته تحيل على القرنين الثاني عشر والثالث عشر. وفي البناية الأولية، تم على الخصوص استعمال عَمارة من الآجر والحجر، عوض الآجر وحده، على شاكلة الاستعمال المميز للصدور السابقة؛ ونلحظ عليه مزيداً من أنواع الفتحات بالرغم من كون العقد المنكسر والمتجاوز لازال متداولاً، ويحمل فوقه عقداً آخر متعدد الفصوص. تمت زخرفة الجزء الأوسط من الصدر بترس من الحجارة يرجع إلى فيرنان ألفاريس دي طوليدو (ت. 1464)، الكونت الأول لألبا دي طورميس، وابن أخ المطران، دون جوتيير ألفاريس دي طوليدو (ت. 1445)، محاطٍ بأعلام تخلد أخذ هويسكار وهويلما.  
يقدم سور الدير خاصيات مشابهة؛ وبعضُ فتحات المدافع دائرية الشكل. ويمكن من الخارج، أن نرى الجرس ذا الفانوس مع عقدين متجاوزين ومنكسرين. ويقدم حائط الواجهة الرئيسية المشيدة من الآجر على جوانبه عقدين مصمتين مع تناوب فصوص مقعرة ومنكسرة، حسب التقليد الموحدي. يحتفظ باب الكنيسة الذي تم تغييره تغييراً كبيرا في جزئه العلوي بتقاطعات قناطر زخرفية من الآجر، أكثر تعقيداً من تلك المزينة لنماذج أخرى طليطلية. كما تتخذ السقوف المدجنة التي يمكن تأريخها في القرنين الرابع عشر والخامس عشر أشكالا مختلفة؛ وتبقى القطعة الأكثر بروزاً تُوخيل الموْهف الخارجي أو موْهف الكنيسة، الذي تمت زخرفته ب 16 تشبيكاً نجدها في إفريز الزليج، حيث تزيد عناقيدُ من المقرنصات المذهبة من جماليتها. تعرضت الزخرفة المدهونة لضرر أكبر، ومن المرجح أنها تنتمي إلى نهاية القرن الرابع عشر أو بداية القرن الخامس عشر. وقد كانت الكنيسة في الأصل مغطاة بسقف بديع ذي مسند ورباط ومزود بأوتار، وقد أعيدت تغطيتها اليوم بقبة باروكية. كما كان الصدر القديم المستند إلى البلاطة الرئيسية عبارة عن بناية مدجنة من الجص تعود إلى القرن الخامس عشر وسقف من الخشب لم يبق منه إلا بقايا جد صغيرة.

يحتفظ هذا الدير الذي يشكل أحد أقدم الأديرة في طليطلة، والمُعدَّل على طول القرون بأعمال مدجنة هامة: صدره المبني بعمارة مركبة مع قاعدة أفقية من الآجر، وهي الزينة النمطية للفن المدجن الطليطلي، ويبرز في موهف الكنيسة سقف ذو تشبيكات وعناقيد من المقرنصات المذهبة.
dynasty: فترة المدجنين؛ تأسس في القرن 13، المنشأة الرئيسية ترجع إلى القرن 14.
history: يعتبر هذا الدير الذي تسكنه طائفة من أمهات أغسطسية واحداً من أقدم الأديرة في طليطلة. ويبدو أن تكريسه للقديسة أورسيل مرتبط بالانتشار غير العادي لتقديس هذه القديسة التي كابدت مع أصحابها (11000 حسب الرواية المتوارثة) في كولن؛ وهو تكريس ليس له علاقة بالقديس أغسطس، ولكن كان له الوقع الكبير في طليطلة. ويعود أصل الطائفة إلى عام 1260 عندما تم البدء في بناء الصرح. وفي عام 1360، جرى توسيع هذا الأخير، وقام دييجو جونزاليث، رئيس شمامسة كالاترافا بتشييد الكنيسة.

en.name: Convent of Santa Úrsula.
description: Despite its transformation over the centuries, this convent still contains interesting Mudéjar works relating to the original church and the convent cloister. The Mudéjar influence is evident on the outside in the apse and the adjacent walls of the old chorus and the Chapel of St Nicholas of Tolentino. The typically Toledan apse must belong to the last third of the 14th century, although its characteristics relate to the 12th and 13th centuries. When initially constructed, masonry with string courses was used instead of simply bricks, as was common in existing apses. It has a greater number of openings, although it does retain the model of the pointed horseshoe arch surrounded by a poly-lobed arch. The central part of the apse is decorated with a magnificent stone shield belonging to Fernán Álvarez de Toledo (d. 1464), first Count of Alba de Tormes, nephew of Archbishop Gutierre Álvarez de Toledo (d. 1445), surrounded by flags in commemoration of the taking of Huescar and Huelma. The convent wall has similar characteristics. Some of the several openings are circular. From outside you can see the belfry with two pointed-horseshoe arches. The brick wall of the main façade has blind arches to the sides with alternating concave and pointed lobes, in the Almohad tradition. The door of the church, now significantly modified, has retained in its upper part a decorative brick arcade with crossing and interlinked arches more complex than other Toledan examples. The Mudéjar roof structures, datable to the 14th and 15th centuries, vary in form. The most noteworthy piece is the *taujel* ceiling of the outer sacristy or the church sacristy, which is decorated with 16-lazo knots that continue into the tile frieze. Honeycomb-work clusters further enhance its beauty. The painted decoration is in poor condition and it is only just possible to make out plant arabesques and loopholes with black dots on a white background, probably from the late 14th or early 15th centuries. The church was originally covered with a splendid collar-beam roof with tie beams, now covered by a baroque vault. The so-called 'old chorus', which backs on to the main nave, was also originally a Mudéjar construction with 15th-century plasterwork and a wooden ceiling of which practically nothing has survived.

Although it has changed over the centuries, this convent, which is one of the oldest in Toledo, has retained some interesting Mudéjar features: its masonry walls incorporate rows of bricks, a bond common in Mudéjar buildings in Toledo, and the sacristy has an interlaced ceiling structure with clusters of golden *muqarnas* (honeycomb-work).
dates: Founded in the 13th century; the main structure dates from the 14th century.
history: The convent, inhabited by a community of Augustine sisters, is one of the oldest in Toledo. The dedication to Saint Ursula appears to be linked to the extraordinary spread of veneration to the saint who, along with her female companions (11,000 of them, according to tradition), was martyred in Cologne. This dedication has nothing to do with St Augustine, but nonetheless had a profound effect in Toledo. The origin of the community dates back to 1260 when the building was started. It was extended in 1360 and Diego González, Archdeacon of Calatrava, built the church.

es.name: Convento de Santa Úrsula.
description: Este convento, trasformado a lo largo de los siglos, conserva aún, con todo, obras mudéjares de interés, correspondientes a la primitiva iglesia y a la clausura conventual. El mudejarismo se hace evidente ya en el exterior, con el ábside y los dos muros contiguos que corresponden interiormente al coro viejo y la capilla de San Nicolás de Tolentino. El ábside, típicamente toledano, debe de pertenecer al último tercio del siglo XIV, si bien sus caracteres remiten a los siglos XII y XIII. En su original construcción se empleó esencialmente mampostería con verdugadas de ladrillo, en vez de ladrillo solo, como era característico de los ábsides anteriores. Ostenta mayor número de vanos, si bien perdura el modelo de arco de herradura apuntado, cobijado por otro polilobulado. La parte central del ábside está decorada con un magnífico escudo de piedra, perteneciente a Fernán Álvarez de Toledo (m. 1464), primer Conde de Alba de Tormes, sobrino del Arzobispo D. Gutierre Álvarez de Toledo (m. 1445), rodeado de banderas, en recuerdo de la toma de Huéscar y Huelma. El muro del convento es de análogas características. Entre los diversos vanos, algunos son circulares. Desde fuera puede verse la espadaña, con dos arcos de herradura apuntados. El muro de la fachada principal, de ladrillo, presenta a los lados arcos ciegos con alternancia de lóbulos cóncavos y apuntados, de tradición almohade. La puerta de la iglesia, muy modificada, conserva en la zona alta una arquería decorativa en ladrillo, con arcos entrecruzados y enlazados, de mayor complejidad que otros ejemplares toledanos. Las armaduras mudéjares, fechables en los siglos XIV y XV, tienen distintas formas. La pieza más destacada es el taujel de la sacristía exterior o sacristía de la iglesia, decorado con lazo de dieciséis, que se continúa en el alicer. Realzan su belleza racimos de mocárabes dorados. De su decoración pictórica, en mal estado, apenas se aprecian atauriques y saetinos con puntos negros sobre fondo blanco. Probablemente pertenece a fines del siglo XIV o comienzos del XV. En su origen, la iglesia estaba cubierta por una espléndida armadura de par y nudillo, provista de vigas tirantes, hoy tapada por una bóveda barroca. El llamado “coro viejo”, adosado a la nave principal, también fue en origen una construcción mudéjar con yeserías del siglo XV y techumbre de madera, de las que solo quedan mínimos vestigios.

Aunque transformado a lo largo de los siglos, este convento, uno de los más antiguos de Toledo, conserva elementos mudéjares de interés: su ábside está construido en mampostería combinada con hiladas horizontales de ladrillo, paramento típico del mudéjar toledano; en la sacristía destaca la armadura de lacería con racimos de mocárabes dorados.
dates: Fundado en el siglo XIII, la obra principal es del siglo XIV.
history: Este convento, habitado por una comunidad de madres agustinas, es uno de los más antiguos de Toledo. La advocación a Santa úrsula parece vincularse a la extraordinaria difusión de la devoción a la santa que, junto con sus compañeras (11.000, según la tradición), sufrió martirio en Colonia; dicha advocación nada tiene que ver con san Agustín, pero sí tuvo amplia repercusión en Toledo. El origen de la comunidad se remonta a 1260, cuando se inició la construcción del edificio; en 1360 fue ampliado y Diego González, arcediano de Calatrava, levantó la iglesia.

fr.name: Couvent de Santa Úrsula (Sainte-Ursule).
description: Ce couvent, transformé au long des siècles, conserve encore, malgré tout, des œuvres mudéjares intéressantes correspondant à l'église primitive et à la clôture conventuelle. L'empreinte mudéjare est déjà évidente de l'extérieur avec l'abside et les deux murs contigus qui correspondent, à l'intérieur, au vieux chœur et à la chapelle Saint-Nicolas de Tolentino. L'abside, typiquement tolédane, doit appartenir au dernier tiers du XIVe, bien que ses caractéristiques renvoient aux XIIe et XIIIe siècles. Dans la construction d'origine, on employa essentiellement une maçonnerie de brique et pierre au lieu de la brique seule, comme c'était l'usage caractéristique des absides antérieures. On y observe davantage de types d'ouvertures, même si l'arc outrepassé brisé y perdure, surmonté par un autre arc polylobé. La partie centrale de l'abside est décorée d'un magnifique blason en pierre appartenant à Fernán Álvarez de Toledo (m. 1464), premier comte d'Alba de Tormes, neveu de l'archevêque Don Gutierre Álvarez de Toledo (m. 1445), entouré de drapeaux commémorant la prise de Huéscar et de Huelma. Le mur du couvent présente des caractéristiques analogues. Certaines des embrasures sont circulaires. De l'extérieur, on peut voir le clocher à lanternon avec deux arcs outrepassé brisé Le mur de la façade principale, en brique, présente sur ses côtés deux arcs aveugles avec une alternance de lobes concaves et brisés, dans la tradition almohade. La porte de l'église, amplement modifiée, conserve dans sa partie supérieure des entrecroisements d'arcatures décoratives en brique plus complexes que ceux d'autres exemplaires tolédans. Les charpentes mudéjares, datables des XIVe et XVe siècles, ont diverses formes. La pièce la plus remarquable est le *taujel* de la sacristie extérieure ou sacristie de l'église, décoré d'entrelacs de seize que l'on retrouve dans la frise d'*azulejos*. Des grappes de *mouqarnas* dorés rehaussent sa beauté. La décoration peinte, très dégradée, appartient probablement à la fin du XIVe ou au début du XVe siècle. Á l'origine, l'église était recouverte par une splendide charpente à *par y nudillo* pourvue de tirants, aujourd'hui recouverte par une voûte baroque. Le dit “ancien chœur”, adossé à la nef principale, était aussi, à l'origine, une construction mudéjare avec des stucs du XVe siècle et un plafond en bois dont il ne reste que d'infimes vestiges.

Ce couvent, l'un des plus anciens de Tolède, transformé au long des siècles, conserve tout de même des œuvres mudéjares intéressantes : son abside construite en maçonnerie associée à une assise horizontale de brique, parement typique du mudéjar tolédan ; dans la sacristie se remarque le plafond à entrelacs et grappes de *mouqarnas* dorés.
dates: Fondé au XIIIe siècle, l’ouvrage principal est du XIVe.
history: Ce couvent, habité par une communauté de mères augustines, est l'un des plus anciens de Tolède. Sa consécration à sainte Ursule semble être reliée à l'extraordinaire diffusion de la dévotion à cette sainte qui, avec ses compagnes (11 000 selon la tradition), subit le martyre à Cologne. Cette consécration n'a rien à voir avec saint Augustin, mais elle eut une grande répercussion à Tolède. L'origine de la communauté remonte à 1260, lorsque fut commencée la construction de l'édifice. En 1360, il fut agrandi et Diego González, archidiacre de Calatrava, érigea l'église.

en.name: Fortifications
description:
The Juromenha fortifications, protected by the Ribeira de Mures and the River Guadiana and controlling one of its natural harbours, were built in an area of fertile land and rivers that are full of fish. There are also several remains of ancient mining structures to be found in the surrounding area. The fortifications occupy a dominant position, from where it is possible to see as far as Badajoz in the distance.  
Although the building of the fortifications, which began in the 17th century, was to destroy much of the evidence of earlier occupations on the site, a large part of the mediaeval perimeter wall still remains, and most notably the sections dating from the Islamic period.  
At the north-east end, there still stands a solid masonry tower, in which three stones have been placed dating from the Visigothic period (two of them taken from a frieze, whilst the other originates from the base of an altar). This tower may belong to the period when most of the western territory of the Iberian Peninsula attempted to assert its autonomy in relation to the power of Cordoba, under the leadership of Abd al-Rahman Ibn Marwan al-Jilliqi, in the 3rd/9th century.  
Built against this tower are sections of a drymud wall of the military type. These walls, whose last period of rebuilding must have taken place in the Almohad period, present a set of regular-shaped towers placed immediately next to the abovementioned tower. These towers have very little space between them and no L-shaped entrances, so that they are similar to the fortifications typically built in the period of the *Caliph*s (4th/10th century).  
Islamic geographers from the 4th/10th century in fact, mention Juromenha. Ibn Sahib al-Sala provides abundant detail about its occupation by Geraldo Sem Pavor and his men, during the years from 561/1166 to 564/1169. According to the philosopher Ibn Arabi, writing at the end of the 6th/12th and beginning of the 7th/13th century, it functioned as a *ribat*, or fortified Muslim hermitage, dedicated to the *jihad*.  
Archaeological excavations carried out in the fortifications revealed a set of silos used for the storage of grain, which must first have been used in Islamic times.

es.name: Fortificación
description:
La fortificación de Juromenha, protegida por el Mures y el Guadiana —río del cual controla uno de sus puertos naturales— se asienta sobre una zona de tierras fértiles y aguas ricas en peces, sin que falten en sus alrededores vestigios de antiguas explotaciones mineras. Ocupa una posición dominante desde la que se avista, en la lejanía, Badajoz.  
A pesar de que las profundas obras llevadas a cabo a partir del siglo XVII han destruido muchos vestigios de las ocupaciones de épocas anteriores, conserva aún gran parte del perímetro amurallado medieval, a destacar las murallas de época islámica.  
En el extremo nordeste queda una torre maciza, de albañilería, donde se han colocado tres piedras datadas en época visigótica (dos partes de un friso y un pie de altar), torre que quizá sea contemporánea de la fase en que buena parte del territorio del occidente peninsular afirmó su autonomía frente al poder de Córdoba al mando de Abd al-Rahman Ibn Marwan al-Yilliqi, en el siglo III/IX.  
Pegados a la torre se encuentran lienzos de muralla en *tapial* de tipo militar. Estas murallas, cuya última reforma debe de datar de época almohade, presentan, aparte de la mencionada, algunas torres regulares y poco espaciadas entre sí, sin entradas en ángulo, semejantes a las de las fortificaciones de época califal (siglo IV/X).  
Además, Juromenha es citada ya en el siglo IV/X por geógrafos del mundo islámico. Ibn Sahib al-Sala, por su parte, da abundantes pormenores de su ocupación por Geraldo Sin Miedo y sus hombres durante los años 561/1166 a 564/1169. Según el filósofo Ibn Arabi, a finales del siglo VI/f. XII-p. VII/p. XIII cumplía las funciones de *ribat* o eremitorio fortificado musulmán dedicado a la *yihad*.  
Seguramente data de época islámica el inicio de la utilización del conjunto de silos para almacenar cereales, que las excavaciones arqueológicas han localizado en su interior.

en.name: Monumental Ensemble of Bussaco
short_description:
The Bussaco Park and the monastery were created by the Discalced Carmelites (1620–1834). From 1888 to 1930s a new ensemble is erected, with multiple buildings, either close to the former convent, or replacing the convent’s library, kitchen and dining room.  
By mid-19th century the forest is revitalized associated to emergent rituals of tourism, journeys and leisure. The design of Buçaco Palace was commissioned by King Charles to Luigi Manini, scenographer and architect. Later on, Nicola Bigaglia, José Alexandre Soares and Norte Júnior also cooperated, namely in the Casa dos Embrechados, Casa dos Arcos, Casa dos Cedros and Casa dos Brasões. The final result reflects a fragmentary romanticist attitude, deeply marked by revivalism and multiple references to the Portuguese Discoveries.
type: Civil architecture changing the ancient religious architecture
artist: Luigi Manini (scenographer and architect); architects: Nicola Bigaglia, Manuel Joaquim Norte Júnior, José Alexandre Soares, José Paulo dos Santos; tilework: Jorge Colaço; painters: António Ramalho, Veloso Salgado, Carlos Reis, João Vaz e Ernesto Condeixa; sculptors: António Augusto Gonçalves, Costa Mota, Simões de Almeida Sobrinho, João Machado; stonemasons: Bernardo António Figueiredo, João das Neves Machado, Manuel Francisco, António de Sousa Lemos, Manoel Cardoso, José Barata, José Fonseca, António Joaquim, Alberto Caetano, José Ferreira e Anacleto Garcia
history: 1620 - the Barefoot Carmelite created a “Bos Sacrum” in a walled forest of 105 acres, on the Bussaco Mountain, north of Coimbra, supposed to represent “Mount Carmel” and the “Earthly Paradise”. Following the dissolution of the monasteries in 1834 the forest was abandoned. 1850 - plans followed to turn the ancient convent into a royal residence for Queen Maria Pia, with  luxurious landscape intervention by Roda & Figli (Torino) taking place.  Political circumstances interrupted the project that was later commisioned by her grandson King Charles with the construction of the iconic Neo-Manueline castle, from 1888 to 1907, under project of Luigi Manini, as an homage to the Portuguese Age Discovery and the Battle of Bussaco. 1917 it was transformed into the deluxe Bussaco Palace Hotel.

ar.name: سجادة.
description:
سجادة أوشاكية من القرن 10 / 16، حيكت لحمتها وسداتها من الصوف. والتقنية المستخدمة في الحياكة هي "الحبكة التركية المزدوجة" التي تُعرف باسم حبكة جيردس. السجادة مؤلفة من قطعتين. وعلى الأرضية الحمراء ذات الأنساق متعرجة الخطوط، رسمت أشكال تعرف باسم شينتاماني أو بيلنك (تشكيلات من بقع لونية شبيهة بتلك على جسد الفهد أو خطوط شبيهة بتلك على جسد النمر). ثمة أشكال شينتاماني سوداء وزرقاء داكنة محفوفة باللون الأزرق مرتبة إلى جانب خطوط نمرية صفراء محفوفة باللون الأسود، وفقاً لقاعدة اللاتناهي. وهذه الأشكال ذات جذر بوذي، وتعكس التأثر بفن الشرق الأقصى؛ حيث يمكن رؤيتها على الملابس في الصور الموجودة في كهوف ترفان في تشينكيانغ في الصين، والتي ربما رسمت في القرن 1- 3 / 7- 9.  
  
استخدمت تصاميم شينتاماني أو بيلنك كرموز للقوة والسلطة، وقد دخلت فنون البلاط العثمانية مع احتلال تبريز، إثر الانتصار في معركة تشالديران في عام 920 / 1514 على يد السلطان سليم الأول ( حكم في الفترة 918- 927 / 1512- 1520). ومنذ القرن 10- 12 / 16- 18 أصبحت هذه الأشكال تشاهَد في فنون الزخرفة التي يؤديها فنانون تحت إشراف البلاط، وبصورة خاصة في صناعة المنسوجات والخزف وتجليد الكتب والأشغال الخشبية. وكانت أكثر شيوعاً في ظل السلطان سليم الثاني ( حكم في الفترة 974- 982 / 1566- 1574).  
  
يوجد على محيط السجادة حاشيتان ضيقتان وأخرى عريضة. تتألف الحاشية الأولى الضيقة من أرضية زرقاء داكنة تتوسط مساحة حمراء برتقالية تشتمل على بقع زرقاء وحمراء، وخط أحمر. كما أنها مكسوة بورود الخزامى والقرنفل المتداخلة مع شبكة من السويقات الحمراء. ويزين الحاشية العريضة أزهار اللوتس الكثيفة وبتلات الورد وأشكال مبسَّطة من الزهر والأوراق، بألوان حمراء فاتحة وداكنة ذات حواف بنية. أما الحاشية الأبعد فتغطيها رسوم لأزهار الخزامى والقرنفل الملوَّنة بالأزرق الداكن والأزرق والأصفر الشاحب، موزعة بين سويقات متشابكة على خلفية حمراء.

هذا البساط مُحاك في أوشاق، لمسجد السلطان سليم في قونية. ورسوم التشنتاماني (بقع فرو الفهد)، رموز القوة والسلطة، ذات الجذور المُمتدَّة إلى الشرق الأقصى، والأمهار، والزنابق، والقرنفلات، كانت مُستخدمة لتزيين ألواح الآجرّ، والأقمشة الأدوات الخشبية، بين القرنين العاشر والثاني عشر الهجريين/ السادس عشر والثامن عشر الميلاديين.

en.name: Rug.
description:
An Ushak carpet of the AH 10th / AD 16th century; the warp and the weft of which are of wool. The weaving technique used is the 'Turkish double knot', known as the Gördes knot. The rug is in two pieces.  
  
On a red ground, arranged on a zigzag axes, are motifs known as *chintamani* or *pelenk* (leopard-spots or tiger-stripes motif). Black and dark-blue *chintamani* motifs with blue contours are arranged together with yellow tiger stripes with black contours, according to the principle of infinity. These motifs have Buddhist roots and show Far Eastern influence; they appear on the clothing of figures in the caves at Turfan in the Xinjiang province of China, probably painted in the AH 1st–3rd- / AD 7th–9th -century.  
  
The *chintamani* or *pelenk* motifs were used as symbols of power and authority, entering Ottoman palace art with the capture of Tabriz, following the victory won at Chaldiran in AH 920 / AD 1514 by Sultan Selim I (r. AH 918–27 / AD 1512–20). From the AH 10th–12th / AD 16th–18th century the motifs are seen in all the decorative arts made by artists directed by the Ottoman court, seen especially in textiles, ceramics, book-bindings and woodwork; they were most popular under Sultan Selim II (r. AH 974–82 / AD 1566–74).  
  
The perimeter of this carpet has two narrow borders and one broad border. The first narrow border consists of a dark-blue ground between an orange-red strip, with blue and red dots and a red line. It is filled with tulip and carnation motifs between interweaving red stems. The main border is decorated with enormous lotuses, rose-petals, and stylised flower and leaf motifs in light- and dark-red with brown contours. The outermost border is filled with dark-blue, blue, and cream-coloured tulip and carnation motifs amid interweaving stems on a red background.

This rug was woven at Uşak for the Sultan Selim Mosque in Konya. *Chintamani* motifs (leopard spots), symbols of power and the sultanate of Far East origin, and *hatayi* (peonies), tulips and carnations were also used in tiles, textiles and woodwork between the AH 10th and 12th / AD 16th and 18th centuries.
holder: Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts.

es.name: Alfombra.
description:
Alfombra de Uşak del siglo X / XVI con trama y urdimbre de lana. La técnica de tejedura utilizada es la del doble nudo turco, conocido como «nudo de Gördes». La alfombra se conserva en dos piezas.  
Sobre un fondo rojo hay motivos conocidos como *chintamani* o *pelenk* (de manchas de leopardo o rayas de tigre), dispuestos en un eje en zigzag. Los motivos *chintamani* negros y azul oscuro perfilados en azul se combinan con las rayas de tigre amarillas perfiladas en negro, siguiendo el principio de infinitud. Estos motivos tienen raíces budistas y demuestran la influencia del Lejano Oriente, ya que también están presentes en los trajes de las figuras de las cuevas de Turfán (provincia china de Xianjiang), que probablemente fueron pintadas en los siglos I-III / VII-IX.  
Los motivos *chintamani* o *pelenk* se utilizaban como símbolos del poder y de la autoridad. Llegaron al arte palaciego otomano con la conquista de Tabriz, subsiguiente a la victoria del sultán Selim I (r. 918-927 / 1512-1520) en Chaldiran en 920 / 1514. Desde los siglos X-XII / XVI-XVIII, estos motivos aparecen en las obras de los artesanos dirigidos por la corte otomana, en todas las artes decorativas, especialmente en los tejidos, la cerámica, la encuadernación de los libros y la ebanistería. Alcanzaron su apogeo durante el reinado del sultán Selim II (r. 974-982 / 1566-1574).  
El contorno de la alfombra tiene dos bordes estrechos y uno ancho. El primer borde estrecho consta de un fondo azul oscuro en medio de una banda naranja rojiza, con puntos azules y rojos y una línea roja. Está decorada con tulipanes y claveles situados en medio de tallos rojos entrelazados. El borde principal está decorado con enormes lotos, pétalos de rosa y motivos vegetales y florales estilizados, de colores rojo claro y oscuro contorneados en marrón. El borde exterior presenta tulipanes y claveles de colores azul, azul oscuro y crema, situados en medio de tallos entrelazados sobre un fondo rojo.

Alfombra tejida en Uşak para la mezquita del Sultán Selim (Konya). En los siglos X-XII / XVI-XIII también se usaron en azulejos, tejidos y obras de madera motivos *chintamani* (de leopardo) –símbolos de poder y del sultanato de origen oriental–, así como *hatavi* (peonías), tulipanes y claveles.
holder: Museo de Arte Turco e Islámico.
dates: Siglo X de la Hégira / XVI d. C.
keywords: Alfombra; chintamani; cintamani; Konya; leopardo; motivos pelenk; Selim II; Gördes.

fr.name: Tapis.
description:
Tapis d'Ouchak du Xe siècle H (XVIe siècle J.-C.) à trame et chaîne en laine. La technique est celle du double nœud turc également appelé nœud de Ghiordes. Il est séparé en deux morceaux.  
Des motifs *chintamani* ou *pelenk* (taches de léopard ou rayures de tigre) se répartissent en zigzag sur fond rouge. Sur toute la surface, ces motifs noir et bleu foncé à contours bleus alternent avec des rayures de tigre jaunes à contours noirs, selon le principe de l'infinité. Ensemble, ces motifs observés pour la première fois sur les vêtements de figures peintes dans les grottes de Turfan (province chinoise du Xinjiang), probablement vers le Ier-IIIe siècle H (VIIe-IXe siècle J.-C.), illustrent l'influence de l'Extrême-Orient et de certaines racines bouddhistes.  
Les motifs de *chintamani* ou *pelenk,* symboles de puissance et d'autorité, apparaissent dans l'art palatial ottoman après la prise de Tabriz par la victoire de Chaldiran remportée en 920 H / 1514 J.-C. par le sultan Sélim Ier (r. 918-927 H / 1512-1520 J.-C.). Dès le Xe siècle H (XVIe siècle J.-C.), ils sont présents dans l'ensemble de la production artistique réalisée pour la cour ottomane, en particulier dans le travail du bois et dans les textiles, céramiques et reliures. Ils furent particulièrement populaires sous le sultan Sélim II (r. 974-982 H / 1566-1574 J.-C.).  
Le tapis est entouré de trois bordures, deux étroites et une large. La première, étroite, se compose, sur un fond bleu foncé pris entre une bande rouge orangé à points bleus et rouges et filet rouge, de motifs de tulipes et d'œillets entre des tiges végétales rouges entrelacées. La bordure principale est décorée d'énormes fleurs de lotus, pétales de rose et motifs de fleurs et de feuillages stylisés en rouge sombre et clair à contours bruns. La bordure extérieure fait appel à des motifs de tulipes et d'œillets bleu foncé, bleu et crème répartis parmi des entrelacs de tiges végétales sur un fond rouge.

Ce tapis fut tissé à Ouchak pour la mosquée du sultan Sélim à Konya. Les motifs *chintamani* (rayures de tigre), symboles du pouvoir et du sultanat d’origine extrême-orientale, les pivoines (*hatayi*), tulipes et œillets étaient également utilisés pour les carreaux de céramiques, les textiles et le bois ouvragé entre le Xe et le XIIe siècle H (XVIe-XVIII s. J.-C.).
holder: Musée des arts turcs et islamiques.
dates: Xe siècle de l’Hégire (XVIe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: Tapis; chintamani; cintamani; Konya; léopard; motif pelenk; Sélim II; Gördes.
materials: Laine sur trame de laine, tissée en double nœud turc également appelé nœud de Gördes.
tags: Laine sur trame de laine, tissée en double nœud turc également appelé nœud de Gördes.
partner: Musée des arts turques et islamiques

tr.name: Halı.
description:
10\. / 16. yy. Uşak halısıdır. Atkı ve çözgü iplikleri yündür. Gördes düğümü ile dokunmuştur. İki ayrı parça halindedir.  
  
Kırmızı zemin üzerine şaşırtmalı eksende yerleştirilmiş, çintamani ve pelenk (kaplan çizgisi veya leopar beneği) denilen motifler yer alır. Mavi renk konturlu siyah ve koyu mavi çintamani motifleri ile siyah konturlu sarı renkli kaplan çizgileri sonsuzluk prensibiyle verilmişlerdir. Budist kökenli, Uzak Doğu etkili bu motifler çin'de Sincan (Xinjiang)'daki Turfan Bezeklik Mağarası'nda 1.-3. / 7.-9. yy duvar resimlerindeki giysi motiflerinde görülür. Gücün ve saltanatın simgesi olarak kullanılan bu motifler, Sultan Yavuz Selim'in (918-927 / 1512-1520) 920 / 1514 yılında çaldıran zaferi ile Tebriz'i ele geçirmesiyle Osmanlı Saray sanatına girmiştir. 16. yy'dan 18. yy'a kadar Osmanlı Sarayının yönlendirdiği sanatçılar tarafından bütün dekoratif sanatlarda özellikle kumaş, çini, kitap ciltleri ve ahşap üzerinde görülen bu desenlerin uygulaması Sultan II. Selim (974-982 / 1566-1574) yıllarında en yüksek değere ulaşmıştır.  
  
Halının çevresini iki dar, bir geniş bordür dolanır. Birinci dar bordür lacivert zeminli olup mavi ve kırmızı noktalı sedef bordür ile kırmızı çizgi arasındadır. Kırmızı renkli sarmaşık dalları arasında lale ve karanfil motifleri ile dolguludur. Ana bordür, kahverengi konturlu açık ve koyu kırmızı renkli iri hatayiler, gül yaprakları, stilize çiçek ve yaprak motifleri ile bezelidir. En dış dar bordür ise kırmızı zemin üzerine sarmaşık dallar arasında lacivert, mavi, krem renkli lale ve karanfil motifleri ile doldurulmuştur.

Sultan II. Selim tarafından inşa ettirilen Konya Selimiye Camii için Uşak'ta dokunmuştur. Bu dönemde en yüksek değerine ulaşan Uzak Doğu etkili, gücün ve saltanatın simgesi çintamani ve leopar beneği ile hatayi, lale, karanfil motifleri 10.-12. / 16.-18. yüzyıllarda çini, kumaş ve ahşapta da kullanılmıştır.
keywords: halı; II. Selim; çintamani; pelenk; Konya; Gördes

en.name: Ballroom
description: The perspective illusionism of the ceiling emphasizes the false columns, embraced by leaves painted on the walls. The chequered floor, dating to the seventeenth-century, is an homage to the Pepoli coat of arms.
artist: Domenico Maria Canuti and Domenico Santi known as Mengazzino
partner: Musei Civici d’Arte Antica di Bologna in cooperation with the Province of Bologna

it.name: Sala da ballo, particolare del soffitto
description: Particolare della sala da ballo con la sua stupefacente quadratura barocca che incornicia scene della vita di Ercole. Lo stemma Pepoli sormontato da un cigno è ripetuto in continuazione. L'illusionismo prospettico del soffitto prolunga le false colonne, avvolte da foglie e dipinte sulle pareti. Il pavimento a scacchi, databile al XVII secolo, è  un omaggio allo stemma  Pepoli .
artist: Domenico Maria Canuti e Domenico Santi detto Mengazzino

ar.name: الطيفور (صحن مقعّر).
description: طيفور ذو فوهة دائرية وحواف مستديرة مشطوبة. جسمه نصف بيضوي، والقسم السفلي منه أو البدن يبدو ناعماً وله شكل نصف كرة. قاعدته محدّبة، وساقه حلقية منحرفة. تبدو القطعة من الخارج مغطاة بطلاء مزجج أحادي اللون عسلي ومخضرّ، في حين يحتوي الداخل على زخارف بتقنية الحبل اليابس الكاملة *cuerda seca*، التي تكون فيها ألوان الأبيض والأخضر والعسلي مفصولة عن بعضها البعض بخطوط من المنغنيز. يتألف الموضوع الزخرفي المركزي المنقوش داخل دائرة من أيل أو من ظبي يقف بلا حراك، ورأسه منتصب في وضعية الانتباه وكأنه يتأهب للهرب. توحي الأشكال النباتية غير المحددة التي تملأ الأماكن الفارغة بالمنظر المحيط بالحيوان. ويُستكمل التكوين على حواف الصحن بإفريز من مروحة متصبعة. قطعة مرمّمة.

طبقٌ مزخرف بالحبل اليابس الكامل. الشكل المركزي للقطعة منقوش داخل دائرة، وهو عبارة عن أيل أو ظبي يقف بلا حراك، ورأسه منتصب في وضعية التأهب للفرار. جرى ملأ الفضاء الفارغ بأشكال نباتية، تمثل المنظر المحيط بالحيوان.
dynasty: الفترة المرابطية أو الفترة الموحدية، القرن 6 الهجري / القرن 12 الميلادي
keywords: تجارة؛ خزف؛ تقنية الحبل اليابس الكاملة cuerda seca .
materials: فخار مصقول مصنوع من عجينة لها مسام، لونها وردي وأصفر مثل قش القمح، تم تشكيلُها بدولاب سريع، وشيُّها في محيط مؤكسد، وزخرفتُها بتقنية الحبل اليابس cuerda seca.

en.name: Glazed bowl.
description: Glazed bowl with bevelled rounded rim, circular mouth, semi-oval body with gentle carination towards the bottom and convex base with a diagonal foot-ring. The exterior of the piece is glazed in honey-coloured monochrome, while the interior is decorated entirely using the *cuerda seca* technique in which the white, green and honey colours of the glaze are separated by lines of manganese. The central ornamental theme, enclosed in a circle, consists of a deer or antelope in a static pose, with its head raised in an alert posture, ready to flee. Indeterminate plant motifs fill the empty spaces, and seem to suggest the landscape around the animal. Around this, on the wall of the bowl, the composition is completed with a frieze of palmettes made by finger impressions. The object has been restored.

Bowl made entirely using *cuerda seca*. The central motif of the piece, enclosed by a circle, is a deer or antelope in a static pose with its head raised, alert and preparing to flee. The empty space is filled with plant motifs, which represent the landscape around the animal.
keywords: cuerda seca; ceramic; trade
materials: Glazed ceramic made with porous pink straw and paste mix, modelled on a wheel, fired in an oxidising atmosphere and decorated with the *cuerda seca* technique throughout.

es.name: Ataifor.
description: Ataifor de borde redondeado biselado, boca circular, cuerpo semiovalado con suave carena baja y base convexa con pie anular diagonal. El exterior de la pieza está revestido de vidriado monocromo melado verdoso, mientras que el interior presenta decoración ejecutada con la técnica de la cuerda seca total en la que los colores blanco, verde y melado del vidriado se encuentran separados por trazos de manganeso. El tema ornamental central, encerrado en un círculo, consiste en un corzo o antílope en pose estática, con la cabeza erguida en actitud de alerta, preparado para la huida. Encontramos motivos vegetales indeterminados rellenando los espacios vacíos, y parecen sugerir el paisaje que rodea al animal. Alrededor, en la pared del ataifor, la composición se completa con un friso de palmetas digitadas. Pieza restaurada.

Ataifor en cuerda seca total. El tema decorativo central, encerrado en un círculo, es un corzo o antílope en posición estática, con la cabeza erguida en actitud de alerta, preparado para la huida. Los motivos vegetales que rellenan los espacios vacíos parecen sugerir el paisaje que rodea al animal.
dates: Siglo VI H. /  XII d. C.

fr.name: Ataifor (plat creux).
description: *Ataifor* à bouche circulaire, bord arrondi et biseauté, corps mi-ovale avec une douce carène basse, hémisphérique, base convexe et pied annulaire diagonal. L'extérieur de la pièce est couvert d'une glaçure monochrome couleur miel et verdâtre, tandis que l'intérieur est décoré à la *cuerda seca* totale où les couleurs, blanc, vert et miel de la glaçure se trouvent séparées par les traits au manganèse. Le thème décoratif central, inscrit dans un cercle, consiste en un chevreuil ou une antilope dans une pose statique, la tête dressée dans une attitude d'alerte, prête à la fuite. Les motifs végétaux indéterminés qui remplissent les espaces vides semblent suggérer l'environnement de l'animal. Sur le rebord du plat, la composition est complétée par une frise de palettes digitées. Pièce restaurée.

Plat décoré à la *cuerda seca* totale. Le motif central de la pièce, inscrit dans un cercle, est un chevreuil ou une antilope dans une pose statique, tête dressée, en alerte et prêt à fuir. L'espace vide est rempli par des motifs végétaux, qui représentent le paysage autour de l'animal.

pt.name: Tigela.
description: Tigela de bordo arredondado biselado, boca circular, corpo semi-ovalado com suave carena baixa e base convexa com pé anular diagonal. O exterior da peça está revestido com vidrado monocromo melado esverdeado, ao passo que o interior apresenta decoração executada com a técnica da cuerda seca total, na qual as cores branca, verde e melada do vidrado se encontram separadas por traços de manganés. O tema ornamental central, encerrado num círculo, consiste num corço ou antílope em pose estática, com a cabeça erguida em atitude de alerta, preparada para a fuga. Encontramos motivos vegetais indeterminados preenchendo os espaços vazios, e parecem sugerir a paisagem que rodeia o animal. Em redor, na parede da tigela, a composição completa-se com um friso de palmetas digitadas. Peça restaurada.

en.name: Triple-arched house
description: The layout of this house is composed of various rooms, symmetrically arranged around three sides of a large, north-facing central room called a *dar*. Three large arched windows, in a neo-gothic style, open onto a narrow balcony. The three sides of rooms do not communicate with each other, and thus the *dar* is both a communal living space and the physical centre of the home.
history: This kind of house started appearing around Beirut in the 1860s. It is often read as being representative of "Ottoman modernity" during the Tanzimat period, and its design and construction was outlined in/limited by the law. Indeed, this new architectural style was based on a new conception of the domestic space: domestic activities have been absorbed into the living space, and outdoor spaces are less prevalent. Balconies, backyards, courtyards and gardens, for example, no longer play an important role in the design of these homes.
keywords: Typology; Tile; Architecture; Tradition; House

de.name: Katholische Dekanats- und Pfarrkirche Mariae Himmelfahrt
description: Die Disposition des Grundrisses folgt dem einfachen Schema gotischer Pfarrkirchen mit rechteckigem Langhaussaal, eingezogenem Chor mit polygonalem 3/8-Schluß und Chorwinkelturm. Das übergreifende spätgotische Gewölbe wurde zu einer Tonne mit Stichkappen umgeformt, geschwungene Wandpfeiler mit Pilastern unterteilen das Langhaus in drei Joche, der Chor weist einfache Pilastergliederung auf. Große geschwungene Fenster sorgen für reichen Lichteinfall, der die stilreine, sehr einheitliche Ausstattung mit Altären, Kanzel, Beichtstühlen etc. in reicher Goldfassung und die Deckenmalereien zur Wirkung bringt.

Die in reizvoller landschaftlicher Lage errichtete Pfarrkirche von Sillian, ein stattlicher Bau der späten Gotik, birgt in ihrem Inneren einen Raum reinsten spätbarocken Stils. Die Umgestaltung wurde unter Leitung des k. k. Hofkammermalers in Tirol, Josef Adam Mölck, durchgeführt. Obgleich die alte Bausubstanz dabei weitgehend erhalten blieb, ist der gotische Baustil nur mehr am Außenbau erkennbar – das Innere wird von der schwungvollen und kräftigen Formensprache des 18. Jahrhunderts geprägt, die sich einheitlich in Architektur und Ausstattung manifestiert.
history: Die Urpfarre von Sillian wird zuerst im Jahr 1212 urkundlich erwähnt, eine Chorweihe ist für 1326 dokumentiert. Der bis heute im Kern erhaltene  spätgotische Neubau wurde 1441 geweiht. Der barocke Umbau erfolgte 1759-64 unter der Regie von Josef Adam Mölck, die Planung und Ausführung übernahm Rudolf Schraffl aus Toblach. Eine geplante Regotisierung im 19. Jahrhundert unterblieb. Im Zuge der Generalsanierung von 1988-96 wurde auch ein neuer Volksaltar mit Ambo aufgestellt.
keywords: Barocksierung; Spätbarock

en.name: Catholic Decanal and Parish Church of the Assumption
description: The ground plan follows the simple scheme of Gothic parish churches with a rectangular nave hall, retracted choir with polygonal 3/8 termination and tower above a corner of the choir. The overarching Late Gothic vault has been remodelled to form a barrel vault with vaulting cells; curved wall piers with pilasters divide the nave into three bays and the choir is characterised by a simple pilaster arrangement. Large curved windows provide ample illumination which shows to best advantage the stylistically pure, highly uniform interior work with richly gilded altars, pulpit, confessional boxes etc. and the ceiling paintings.

The parish church, situated in a delightful rural setting, is an imposing Late Gothic building housing an interior executed in the purest Late Baroque style. Although the old building fabric was largely retained, the Gothic architecture is now only visible on the exterior – the interior, in respect of both architecture and fittings, is uniformly executed in the formal language of the 18th century.
artist: Architecture/concept for Baroque redesign: Johann Adam Ritter von [of] Mölck (1718–1794); planning and execution: Rudolf Schraffl (1713–1768); altarpiece superstructure (carpenter): Johann Jaufer [n.d.]; sculpture: Johann Paterer (1712–1785); ceiling frescoes: Joseph Adam Ritter von [of] Mölck
history: The ancient parish of Sillian is first mentioned in records in 1212, the consecration of a choir is documented for the year 1326. The Late Gothic building, the core of which has been retained to this day, was consecrated in 1441. The Baroque modification was carried out between 1759 and 1764 under the direction of Josef Adam Ritter von Mölck. The planning and execution was conducted by Rudolf Schraffl of Tolbach.
keywords: Baroque redesign; Late Baroque

en.name: *Self Portrait*
description:
The portrait painter, Ádám Mányoki, was one of the most prominent figures of Baroque art in Hungary. His career began in Hanover and Hamburg and then, in the first decade of the 18th century, he worked for Frederick William at the Berlin court. From 1707 to 1712, he was court portraitist to Prince Ferenc Rákóczi II in Hungary, where he worked for a number of years before carrying out other assignments for the prince in the Netherlands and Berlin.  
He painted the *Self Portrait* rendered with a captivating candour and self-assurance in Berlin. He used a trick of the self-portraitist that had been popular since Rembrandt: the soft velvet hat with its upturned rim casting a warm, brown shadow over the upper half of his face. The painting reveals a synthesis of the influence of Antoine Pesne, a French portraitist of the Prussian court, and of Mányoki's studies in northern Germany. The choice of colours and some formal details are clearly traceable to Pesne's work, while some characteristic features of the composition are rooted in 17th-century Dutch and German painting, including Johann Heinrich Roos' self-portrait. Mányoki may have known Roos' self-portrait from an engraving by Philip Kilian and taken inspiration from it in the figure's posture and the shirt loosely opening in front.  
From 1713, Mányoki was employed by August II the Strong, King of Poland and Elector of Saxony; from 1717 he was portrait painter to the court. Thereafter he received an increasing number of commissions in Leipzig to portray the professors of the university, the well-to-do burghers and merchants and their families. In the mid-1720s, Mányoki, intent on repatriation, returned to Hungary for a short time. However, a lack of patronage and inability to make a living meant he left for Dresden again, this time for good. He adjusted his later work in the main to the expectations of 18th-century German middle-class art collectors.

The son of a Protestant clergyman in Szokolya, Mányoki studied art in Germany. Called back to Hungary by Prince Ferenc Rákóczi II in 1707, he remained there until 1712. Following the collapse of the struggle against the Habsburgs for independence led by the prince, he worked for the Polish-Saxon court in Dresden from 1713.  
Painted in Berlin, the *Self Portrait –* rendered with captivating candour and self-assurance –represents an excellent “French-style” example of the artist's portrait painting.
keywords: Self-portrait; King Frederick William; patronage; burghers; Protestants

en.name: Church of La Calahorra
description: The Church of La Calahorra stands out above the houses of the village. Built in 1550, to the plans and conditions of Francisco de Antero who presented them in 1546, the tower, built in brick, is one of the best examples to be found in the area. Once inside, the church has a single nave, with a choir loft at the foot. The ceiling is one of the most successful of the Mudéjar type: double *limas* with single cross braces and five paired anchor ties, decorated with strapwork, on corbels. There are two brick portals, one at the foot of the church and another at the side, giving onto a square. The sanctuary, separated from the rest of the building by one of its main arches, was modified in the 18th century.

es.name: Iglesia de La Calahorra
description: Entre el caserío sobresale la iglesia, construida en 1550 sobre trazas y condiciones de Francisco de Antero, dadas en 1546. La torre, realizada en ladrillo, es uno de los mejores ejemplos que podemos encontrar en la comarca. Una vez ante ella, veremos que la iglesia es de una sola nave, con un coro a los pies. Su cubierta es una de las soluciones más sabias de la *armadura* mudéjar: *limas* dobles con cuadrales simples y cinco tirantes pareados y apeinazados sobre canes. Al interior se accede mediante dos portadas de ladrillo, una a los pies de la iglesia y otra en el lateral que da a la plaza. La capilla mayor, separada del resto del edificio por un arco toral, fue modificada profundamente en el siglo XVIII.

ar.name: صفحة من مصحف أزرق
description: هذه الصفحة أتت من مصحف أزرق والذي سمي بذلك من أجل المستوى اللوني الغني للسطح المصبوغ بالنيلة . وصبغ البرشمان لاستخدامه في المخطوطات الفاخرة أصلها من العالم البيزنطي واستمرت حتى بداية العصر الإسلامي. وحبر الذهب والفضة للنص الكوفي وعلامات الآيات الدائرية تضاف لغنى هذه الصفحة . بينما يعتقد العديد من الباحثين أن هذا المصحف أصله من القيروان في تونس فإن التفاصيل في علامات الآيات فيه تقول بأنه ربما قد كتب فعلا في قرطبة الأموية .على أن وصف المخطوطة بنفس المواصفات في هذه الصفحة التي تظهر في قائمة محتويات القيروان في 693 هجري / 1293 ميلادي تشير إلى أنها كانت جزءا من مقتنيات المسجد في ذلك الوقت.

en.name: Folio from the 'Blue Qur'an'
description: This folio comes from the Blue Qur'an, so named for the rich hue of its indigo-dyed surface. The dyeing of parchment for use in luxurious manuscripts originated in Byzantine tradition and continued into the early Islamic period. The gold and silver ink of the *kufic* text and circular verse markers add to the opulence of this folio. While many scholars believe this Qur’an to have originated in Qayrawan, Tunisia, details in its verse markers have led others to argue that it may have actually been produced in Umayyad Córdoba. Nevertheless, a description of a manuscript with the same specifications as this one appeared in an inventory of the Mosque of Qayrawan in AH 693 / AD 1293, indicating that it was part of the mosque’s endowment by this time.
dates: Hegira 3rd–4th century / AD second half 9th–mid-10th century
keywords: Zirid; Qairawan; Tunisia; ink; opaque watercolor; gold; parchment; Qur'an; Arabic inscription; calligraphy; religious object; writing; kufic; calligrapher; dedicatory inscription; female patronage; Prophet Muhammad

en.name: Clay loom weight
description: Loom weights are made from a roll of clay twisted and shaped into spheres, flattened cylinders, or conical shapes. They are used to keep the warp threads of the loom taut and provide even tension in order to weave with ease.

en.name: Moorish Castle
description: Crowning the Sintra hills and covering an area of four hectares there can still be seen a long stretch of crenellated wall with rectangular turrets. Little now remains of this fortified settlement, which was still inhabited in the 5th/11th century and was certainly also used by shepherds and their flocks as a temporary shelter. The Prince Regent D. Fernando II, the same man who had rebuilt the nearby Pena Palace in the mid-19th century, was also the creator of the Romantic scenography that now surrounds these beautiful ruins. The battlements, steps and parapets were adapted to form a path that affords visitors the chance to enjoy extraordinarily beautiful views over the surrounding landscape.

es.name: Castelo dos Mouros
description: Coronando la sierra de Sintra y delimitando un área de 4 ha, se puede ver hoy una larga cortina de murallas almenadas con sus torreones cuadrangulares. Queda poco de esta población fortificada, todavía habitada en el siglo V/XI y que ciertamente servía también de refugio temporal a los pastores y sus rebaños. El príncipe regente D. Fernando II, el mismo que a mediados del siglo XIX reconstruyó en las inmediaciones el Palacio da Pena, fue también el autor de la escenografía romántica que hoy envuelve estas bellas ruinas. Los adarves, escalinatas y parapetos fueron adaptados a un recorrido que permite disfrutar de paisajes de rara belleza.

en.name: Wardrobe of Luigi Elli of Milan [Paris Exhibition, 1878]
names: Armadio letto di Luigi Elli di Milano
short_description: One curiosity, presented at the Universal Exhibition of Paris in 1878, is a modern "bed wardrobe" designed by the Milanese industrialist Luigi Elli. Appreciated more in France than in Italy, and initially excluded from Italian orders, it was reintroduced when the France decided to display it within other French works.

en.name: Caucasian carpet
description:
In the Caucasus there is great variety of motifs due to artistic exchange among the ethnic groups. Different classifications of carpets are based on weaver's ethnicity, geographic origin of the carpet or the carpet structure. No system of classification is based on design or motifs. Therefore, for this peculiar carpet, it is difficult to establish its origin.  
The central field is decorated with polychrome floret and octagons with star motifs on red ground. Three borders frame the central field. The main border is floral. Minor borders are decorated with chain of S shapes on a blue background.
keywords: Caucasus; small filler elements

en.name: Karabagh Medallion and Sickle Leaf Rug
description:
It has a well-proportioned pattern of two full medallions on a dark blue field and a partial medallion at the upper and lower ends. The medallions have hooking, lancet-leaf ivory arms and are linked by fringed ivory palmettes. The remaining area of the field is filled with rosettes, flowers and leaves.  
  
Ellis includes it among the rare blue field carpets he proposes as analogues of a late 17th or early 18th century Shirvan or Karabagh rug with multiple medallions held by the Art Institute, Chicago, describing it as, "a rather small and narrow example on a blue ground". The rug was determined to be 17th century Armenian by Károly Gombos in 1983. Jennifer Wearden published it in connection with Azerbaijan embroideries as an "early 18th century Caucasian or Armenian Floral Carpet".

en.name: Karaköy (Sinan Bey) Madrasa
description:
It is known that a great number of *madrasa*s were constructed in Manisa during the Saruhan and Ottoman periods. Only four of these *madrasa*s (Great Mosque \[14th c.\], Sinan Bey \[15th c.\], Hafsa Sultan \[16th c.\], and Muradiye \[16th c.\] Madrasas) have survived up to the present day. Of these buildings, the only example dating to the early Ottoman period is Sinan Bey Madrasa. This building, also known as the Karaköy Madrasa, does not have an inscription. According to its *waqf* charter dated 1549, the *madrasa* together with a *mektep* –which has not survived– were commissioned by a person named Sinan Bey, who according to some researchers, was one of the treasurers during Sultan Mehmed II’s reign (1451-1481). According to some other scholars, though, he was one of the same Sultan’s *müderris*. Although the *waqf* charter dates to 1549, the *madrasa*’s architectural characteristics indicate that it was constructed in the middle of the 15th century, which is the accepted view.  
Constructed out of stone and brick, the building is entered through the monumental entrance in the middle of the north facade. The courtyard is surrounded with porticoes on all four sides. On the east and west wings of the courtyard, there is a total of 10 student cells, in all of which there is one fireplace and various numbers of niches. The cells and porticoes are covered with cross-vaults, which is striking because this type of vault, uncommon in Turkish architecture, was quite fashionable and used in 14th- and 15th-century buildings in West Anatolian cities like Manisa, Tire and Menemen. To the south of the courtyard is the *dershane* reached via a set of stairs. In most of the Anatolian *madrasa*s, the *dershane* area was also used as a *masjid*. Here, the *dershane*, together with the portico in front of it, were raised above the rest of the structure, providing the area with an independent masjid quality. The *dershane*/*masjid* is covered with a dome supported by squinches filled with *muqarnas*. The Sinan Bey Madrasa was thoroughly renovated in 1985 and is used today as a Handcrafts Centre in which silverworking ateliers are found.

es.name: Madrasa de Karaköy (o de Sinan Bey) (opción)
description:
Se sabe que en los periodos saruhaní y otomano se construyeron en Manisa numerosas *madrasa*s, pero solo cuatro (la de la mezquita Mayor, del siglo XIV; la de Sinan Bey, del XV; la de Hafsa Sultan, del XVI; y la de Muradiye, también del XVI) han perdurado hasta hoy y, de ellas, la única correspondiente a la primera época otomana es la *madrasa* de Sinan Bey, también conocida como *madrasa* de Karaköy. No existe ninguna inscripción que nos informe de la fecha de construcción, pero, según el acta fundacional del *waqf*, de 1549, se levantó por orden de Sinan Bey, junto con el *mektep* ahora desaparecido. En opinión de algunos investigadores, Sinan Bey era uno de los tesoreros del sultán Mehmet II (1451-1481); según otros, era uno de los *müderris* del sultán. Pese a que en el acta de constitución de la fundación figure el año 1549, las características arquitectónicas de la *madrasa* hacen pensar que se levantó a mediados del siglo XV, y es el punto de vista más aceptado.  
Al edificio, construido en piedra y ladrillo, se entra por una puerta monumental de la fachada norte. El patio está circundado de pórticos en los cuatro lados; en las alas este y oeste se encuentran 10 celdas de estudiantes, todas con hogar y varias hornacinas. Los cuartos y los pórticos están techados con bóvedas de crucería, bastante raras en la arquitectura turca, pero muy en boga en los siglos XIV-XV en ciudades de Anatolia occidental como Manisa, Tire y Menemen. El *dershane* está situado en el lado sur del patio, al final de una escalera. En la mayoría de las *madrasa*s de Anatolia, el *dershane* servía también de *masyid*. Aquí, el *dershane* y el pórtico antepuesto están más altos que el resto del edificio, lo que les da el aspecto independiente de los *masyid*s. La estancia está cubierta por una cúpula sostenida por pechinas llenas de *muqarnas*. La *madrasa* de Sinan Bey fue completamente reformada en 1985 y hoy se usa como centro de artesanía con talleres de trabajo en plata.

en.name: Matbakh al-‘Ajami
description: The so-called Matbakh al-’Ajami was originally an Ayyubid palace that likely belonged to the ‘Ajami family. About a third of this palace was demolished when the street to the south of it was widened, and the palace was given a false façade in the Mamluk style. An inconsequential entrance leads to the north-east corner of a spacious courtyard surrounded by four *iwans* and covered by a dome on *muqarnas* pendentives, possibly the largest preserved Ayyubid dome in Syria. All four *iwans* are flanked by narrow, arched openings, forming a tripartite-façade composition typical of Ayyubid palaces. The northern *iwan*, framed by an elaborate arch with pendant voussoirs, has an exquisite *muqarnas* vault that resembles a starry sky.

de.name: Schlacht an der Milvischen Brücke
description: Das die ganze Fläche des Chorgewölbes einnehmende Deckengemälde zeigt den im Zeichen des Kreuzes geführten Kampf Kaiser Konstantins des Großen gegen seinen Thronkonkurrenten Maxentius an der nördlich von Rom gelegenen Tiberbrücke. Einem berühmten Vorbild ist die dramatische, einen Brückenbogen umwogende Komposition verpflichtet, indem sie die Amazonenschlacht des Pieter Paul Rubens paraphrasiert.

en.name: Battle of the Milvian Bridge
description: The ceiling painting, which covers the entire surface of the chancel vault, shows the battle of Emperor Constantine the Great, led by a vision of the Christian Cross, against Maxentius, his rival to the throne, at the Tiber Bridge north of Rome. The dramatic figural composition, surging around a bridge arch, is based on a famous model by paraphrasing the Battle of the Amazons by Pieter Paul Rubens.
partner: University of Munich, Institute of Art History

en.name: Ballroom
description: This great hall is considered one of the most peculiar interiors in Italian Baroque architecture. It is a triple volume hall with several balustrades, culminating with the lantern on the top (33 m. height and about 800 square feet surface). There is no painted decoration, only white stucco mouldings that emphasise the extreme lightness of the architecture.
partner: Musei Civici d’Arte Antica di Bologna in cooperation with the Province of Bologna

it.name: Sala da ballo
description: Il grande salone è considerato uno degli interni più straordinari del'architettura barocca italiana. E' uno spazio dal volume triplo  con diversi affacci, che culmina nella lanterna al vertice (33 m di altezza e circa 800 metri quadri di superficie). La decorazione dipinta è assente, i candidi stucchi  enfatizzano l'estrema leggerezza dell'architettura.

en.name: Variation of the Basmala
description: This scroll painting is made of patterned dark blue-gold silk with mounted calligraphy on paper. The paper has been treated with a light wash of semitransparent black ink drippings. The Arabic calligraphy in opaque black ink forms an abstract vegetal design. The title of the work appears in black ink on the left, above two red seals. A third red seal appears on the top right.
